items.title: Putin’s decree allowing the state to take over companies that fail to protect against drones ‘is not about nationalization,’ First Deputy PM Manturov says
items.summary: A decree signed by Vladimir Putin that allows temporary state management of critical infrastructure facilities whose owners failed to protect them from drones does not amount to nationalization or a change in ownership, First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov told reporters.
items.body_text:
Putin’s decree allowing the state to take over companies that fail to protect against drones ‘is not about nationalization,’ First Deputy PM Manturov says
A decree signed by Vladimir Putin that allows temporary state management of critical infrastructure facilities whose owners failed to protect them from drones does not amount to nationalization or a change in ownership, First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov told reporters.
“I want to stress that this is not about nationalization or a change in the form of ownership: the decree implies the state stepping into management of a company to address specific security tasks,” he said.
According to him, the decree does not envision “mass application.” Manturov said “targeted and carefully calibrated decisions will be made at the highest level.”
The deputy prime minister added that private companies, like state-owned ones, play a key role in the national economy, the economy, and the social sphere. However, he said, “business owners approach today’s pressing threats with varying degrees of responsibility,” and in some cases, “ensuring the safety of facilities and employees, unfortunately, is not a priority for them.”
“In such cases, federal executive bodies work with the owners, draw attention to the problems and help resolve them. In situations where there is no response or willingness to cooperate from the owner, and risks arise for entire industries, the state has to temporarily take full responsibility for protecting companies from terrorist attacks,” Manturov concluded.
Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on August 24 that allows temporary management to be imposed at critical infrastructure facilities whose owners fail to protect them from security threats, including drone attacks. The document applies to facilities in the fuel and energy sector, power generation, industry, communications, utilities, and transportation and logistics infrastructure, as well as “other facilities of particular importance for ensuring the security and economic stability of the Russian Federation.” Under the decree, the temporary manager will be Rosimushchestvo or “another entity” to be determined by the government.

items.title: Kremlin calls reports of new mobilization in Russia ‘fabricated stories’
items.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused Ukrainian authorities of trying to “ideologically destabilize the situation in our country” through their statements about a possible mobilization in Russia, he told the Russian media outlet RTVI.
items.body_text:
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused Ukrainian authorities of trying to “ideologically destabilize the situation in our country” through their statements about a possible mobilization in Russia, he told the Russian media outlet RTVI.
Reporters had asked Peskov how the Kremlin views claims that a new mobilization is being prepared, and whether Russian authorities are considering any scenario that would involve announcing one.
“You know, all of this is being planted by the Ukrainian authorities. Naturally, the regime is trying to ideologically destabilize the situation in our country. These are all fabricated stories that are deliberately being planted in the information space,” the Kremlin spokesperson said.
Reports that Russia might announce another mobilization after elections to the State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, have circulated for several weeks. Meduza’s sources, sources in Western media, and Ukrainian officials have all raised the possibility, with Ukrainian authorities mentioning it regularly. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian authorities are allegedly planning to mobilize up to 300,000 people in the fall, a claim Russian authorities deny.
Dmitry Peskov also denied plans for what became September 2022‘s “partial mobilization.” On September 13 of that year, he said that “at the moment” there was no talk of mobilization.

items.title: 'Horrifying to the core': Gurgaon rain traps kids in school buses for over 7 hours
items.summary: A severe monsoon downpour caused extensive flooding across Gurgaon roads on Monday. Many school buses were stranded for several hours, causing significant distress to students. Parents faced helplessness while tracking their children and exchanging updates on messaging groups. Some parents waded through deep water to reach their children from stranded buses. The incident highlighted the city's recurring infrastructure failures during heavy rainfall.
items.body_text:
GURGAON: When a student of Class II returned home on Monday, she was traumatised and stressed. Kiara, who had left school in Sector 47 at 12.30pm, reached home in Sector 51 at 8.30pm.
There were many more like her, who spent anywhere between 3-6 hours in school buses before they could finally reach home as a monsoon downpour flooded roads and left buses stranded on Monday afternoon, leaving hundreds of parents bitter and seething about the city's civic infrastructure.
Parents could do little beyond calling the school, tracking buses and exchanging updates on messaging groups. A series of messages exchanged among parents captured the anxiety as school transport got stuck at severely waterlogged stretches, particularly around Subhash Chowk. "Have the kids reached home?" an anxious parent asked in a group. The replies offered little reassurance. As rain battered the city, their hearts pounded. The helplessness deepened as the hours passed. "Kyra's bus is stuck at Subhash Chowk. It has been more than two hours," an anxious parent said as updates continued to come in. Those who tried to drive towards the stranded buses found their cars could make little progress.
At Subhash Chowk, parents were seen wading to the buses to get their children out and carry them back on their laps. "Some parents waded through 3.5 feet of water for several hundred metres to escort children trapped inside school buses to safety and then waited for their guardians to turn up," said a parent whose daughter was among those in the stranded buses.
A parent's response summed up the mood: "It is horrifying to the core." "We pay taxes and our kids are getting stuck in buses for hours. I mean, what is too much to expect from the govt?" the parent asked. For many families, the anger was directed at what they described as the recurring failure of the city's infrastructure during rain. "We were worried because we can't go to pick them up. What if they need to use the toilet, feel hungry or something else happens? We were completely helpless," said a parent.
Aarav and Aarush were among children stuck near Subhash Chowk. Their bus had been stationary since 12.30pm, with waterlogging and broken-down buses further adding to the gridlock. They eventually reached home, stressed and hungry, around 5pm. Another parent described the situation as a "horrible state of affairs". "Don't know why govt is not taking sufficient measures. It has become an everyday affair in the rains. Two hours of rain and the entire city is heavily flooded," the parent said.
items.normalised_title: horrifying to the core gurgaon rain traps kids in school buses for over 7 hours

items.title: No longer safe at the rear? How China's hypersonic weapons could hunt US aircraft
items.body_text:
China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air missiles, a new capability that could threaten high-value US aircraft such as command-and-control and surveillance planes from thousands of miles away, according to Bloomberg.
The development is part of Chinaâs wider effort to expand the use of its huge missile arsenal for different military missions. A person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that China has also added air-to-air capabilities to some hypersonic cruise missiles and anti-ship capabilities to several other missile types.
China Reveals New Mobility Trick For DF-17 Hypersonic Missile | Watch
Hypersonic weapons could target support aircraft
US military aircraft such as aerial tankers, airborne warning-and-control planes and flying command posts are designed to stay away from the main battlefield. But the new Chinese weapons could put even these aircraft at risk.
A hypersonic glide vehicle launched by a DF-17 missile could travel about 1,500 miles (2,414 km), a distance just short of the route from China to the US territory of Guam, a major American military base.
Chinaâs DF-27 missile has an estimated range of about 5,000 miles, putting Hawaii within its reach.
Hypersonic glide vehicles, or HGVs, are warheads that can move and change direction while travelling through the atmosphere. 
This makes them harder to track and intercept than traditional ballistic missiles.
No other country is publicly known to operate a weapon that combines an HGV with air-to-air missiles.
A report by the US air forceâs China Aerospace Studies Institute this year said that Chinaâs missile modernisation efforts âincreasingly prioritize the ability to inflict coordinated, systemâlevel damage across an adversaryâs operational architecture.â
Weapon has major challenges
Despite the threat, using a ballistic missile to attack an aircraft thousands of miles away would not be simple.
At maximum range, a ballistic missile could take 20 minutes or more to reach its target. This means the missile would need highly accurate and constantly updated information about the aircraftâs location.
The process of collecting information from distant sensors and passing it to the missile creates a long âkill chainâ, which an enemy could potentially disrupt.
There is another major risk. A ballistic missile launch could be mistaken for a nuclear attack. This âdiscrimination problemâ could make the weapon especially dangerous during a major conflict, as an opponent might misinterpret the launch and respond with nuclear weapons.
China expands missile arsenal
China appears to have sharply increased missile production in recent years. Bloomberg reported in May that Chinese missile production rose at the fastest pace since Xi Jinping became president in 2013, based on its analysis of the sectorâs finances.
Chinaâs long-range PL-15 air-to-air missile has already been used in combat. The missile featured during last yearâs brief conflict between India and Pakistan, with Pakistan saying it used the weapons to shoot down several Indian aircraft.
The Pentagon estimated that China had at least 3,150 ballistic missiles and 300 ground-launched cruise missiles as of 2024. Those figures represented increases of 147% and 50%, respectively, from 2015, when the US began publicly disclosing such estimates.
US also develops longer-range missiles
Long-range air-to-air missiles are considered important for any future major conflict.
The US has developed the AIM-174B from RTX Corp.âs SM-6 air defence missile. Its exact range is classified, although the ground-launched SM-6 can travel 250 miles or more.
On Saturday, the US Navy said it was testing the AIM-424 Malice air-to-air missile made by RTX unit Raytheon Co. The missile has a range of more than 300 miles, according to the Navy.
Lockheed Martin Corp.âs AIM-260 is also in production but has not yet entered service. It is expected to have a very long range.

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Monday took a swipe at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) after waterlogging was seen at Delhi's Talkatora Stadium, where BJP national president Nitin Nabin flagged off a series of âPavan Mati Kalashâ processions.AAP MLA from Kondli Kuldeep Kumar shared a video on X showing Nabin flagging off the yatra amid waterlogged portions of the stadium. Taking a dig at Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta and the BJP, Kumar wrote:
âChief Minister @gupta_rekha ji has made excellent arrangements for a splendid swimming pool at Talkatora Stadium today for BJP's National President Nitin Nabin ji! Nitin Nabin ji inaugurated the swimming pool by waving the flag and gave full credit for this work to the accomplished Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ji!â
BJP holds Sant Ravidas anniversary programme
The AAP's jibe came after BJP leaders on Monday gathered at the stadium to launch the procession as part of the party's Sant Ravidas birth anniversary programme.Led by Nabin, BJP leaders flagged off âPavan Mati Kalashâ processions across all districts of Delhi to mark the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas.The programme at Talkatora Stadium was organised under the banner of the âSamrasta Sankalp Abhiyanâ.Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra and several seers and spiritual leaders also attended the event, according to news agency PTI.
Nabin said Sant Ravidas showed society the path of social harmony and equality.Gupta said sacred soil brought to Delhi from Varanasi, described as Sant Ravidas' birthplace, would be taken to different sections of society.âOur effort is to ensure that this sacred soil reaches every household and every locality, and through it, the teachings and blessings of Gurudev Sant Shiromani Ravidasji reach every individual,â Gupta said.
She said the âPavan Mati Kalash Abhiyanâ was intended to take Sant Ravidas' thoughts and message to households, streets and localities across Delhi.Malhotra said the BJP was conducting a nationwide campaign on the occasion of Sant Ravidas' 650th birth anniversary to take his life, thoughts and teachings to different sections of society.

items.title: Trump plans to impose over $100,000 fee for H-1B visas: How will it impact Indians
items.summary: The proposed rule by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, posted in the Federal Register on August 24, would make a ⁠fee of $103,265 permanent, which will significantly impact Indians.
items.body_text:
U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday (August 24, 2026) released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented fee of more than $100,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers.
The fee, first temporarily imposed by Mr. Trump in 2025, dramatically raises the cost of visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors, spelling bad news for Indian techies and students who aspire to work/study in the U.S.
What is H1-B visa programme?
The H-1B programme allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers with training in specialty fields. It offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 visas for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years.
Mr. Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program say it is abused by many companies who replace American workers with cheaper foreign labor. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers for some jobs and to allow U.S. businesses to recruit top talent.
About 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee on a total of 85 visa applications as of late February, according to court filings, the Reuters reported
How will H1-B visa fee hike impact Indians
Those visas typically came with fees between $2,000 and $5,000 before the U.S. President’s order. The proposed rule by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, posted in the Federal Register on August 24, would make a fee of $103,265 permanent. It could be finalised by the end of the year.
Indians account for the largest share of H-1B visa holders, making up 71% of all beneficiaries in FY2024. This move will significantly impact Indian technology workers who are hired by tech companies and others on H-1B visas.
The Hindu had earlier reported that a $100,000 surcharge would, in a majority of cases match or even exceed the yearly salaries earned by Indian H-1B workers. Since Indian professionals typically report lower median wages than their peers from other countries, they are likely to be hit the hardest, both in absolute numbers and as a share of total workers.
Who are exempted from fee hike
But the fee would not apply to visas granted to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, or to renewals of current visas.
Fee hike faces legal challenges
The fee hike is being challenged by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the largest U.S. business lobbying group, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalized.
A federal judge in June 2026 ruled that the fee was unlawful and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it, much to the relief of Indian diaspora. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group.
Amid Mr. Trump’s broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down more than 25% from 2024 and fewer than half of the 794,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data, opens new tab from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.
The Trump administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed a new visa selection process that would favor higher-skilled and better-paid workers. Earlier in August, the Department of Homeland Security in a separate rule added fees of up to $4,500, opens new tab to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the United States.
The U.S. administration move is aimed at protecting American workers while ensuring that companies have a pathway to hire “truly extraordinary people” and bring them to the United States.
(With inputs from Reuters)
Published - August 25, 2026 12:41 pm IST

items.title: ‘Structural differences have not disappeared’: Chinese strategic affairs scholar on India-China ties
items.summary: On the border, I would expect the immediate focus to be less on a dramatic settlement and more on institutionalising stability, says Hu Shisheng, leading Chinese strategic affairs scholar on South Asia.
items.body_text:
Ahead of talks in Beijing on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Hu Shisheng, a leading Chinese strategic affairs scholar on South Asia, said the focus of both countries would be on “institutionalising stability” even as “structural differences” in the relationship remained.
Also Read | Eyes on Xi visit, ‘early harvest’ as Doval heads to Beijing
India and China will on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) hold the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) on the boundary question. Mr. Doval and Mr. Wang, who is also a member of the Politburo, will also take stock of relations ahead of next month’s expected visit to India by Chinese President Xi Jinping for the BRICS Summit, his first visit in seven years.
“On the border, I would expect the immediate focus to be less on a dramatic settlement and more on institutionalising stability. The priority is to prevent misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC, strengthen military and diplomatic communication, and turn last year’s idea of an ‘early harvest’ into an operational process,” Mr. Hu, who is Director of the South Asia Institute at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR) in Beijing, told The Hindu.
NSA Doval calls on Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng ahead of border talks
He was referring to an agreement at last year’s 24th round on establishing an Expert Group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on border affairs to explore “early harvest on boundary delimitation”.
“The two WMCC meetings this year have discussed delimitation, so there has been procedural progress, but there is still no public indication of a concrete sectoral delimitation agreement,” Mr. Hu said. “The realistic next step would be to operationalise the Expert Group, agree on its mandate, timetable and criteria for identifying relatively less contentious sectors, rather than expect an immediate breakthrough on the boundary itself.”
The broader challenge facing the two SRs, he said, was whether both sides “can work out a sustainable modus vivendi that avoids confrontation, keeps differences manageable, and preserves space for cooperation”.
Mr. Hu said the timing of Mr. Doval’s visit, before the September 12 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, added significance to the visit with Mr. Xi expected to visit India.
“Both sides have a strong incentive to keep the border stable and create a favourable political atmosphere for possible leader-level interaction,” he said, adding that he viewed maintaining stability on the border, achieving “concrete and operational progress” on “early harvest” outcomes, and creating favourable conditions for the BRICS Summit as immediate priorities for the border talks.

At the strategic level, he added, Mr. Doval’s visit would help “clear potential obstacles ahead of the BRICS Summit and lay the groundwork for possible leader-level engagement.” He said ensuring no unexpected border incident before the summit, setting the political tone and identifying deliverables for a possible leaders’ meeting, and coordinating the handover of the BRICS agenda from India to China, which takes over as chair next year, would be three essential issues on the table.
The view in Beijing, as in Delhi, is that the normalisation in relations since the October 2024 meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi is likely to remain gradual and measured.
“As for the broader normalisation, I would describe it as strategic risk management rather than strategic realignment,” Mr. Hu said. “Recent difficulties in India-U.S. relations may give New Delhi greater incentives to diversify its strategic options, while the relative stabilisation of China-U.S. ties reduces some of the external pressure on China-India relations. items.title: Pakistan, Iran explore reopening Strait of Hormuz, easing West Asia tensions
items.body_text:
Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir has held "comprehensive discussions" with the Iranian leadership in Tehran, focusing on measures to prevent further escalation of the West Asia conflict and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the army's media wing said on Tuesday (August 25, 2026).
The Army Chief, who was accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, concluded a day-long visit to Iran as part of Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to break the deadlock in the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
It added that the visit was "part of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to end the stalemate in the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and explore ways for achieving enduring peace and a permanent end to instability in the region”.
The Army Chief called on Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Mohsen Rezaei, Representative of the Supreme Leader on the Supreme National Security Council, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Parliament of Iran, Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of Iran, and Eskandar Momeni, Minister of Interior of Iran.
"Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict,” the statement said.
The Strait of Hormuz is a 55-km-wide narrow waterway between Iran and Oman, separating the Persian Gulf from the Arabian Sea.
It is one of the busiest and most strategically significant shipping routes in the world, as a fifth of global oil passed through it before the conflict began on February 28.
The discussions between leaders from Pakistan and Iran also covered regional peace and possible ways to reach a negotiated settlement to the disputes, the statement said.
The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan's "constructive role” in facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, according to the statement.
Pakistan has been leading the push for peace and reviving its mediation efforts in the stalled U.S.-Iran peace negotiations.
In April, a ceasefire was announced with an agreement to end the U.S.-Iran conflict. However, the peace process faltered later on and has not been put back on track.
The conflict began when the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation and choking the vital Strait of Hormuz and entailing a petroleum price hike.
An interim peace agreement, which Pakistan signed as a guarantor, derailed last month as tensions escalated in West Asia with the U.S. and Iran resuming military strikes. Pakistan's efforts to revive the talks have so far failed to yield results.
The visit by Pakistan's leadership was part of the country's broader diplomatic efforts to help break the deadlock in the conflict and explore ways to achieve lasting peace and an end to regional instability.
The visit comes as Washington ramps up pressure on Iran with an expanded round of sanctions, which U.S. officials say are designed to cut off Tehran's economic lifeline and put the world on notice to cease doing business with the country.
President Donald Trump has also warned of economic consequences for countries providing what he called "any type of lifeline" to Iran, as Washington seeks to intensify pressure on Iran.
Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have been severely disrupted, while Tehran has threatened to target unauthorised tankers attempting to transit the waterway.

items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Rainfall Flood LIVE Photos Update; Delhi NCR MP UP IMD Alert | Rajasthan Mumbai Weather Uttarakhand Himachal
LIVEदिल्ली-NCR में लगातार दूसरे दिन तेज बारिश, गुरुग्राम में वर्क-फ्रॉम-होम:यूपी में 4 की मौत; एमपी समेत 15 राज्यों में ऑरेंज अलर्ट
- कॉपी लिंक
दिल्ली-NCR में मंगलवार को लगातार दूसरे दिन तेज बारिश हो रही है। एम्स फ्लाईओवर, कनॉट प्लेस, ITO और आरके पुरम समेत कई इलाकों में 3-4 फीट तक पानी भर गया। मौसम विभाग ने रेड अलर्ट जारी किया है।
दिल्ली-गुरुग्राम को जोड़ने वाले NH-48 पर महिपालपुर के पास ट्रैफिक जाम लगा। दिल्ली एयरपोर्ट ने यात्रियों के लिए एडवाइजरी जारी की। सोमवार को करीब 390 फ्लाइट्स लेट हुईं, 15 डायवर्ट और 26 कैंसिल की गईं।
गुरुग्राम में कई जगह 3 फीट तक पानी भरने के बाद मंगलवार को सरकारी दफ्तरों और स्कूलों में वर्क फ्रॉम होम लागू किया गया। सोमवार को कई स्कूल बसें 3-6 घंटों तक पानी में फंसी रहीं।
यूपी के अयोध्या समेत 15 शहरों में बारिश हो रही है। वाराणसी में सोमवार रात 8 बजे से बारिश जारी है और स्कूल बंद कर दिए गए हैं। बारिश से जुड़ी घटनाओं में 4 लोगों की मौत हुई। मथुरा में सड़कें और रिहायशी इलाके जलमग्न हैं।
मध्य प्रदेश के भोपाल समेत कई जिलों में भी तेज बारिश हुई। विदिशा के बाजार में पानी भर गया और भोपाल में ट्रैफिक प्रभावित हुआ। प्रदेश में अब तक 28.75 इंच बारिश हुई है।
मौसम विभाग ने 27 अगस्त तक एमपी, यूपी, छत्तीसगढ़, ओडिशा, झारखंड, उत्तराखंड और केरल समेत 15 राज्यों में भारी बारिश का ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया है।
सैटेलाइट मैप में देखें मानसूनी बादलों की स्थिति
देशभर से मौसम की तस्वीरें
देशभर के मौसम से जुड़े अपडेट्स जानने के लिए नीचे दिए गए लाइव ब्लॉग को देखें…
लाइव अपडेट्स
- कॉपी लिंक
छत्तीसगढ़ के कोरबा में हसदेव नदी में उफान के कारण देवपहरी झरने के पास टापू पर रात भर फंसे तीन दोस्तों को बचाने के लिए SDRF का रेस्क्यू जारी है।
- कॉपी लिंक
- कॉपी लिंक
मध्य प्रदेश के देवास में रात भर हुई बारिश के बाद करीब 8 बच्चों को ले जा रही एक स्कूल वैन पानी से भरे अंडरब्रिज में फंस गई। कुछ बच्चे छत पर चढ़ गए। आस-पास के लोगों ने करीब एक घंटे बाद सभी बच्चों को बचाया और बाद में रस्सी का इस्तेमाल करके वैन को बाहर निकाला।
- कॉपी लिंक
- कॉपी लिंक
- कॉपी लिंक
उत्तर प्रदेश के मंगलवार सुबह से वाराणसी, अयोध्या, झांसी, जौनपुर और गाजीपुर समेत 15 शहरों में बारिश हो रही है। काशी में सोमवार रात 8 बजे से रुक-रुक कर हो रही बारिश से सड़कें तालाब बन गई हैं। BHU गेट पर घुटनों तक पानी भरा है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
राजस्थान में आज 17 जिलों में तेज बारिश का यलो अलर्ट है। जयपुर, कोटा सहित कई जिलों में सुबह से बारिश का दौर जारी है। सोमवार को अलग-अलग जिलों में 4 इंच तक बरसात हुई। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
आधे मध्य प्रदेश में मंगलवार को तेज बारिश की चेतावनी जारी की गई है। मौसम केंद्र (IMD) भोपाल के अनुसार, टीकमगढ़, दमोह, नरसिंहपुर, बैतूल और राजगढ़ में अति भारी बारिश का ऑरेंज अलर्ट है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
छत्तीसगढ़ के कोरबा के देवपहरी जलप्रपात में तीन युवक टापू पर फंसे हुए हैं। रातभर SDRF ने ग्रामीणों के साथ रेस्क्यू अभियान चलाया, लेकिन जलस्तर कम नहीं हुआ। तीनों अब भी टापू पर हैं। मौके पर SDRF, पुलिस और जिला प्रशासन के अधिकारी मौजूद हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
हिमाचल प्रदेश में मानसून अगले पांच दिन तक कमजोर रहेगा। इससे कई शहरों के तापमान में चार डिग्री सेल्सियस तक का उछाल आएगा। खासकर 25 से 28 अगस्त तक अधिकांश हिस्सों में धूप खिलेगी। मैदानी इलाकों में उमस भरी गर्मी लोगों को परेशान करेगी। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
बिहार में गंगा का जलस्तर लगातार बढ़ रहा है। पटना से लेकर बेगूसराय और भागलपुर तक गंगा का जलस्तर खतरे के निशान के करीब पहुंच गया है। वहीं, गंडक समेत कई नदियां उफान पर हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
पंजाब और चंडीगढ़ में मानसून थोड़ा कमजोर पड़ गया है। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र चंडीगढ़ के मुताबिक, राज्य के तापमान में एक ही दिन में 0.9 डिग्री की वृद्धि हुई है। मंगलवार को नौ जिलों में कुछ स्थानों पर हल्की से मध्यम बारिश हो सकती है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक
उत्तराखंड के 6 जिलों में देर रात से रुक-रुककर बारिश जारी है। 6 जिलों के लिए यलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। सोमवार को पिथौरागढ़ के बंगापानी में आकाशीय बिजली गिरने से 15 बकरियों की मौत हो गई। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
- कॉपी लिंक

items.title: हाथ में तिरंगा था, तभी पैलेट गन चली:साहिल बोला- होश आया तो अस्पताल में था; शरीर में अब भी छर्रे, आंख से दिख नहीं रहा
items.summary: 20 जुलाई को दिल्ली में CJP के संसद मार्च के दौरान पैलेट गन से घायल साहिल लोहचब की आंखों में आज भी दो छर्रे फंसे हैं। दो बार सर्जरी के बावजूद आंखों की रोशनी लौटने की उम्मीद कम है। साहिल ने बताया कि वह दिल्ली पुलिस भर्ती परीक्षा की तैयारी कर रहे थे। परिवार का खर्च चलाने के लिए पार्ट टाइम ड्राइवर का काम भी करते थे। जंतर-मंतर पर परीक्षाओं में गड़बड़ी को लेकर प्रदर्शन शुरू हुआ, तो साहिल छात्रों का समर्थन करने के लिए वहां चले गए। साहिल का आरोप है कि FIR दर्ज कराने के लिए परिवार ने कई बार पुलिस से संपर
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- CJP Protest Pellet Gun Attack Victim; Sahil Lochab Vs Delhi Police | Rahul Gandhi
भास्कर इंटरव्यूहाथ में तिरंगा था, तभी पैलेट गन चली:साहिल बोला- होश आया तो अस्पताल में था; शरीर में अब भी छर्रे, आंख से दिख नहीं रहा
- कॉपी लिंक
20 जुलाई को दिल्ली में CJP के संसद मार्च के दौरान पैलेट गन से घायल साहिल लोहचब की आंखों में आज भी दो छर्रे फंसे हैं। दो बार सर्जरी के बावजूद आंखों की रोशनी लौटने की उम्मीद कम है।
साहिल ने बताया कि वह दिल्ली पुलिस भर्ती परीक्षा की तैयारी कर रहे थे। परिवार का खर्च चलाने के लिए पार्ट टाइम ड्राइवर का काम भी करते थे। जंतर-मंतर पर परीक्षाओं में गड़बड़ी को लेकर प्रदर्शन शुरू हुआ, तो साहिल छात्रों का समर्थन करने के लिए वहां चले गए।
साहिल का आरोप है कि FIR दर्ज कराने के लिए परिवार ने कई बार पुलिस से संपर्क किया, लेकिन सुनवाई नहीं हुई। 21 अगस्त को राहुल गांधी करीब 6 घंटे संसद मार्ग थाने के बाहर धरने पर बैठे, जिसके बाद शिकायत पर FIR दर्ज हुई।
20 जुलाई के प्रदर्शन में क्या हुआ, पैलेट गन से कैसे घायल हुए, राहुल गांधी से कैसे बात हुई, इन सवालों का जवाब लेने दैनिक भास्कर साहिल के घर पहुंचा, पढ़िए एक्सक्लूसिव इंटरव्यू…
सवाल-1: 20 जुलाई को क्या हुआ?
जवाब: मैं CJP प्रोटेस्ट में गया था। जंतर-मंतर पर लाठीचार्ज शुरू हुआ। हम भीड़ के साथ कनॉट प्लेस सर्कल पर पहुंचे। वहां पहले आंसू गैस के गोले छोड़े गए। मेरे हाथ में भारत का झंडा था। तभी मेरे ऊपर पैलेट गन चली। मैं सुन्न हो गया।
सवाल-2: पैलेट गन लगने के बाद क्या हुआ?
जवाब: मेरी हालत खराब होने पर मुझे लेडी हार्डिंग अस्पताल ले गए। लेडी हार्डिंग में 6 से 7 घंटे रखा गया। उसके बाद सफदरजंग भेजा गया। यहां से मुझे एम्स भेजा गया। पहले एम्स के आई-सेंटर भेजा गया, वहां से फिर ट्रॉमा सेंटर भेजा गया।
मेरी आंख की दो बार सर्जरी हो चुकी है, लेकिन अभी भी मैं देख नहीं सकता। डॉक्टरों ने एक महीने का समय दिया है। रोशनी आने के चांस बहुत कम हैं। मेरे दाहिने हाथ में आज भी नसें दबी हुई हैं। मेरी आंख में दो पैलेट अभी भी हैं। मुझे भी 4 से 5 दिनों तक तो होश ही नहीं था।
आगे जानेंगे कि साहिल छात्रों के प्रदर्शन में क्यों गए, लेकिन उससे पहले भास्कर नॉलेज में जानिए पैलेट गन क्या है और भारत में भीड़ नियंत्रण के उपायों को लेकर कानून क्या कहता है।
सवाल-3: आप जंतर-मंतर पर छात्रों के प्रदर्शन में क्यों गए?
जवाब: मैं नीट पेपर लीक और परीक्षाओं में गड़बड़ी के खिलाफ था और प्रदर्शन में योगदान देना चाहता था, इसलिए 20 जुलाई को संसद मार्च में शामिल हुआ था।
सवाल-4: क्या आपने खुद से FIR दर्ज कराने की कोशिश की थी?
जवाब: 14 अगस्त को मेरी मां और वकील थाने गए थे, लेकिन FIR नहीं लिखी गई। फिर हमने डाक से भी शिकायत भेजी और दिल्ली पुलिस को ईमेल भी भेजा था, लेकिन FIR नहीं हुई। हमें FIR की रिसीविंग भी नहीं मिली।
सवाल-5: कितनी बार थाने गए, किस अफसर से मिले?
जवाब: दो से तीन बार थाने गए। कोई सीनियर अधिकारी तो हमसे बात करने को तैयार ही नहीं था। हम लोग क्राइम ब्रांच भी गए थे। वहां भी हमारी सुनवाई नहीं हुई। कोई जवाब नहीं मिल रहा था।
सवाल-6: आप राहुल के संपर्क में कैसे आए? क्या राहुल ने खुद संपर्क किया?
जवाब: करीब 5 दिन बाद राहुल गांधी की टीम ने मेरी मम्मी से बात की। उन्होंने हेल्थ अपडेट मांगा था। हमने बताया कि हमारी FIR नहीं लिखी जा रही है। तब उन्होंने खुद ही हमें बुलाया। इसके बाद 21 अगस्त की सुबह हम लोग उनके पास पहुंचे। उसके बाद उनके साथ ही पहले कनॉट प्लेस थाने गए। राहुल से मुलाकात को मैं भाग्यशाली मानता हूं।
सवाल-7: आपके घर में कौन-कौन हैं? जवाब: परिवार में हम तीन भाई हैं। पिता दीपक दिव्यांग हैं। मैं पढ़ाई के साथ परिवार का खर्च चलाने में भी मदद कर रहा था। अब मुश्किल हो रही है।
मां ज्योति बोलीं- बेटे की जब खबर मिली तो घबरा गई थी
सवाल: आपको बेटे के हादसे के बारे में जानकारी कब मिली? जवाब: 20 जुलाई की सुबह करीब 10 बजे साहिल घर से निकले थे। लेकिन जब 3 बजे भी उन्होंने फोन नहीं उठाया तो वो घबरा गईं।
इसके बाद लेडी हार्डिंग अस्पताल से परिवार को फोन आया। ये बताया गया कि आपके बेटे साहिल को चोट लग गई है। तब हम लेडी हार्डिंग पहुंचे।
सवाल: पैलेट गन की जानकारी कब मिली जवाब: हम टीवी में देख रहे थे। इतना तो लगा कि हाथ में चोट लगी होगी। लेकिन यह नहीं पता था कि पैलेट गन चली है। ये अस्पताल में जाने के बाद ही हमें पता चला।

जम्मू-कश्मीर के शोपियां में 3 संदिग्ध आतंकी गिरफ्तार:हैंड ग्रेनेड और हिजबुल मुजाहिदीन के पोस्टर बरामद; पुलवामा में भी 2 सहयोगी पकड़ाए
- कॉपी लिंक
जम्मू-कश्मीर के शोपियां जिले में सुरक्षाबलों ने सोमवार रात चेकिंग के दौरान तीन संदिग्ध आतंकियों को गिरफ्तार किया। उनके पास से 2 हैंड ग्रेनेड और हिजबुल मुजाहिदीन के पांच पोस्टर मिले हैं।
पुलिस के मुताबिक, आरोपियों की पहचान कुलगाम निवासी जुनैद अहमद डार, आमिर यूसुफ और जुनैद मुजफ्फर के रूप में हुई है। बरामद सामान को कब्जे में लेकर जांच शुरू कर दी गई है।
वहीं, पुलवामा में भी सुरक्षाबलों ने यरवान जंगल में सर्च ऑपरेशन के दौरान दो संदिग्ध आतंकी सहयोगियों को गिरफ्तार किया है। उनकी पहचान लतीफ अहमद दीदाद और एजाज अहमद बजाद के रूप में हुई है।
पुलवामा में पकड़ाए संदिग्धों से हथियार बरामद
पुलवामा में पकड़ाए संदिग्धों के पास से एक पिस्तौल, 12 कारतूस और हैंड ग्रेनेड मिले हैं। पुलिस ने आर्म्स एक्ट और UAPA की संबंधित धाराओं में केस दर्ज किया है। सुरक्षा एजेंसियां हथियारों के सोर्स और दोनों के आतंकी नेटवर्क से संबंधों की जांच कर रही हैं।
सोपोर में सर्च ऑपरेशन के दौरान AK-47, ग्रेनेड और IED बरामद
इससे पहले सोपोर के मंजसीर इलाके में सोमवार रात को सुरक्षाबलों ने जॉइंट सर्च ऑपरेशन में हथियार बरामद किए हैं।
अधिकारियों के मुताबिक, एक खाली पड़े घर से AK-47 राइफल, 3 मैगजीन, 72 कारतूस, 4 हैंड ग्रेनेड और एक IED बरामद किया गया। मामले की जांच जारी है।

items.title: Water cannons used as protesters in Patna break barricades on way to CM residence
items.summary: Water cannons used as protesters in Patna break barricades on way to CM residence
items.body_text:
Water cannons used as protesters in Patna break barricades on way to CM residence
Bihar government job aspirants marched towards the Chief Minister's residence in Patna, breaking through police barricades and clashing with security personnel.
Hundreds of students and jobseekers in Patna broke through police barricades and marched towards Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's residence on Tuesday, triggering clashes with police as Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) aspirants intensified their agitation.
The protesters are demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination and raising concerns over alleged paper leaks, examination irregularities and employment-related issues.
The confrontation broke out after the protesters breached barricades erected along the route to prevent them from advancing. Police personnel deployed to contain the marchers attempted to stop them, leading to a face-off between the two sides.
Police resorted to lathicharge at multiple points and used water cannons to disperse the protesters. Despite the action, the students continued their march and moved closer to the Chief Minister’s residence.
The march began around 10 am from Gandhi Maidan, with students raising slogans as they headed towards the Chief Minister’s residence. The government had deployed barricades along the route, but protesters removed them as they advanced.
The agitation is part of continuing protests by students and job aspirants in Patna’s Gardanibagh area over various demands related to competitive examinations and recruitment.
The protest came a day after student representatives held talks with the Bihar government. Although the discussions were described as positive, the protesters decided to continue their agitation and announced plans to march from Gandhi Maidan to the Chief Minister’s residence.
Student leader Saurav Kumar said the talks with the government had been "positive", but maintained that the protesters would continue their agitation over their demands, including the conduct of a single examination.
"We want to meet Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary because the government keeps making us hold talks with junior officials, after which the matter is closed. If we are given an opportunity for talks with the Chief Minister and an official notice is issued, we are ready to end our protest," a student leader said durign Tuesday's protest.
He said the protesters had been asked to form a delegation for talks, but they made it clear that they would meet only the Chief Minister or, alternatively, the Education Minister.
"Our first demand is that we should be allowed to meet Samrat Choudhary. The second option is that we should be allowed to meet the Education Minister. We will not meet anyone else," he said.
Amid the protests, the Bihar government on Tuesday announced the launch of a monthly 'Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir' (Student Support Camp) to address student grievances.
Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the camps would be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month, allowing students to directly raise their concerns with the officials concerned.
"The Bihar government is launching Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir starting today to ensure prompt resolution of students’ grievances," Choudhary said in a social media post.
He added that students would also be able to register complaints online and track their status through a dedicated portal and helpline number 1100.
The government’s outreach initiative comes against the backdrop of sustained protests across Bihar over examination-related grievances, even as students continue to demand action on the 70th BPSC examination.

items.title: Can no longer work as much: Nitin Gadkari says new generation should take over
items.summary: Can no longer work as much Nitin Gadkari says new generation should take over
items.body_text:
Can no longer work as much: Nitin Gadkari says new generation should take over
Nitin Gadkari said in Nagpur that he can no longer work as much and that the new generation should take over public responsibilities. His remarks came amid talk of a Cabinet expansion and after the BJP's organisational revamp.
Union Minister Nitin Gadkari has said that he can no longer work as much as he used to and that it was time to hand over responsibilities to the new generation.
Speaking at an event in Nagpur, Gadkari said his involvement in public work has reduced of late and that the younger generation should now be given an opportunity to take the work forward. Gadkari's comments came amid a growing buzz of a possible Cabinet reshuffle in the central government.
“Work should be handed over to the new generation. A new generation has come, and the older generation is guiding them,” Gadkari said, explaining how his participation in day-to-day work has come down.
“I have been continuously working in public life for the last 30 years. I have seen many ups and downs and received many awards. But I can’t work much now, the new generation should be given a chance to work,” Gadkari said.
Gadkari, however, also went on to speak about the development work ahead, saying the scale of work would increase in the coming years. He said the aim was to ensure that no tribal village in Maharashtra remained without electricity and that development became visible across the state.
The Union Minister's remarks came just days after the BJP underwent a major organisational overhaul, the first of this scale since 2015, when Amit Shah was the party president.
Last week, the BJP announced its new national team under party president Nitin Nabin. The 65-member team includes 51 new faces, signalling a significant generational shift within the organisation.
The new team has 13 national vice presidents, including former Rajasthan Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje Scindia and former RSS functionary Ram Madhav. Former Union minister Smriti Irani has been appointed one of the party's eight national general secretaries.
The organisational overhaul has also fuelled speculation about a possible reshuffle of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Union Cabinet.

Rafales face China's J-16 jets in rare drill: Why India is watching closely
Chinese J-16 fighters engaged in direct aerial combat drills against Rafale jets for the first time during a joint military exercise between China and Egypt. For India, the exercise carries significance well beyond a routine military drill. Here's why.
Chinese J-16 jets engaged in combat exercises with French-made Rafale fighters for the first time, in a rare military drill that allowed Chinese pilots to test their capabilities against a Western platform. India will be watching the exercise closely, particularly after its Rafales and Chinese J-10 jets, operated by Pakistan, were involved during the hostilities last year.
The China-Egypt 'Eagles of Civilisation' exercise will offer a valuable glimpse into how the two aircraft perform in a simulated combat environment, as well as the capabilities of the J-16. The J-16, nicknamed the 'Hidden Dragon', is a more advanced version of the J-10, and its performance will be of interest to India amid the growing Chinese air power in the region.
Pakistan currently operates the Chinese-made J-10C, the export variant of the J-10, along with the jointly developed JF-17 Thunder. It has also shown interest in acquiring the J-16 fighter jet, which makes it all the more important for India to keep an eye on the exercise. India, on the other hand, is looking to acquire 114 more Rafales from France.
CHINA'S J-16 CROSSES SWORDS WITH RAFALE
The second edition of the drills began on August 22. On Monday, Chinese J-16s engaged in one-on-one air combat drills with Rafales. The pilots engaged in intense confrontations under realistic combat scenarios. Egypt's MiG-29s were also in action.
Footage released by China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) showed a Rafale performing manoeuvres close to a J-16. It was the first time a Chinese fighter jet engaged in direct aerial combat drills against a Rafale.
Both the J-16 and the Rafale are 4.5-generation fighter jets featuring modern avionics, advanced radar, and electronic warfare systems.
The J-16 is a heavyweight, multirole fighter developed by the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC). Widely regarded as one of China's best combat aircraft, it can carry a variety of munitions and deliver more firepower than the J-10 series. Moreover, the J-16 is a twin-engine, two-seater jet designed for longer-range missions.
Wang Yanan, an aviation expert, told Global Times that while the J-16 and the Rafale belong to the same generation, the French aircraft's overall combat capabilities "may not be as comprehensive" as those of the Chinese jet.
However, it must be noted here that the Rafales used by the IAF have India-specific upgrades that differ from those operated by Egypt.
Interestingly, China had initiated a disinformation campaign against the Rafale aircraft after last year's India-Pakistan conflict to hinder the sales of the French fighter jet, the US Congress was informed.
Egypt's air force also operates American F-16 jets, as well as CH-47 Chinook and AH-64 Apache helicopters. However, they are not part of the exercise as the US maintains strict end-use and export-control curbs on its combat aircraft and sensitive technologies. France, by contrast, is less restrictive in its arms exports.
According to experts, the Eagles of Civilisation exercise is being seen as part of a larger trend of China increasingly joining forces with countries that use Western military equipment.
Recently, China participated in a similar exercise with Thailand, which involved the Thai Air Force, which operates F-16s and Saab Gripen fighters.
WHY WILL INDIA BE WATCHING DRILL CLOSELY?
For India, the China-Egypt exercise carries significance well beyond a routine military drill. items.title: Tamil Nadu scraps Parandur Airport project; CM Vijay to find alternative site near Chennai
items.summary: Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay has scrapped the contentious Parandur airport project to protect farmland, announcing alternative sites and a major expansion at Meenambakkam.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay speaks during the state Legislative Assembly session in Chennai. (IANS)
In light of protecting agricultural lands and local livelihoods, the Government of Tamil Nadu has decided to move away from the highly debated project of Parandur airport to seek a better site.
Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay said while addressing the Assembly that all the efforts put forth in setting up the Greenfield International Airport of Parandur in Kancheepuram district have been scrapped.
Grassroots support: The decision comes as a huge relief for people in Eganapuram and its 12 nearby villages who protested against the relocation of over 1,000 families for almost three years now.
Agricultural safeguarding: Highlighting the fact that agriculture forms the backbone of the nation, the Chief Minister said that no future developments should happen at such high costs involving local communities and farmlands.
Political repercussions: The reversal was criticized heavily by the opposition leaders, including former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, who termed it as an "irreversible blow" to regional economic development.
In order to overcome current capacity issues without affecting the community, the state is now diverting attention to the already existing hub. As per the state's Industries Policy Note, the Airports Authority of India (AAI) has designed a plan for structural improvements.
Capacity upgrade: Currently, the facility accommodates nearly 30 million passengers every year, which is set to increase due to completion of terminals.
Northwest extension: The planners plan to construct a passenger handling system in the northwest of the Meenambakkam airport to facilitate freight and travel management.
Linkage assistance: The officials of the state have promised full cooperation with regard to providing clearance for construction of a new road linking the terminal complex to the national highway.
While the optimisation process is taking place at the existing Chennai International Airport, the administration believes that a second international airport is necessary for sustainable industrial development.
Technical suitability check: The Airports Authority of India (AAI) will conduct a thorough study before signing an agreement with the government.

items.title: Maharashtra: 3 newborns die after fire breaks out in Amravati government hospital
items.summary: About 39 babies were in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Amravati District Women’s Hospital when a fire broke out, killing three newborns
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Fire broke out in the NICU of Amravati District Women’s Hospital.
Three newborns died after a fire broke out in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Amravati District Women’s Hospital early Monday, raising fresh concerns over fire safety and equipment risks in critical hospital wards. The blaze reportedly began after a ventilator exploded, while staff rushed to evacuate 39 babies. Six infants were moved to a super-speciality hospital for further treatment.
The fire broke out at around 3.30 am on Monday on the third floor of the District Women’s Hospital in Amravati, Maharashtra. Preliminary information indicates that the blaze followed an explosion in a ventilator inside the neonatal unit.
About 39 newborns were admitted to the NICU when the fire started. Doctors, nurses and other hospital staff immediately began moving the babies out of the affected ward.
#WATCH | Amravati, Maharashtra: Three newborn babies lost their lives after a fire broke out in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of the District Women’s Hospital. According to preliminary information, the fire erupted at around 3.30 am on the third floor of the hospital,… pic.twitter.com/fhSQvykujw
— ANI (@ANI) August 24, 2026
Despite the evacuation effort, three newborns suffered fatal burn injuries in the fire. Six other infants were shifted to the Super Speciality Hospital for further treatment.
The hospital staff's timely response helped save several other newborns. Further details regarding the cause of the fire and the condition of the rescued infants are awaited, ANI reported.
The Amravati Police Commissioner said, "Prima facie, it appears that the fire started inside a ventilator installed in the NICU."
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday ordered the health administration to conduct a high-level inquiry into the incident.
In a post on X, CM Fadnavis said, "The incident in which three children died in a fire that broke out last night at the District Women's Hospital in Amravati is extremely tragic and heartbreaking. We stand with the families of the victims in their grief. The health administration has been ordered to conduct a high-level inquiry into the incident. The strictest possible action will be taken against those found responsible."
CM Fadnavis also announced financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to the families of the deceased.
"The Health Minister and the Secretary have both been instructed to visit Amravati today itself. The state government will provide financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to the families of the deceased. The Amravati District Collector has also been directed to ensure that the injured children receive treatment at government expense. Fortunately, 36 children were successfully rescued and are safe," he added in the post.
अमरावती येथील जिल्हा स्त्री रुग्णालयात काल रात्री लागलेल्या आगीत तीन बालकांचा मृत्यू झाल्याची घटना अतिशय दुःखद आणि हृदयद्रावक आहे. त्यांच्या कुटुंबियांच्या दुःखात आम्ही सहभागी आहोत.
या घटनेची उच्चस्तरीय चौकशी करण्याचे आदेश आरोग्य प्रशासनाला देण्यात आले आहेत. या घटनेतील दोषींवर…
The Amravati incident came days after a separate NICU fire at the Chhindwara District Hospital in Madhya Pradesh. Three newborns suffered burn injuries after a warmer caught fire early Saturday.
District hospital Civil Surgeon Kanchan Dubey said the incident took place at around 1.50 am. According to her, a spark in the filament of a warmer used in the NICU caused the equipment to catch fire and led to injuries to three babies.
She said 33 children were in the unit at the time. Three babies were affected, while hospital staff quickly moved the other 30 children to safety.
"There were 30 other children there, making a total of 33. Three babies were affected and the remaining 30 were immediately shifted to safety by our staff, including nurses and guards, who acted promptly and saved their lives," she said.

items.title: Delhi: 6 injured, including 2 MLAs, after car crashes into SUV
items.summary: Delhi Police said all six people involved in the crash suffered minor injuries.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Visual from the spot.
At least six people, including Delhi AAP MLA Anil Jha and Karnataka BJP MLA Abhay Patil, were injured in a road accident near ITO in central Delhi on Sunday night, police said. The accident occurred around 9:30 pm near the PWD office on Vikas Marg when a Maruti Suzuki Swift travelling from Laxmi Nagar towards ITO hit the road divider, crossed the railing and collided with an oncoming Toyota Innova.
According to Delhi Police, 32-year-old Ashutosh Pandey was driving the Swift. He was travelling with his wife and two minor children from Laxmi Nagar towards ITO.
Police said the car lost control near the PWD office, struck the road divider and crossed the railing into the opposite lane. It then collided with the Innova, which was travelling from ITO towards Laxmi Nagar.
The Innova was carrying Anil Jha, the sitting AAP MLA from Delhi's Kirari constituency, and Abhay Patil, a BJP MLA from Karnataka. Both MLAs were among those injured in the crash.
(Note: Graphic visuals. Viewer discretion is advised.)
#WATCH | Delhi: A road accident took place at the ITO traffic signal in Delhi, in front of the old Police Headquarters, after an out-of-control car crashed through the divider. More details awaited.
pic.twitter.com/IMmGmKciu2
Delhi Police said all six people involved in the crash suffered minor injuries. They were taken to Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Hospital for treatment and were reported to be in stable condition.
Police said, "Today, at about 9:30 PM, a PCR call regarding a road traffic accident was received at PS I.P. Estate. On reaching the spot, two vehicles, an Innova and a Swift car, were found involved in the accident. As per preliminary local inquiry, the Swift car was being driven by Ashutosh Pandey, aged 32 years, who was travelling along with his wife and two minor children from Laxmi Nagar towards ITO. Near the PWD Office, the Swift car hit the divider and, after crossing the railing, collided with the Innova coming from ITO towards Laxmi Nagar," the Delhi Police said.
Police added, "The Innova was occupied by Anil Jha, sitting MLA from Kirari Vidhan Sabha, and Abhay Patil, MLA from Karnataka. All persons sustained minor injuries and were shifted to LNJP Hospital. All are in stable condition."
The accident took place in front of the old police headquarters near the PWD office. The crash caused major damage to the front of the Innova and affected traffic in the area.
Delhi Fire Brigade teams were called to the scene to help remove the damaged vehicles. The vehicles were cleared from the road to restore traffic movement. Police are continuing their inquiry into the accident.

items.title: Trump administration weighs steep new H-1B, OPT fees: Why Indians could be hit hard
items.summary: Trump’s proposed H-1B and OPT fee hikes could make the American dream significantly more expensive for Indian workers and students.
items.body_text:
The Trump administration is weighing a fresh set of measures that could significantly increase the cost of working and studying in the United States for foreign nationals, with H-1B workers and international students on Optional Practical Training (OPT) potentially facing steep new fees.
The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has sent proposed regulations to the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB), including a proposal that could push the H-1B visa fee to $103,265. The administration had introduced a $100,000 H-1B fee last year, but its implementation was subsequently blocked by the courts.
The proposals could have major implications for Indians, who account for more than 70 per cent of H-1B beneficiaries. In 2024, the US Citizenship and Immigration Services approved 399,402 H-1B petitions, with Indian-born beneficiaries accounting for around 71 per cent of them.
According to immigration services firm Fragomen, the DHS proposals could also introduce a fee of around $100,000 for certain OPT applications. The firm said the proposed rules have already cleared the OMB review process, although their exact provisions remain confidential until they are formally published.
The proposals could therefore make the US significantly more expensive for foreign professionals, international students transitioning from universities into employment, and American employers seeking to sponsor skilled foreign workers.
H-1B and OPT fees could rise sharply
Fragomen said an OPT fee proposal was submitted to OMB on August 20, while a proposal concerning fees for certain H-1B petitions was received and cleared by the OMB a day earlier, on August 19.
The immigration services firm cautioned that the DHS could propose a $100,000 fee for OPT applications. The proposed H-1B fee, meanwhile, could be linked to the ongoing legal battle over the administration’s earlier $100,000 H-1B petition fee.
The exact details of both proposals are not yet public and will only become clear once the regulations are officially released.
Indians among the biggest stakeholders
Any major change to the H-1B system is particularly significant for India because Indian nationals dominate the programme.
USCIS data shows that Indians accounted for roughly 71 per cent of approved H-1B beneficiaries in 2024. That means higher visa costs, tighter rules or increased financial burdens could disproportionately affect Indian technology professionals and other skilled workers seeking employment in the US.
The impact could extend beyond workers themselves. US companies that depend on H-1B talent could also face substantially higher costs when sponsoring foreign employees.
For international students, a steep OPT fee could make the transition from an American university to the US job market considerably more expensive.
H-1B workers could also lose a 60-day grace period
The proposed fees come alongside another potentially significant change.
Earlier this month, DHS proposed eliminating the existing 60-day grace period available to certain H-1B workers after their employment ends. Under the current system, eligible workers can generally remain in the US for up to 60 days after losing their jobs while seeking new employment or otherwise resolving their immigration status.
If the proposed rule is finalised, affected workers and their dependants could be required to leave the US much sooner after employment ends, potentially creating additional uncertainty for thousands of families.
The proposed changes signal a broader tightening of the US immigration system under the Trump administration, with foreign workers, international students and employers likely to bear a greater share of the financial and regulatory burden.
For Indians, who form the overwhelming majority of H-1B beneficiaries, the consequences could be particularly significant.

items.title: SC Justice PB Varale says 0.1% of Nashik Kumbh Mela funds could save Marathi schools: How the Leftist trope of pitting Hindu faith against welfare is flawed
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice PB Varale’s Kumbh-school comparison echoes a classic Leftist trope: pitting Hindu religious expenditure against schools and welfare to portray the former as inherently frivolous.
items.body_text:
There is little to disagree with in the concern expressed by Supreme Court Justice Prasanna Varale over the deteriorating condition of Marathi-medium schools and residential schools in Maharashtra. If schools are genuinely being forced to shut down for want of a relatively small amount of money, the Maharashtra government must answer why it has failed to provide that money.
But the argument that even 0.1 per cent of the money allocated for the Nashik Kumbh Mela could have saved more than 100 Marathi schools gets the priorities of governance completely backwards.
Justice Varale, speaking during a visit to his former school in Nashik, said that if around Rs 32 crore, 0.1 per cent of the Kumbh allocation, had been spent on education, more than 100-150 Marathi schools could have been prevented from shutting down. The concern over educational infrastructure is legitimate. The comparison with the Kumbh, however, is not.
Why must schools and the Kumbh be competing priorities?
The first question that needs to be asked is: Why must the Kumbh Mela and Marathi schools be presented as competing priorities in the first place?
Maharashtra is perfectly capable of doing both.
The state has approved a comprehensive Rs 22,425.39 crore development plan for the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela. The plan is not simply a cheque being handed over for religious festivities. The Kumbh requires enormous temporary and permanent infrastructure because lakhs of devotees will descend on Nashik, creating extraordinary requirements for roads, sanitation, water supply, transportation, medical facilities, crowd management, public safety and other civic infrastructure. The state has constituted dedicated committees and an authority precisely because the event requires large-scale administrative coordination.
So when someone says, “Take 0.1 per cent of the Kumbh allocation and save the schools”, the obvious response should be: Why take it from the Kumbh at all?
Why not ask the government to find Rs 32 crore elsewhere?
Why not ask why schools were allowed to reach a stage where Rs 32 crore could supposedly make the difference between survival and closure?
And if the state has Rs 32 crore to spare, why should that money become available for schools only after taking it away from an infrastructure programme connected with one of India’s largest religious gatherings?
Kumbh infrastructure is not simply “religious expenditure”
The comparison itself creates an unnecessary hierarchy: education is presented as an essential public good while the Kumbh is subtly reduced to an expendable cultural or religious expenditure. That is where the argument becomes problematic.
The Kumbh Mela is not some private religious function for a handful of people. It is a civilisational and spiritual gathering followed by millions of Hindus. The administration has a responsibility to ensure that people who participate in it have access to basic civic facilities and, more importantly, can do so safely.
Imagine the consequences if the government simply said that sanitation, roads, medical facilities, crowd-control infrastructure or public amenities at the Kumbh were unnecessary because the money could instead be spent elsewhere. The same people would quite rightly ask why the state failed to prepare for an event in which an enormous number of people are expected to gather at the same place.
The purpose of Kumbh expenditure is therefore not merely to “spend money on a religious event”. It is to build the infrastructure required to manage a massive congregation safely and efficiently.
Criticise waste, not the existence of the expenditure
To oppose wasteful expenditure is legitimate. To question whether every rupee is being spent wisely is legitimate. To demand greater allocation for education is legitimate.
But turning Kumbh expenditure into the explanation for the failure of Marathi-medium schools is not.

items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count

items.title: 'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
items.summary: "These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
items.body_text:
'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
- World News
- 3 min read
Ankara: Turkiye on Wednesday rejected Israel's claim that its airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur military airport were linked to a planned Turkish troop deployment, saying the allegations "lack seriousness" and seek to legitimise strikes on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In a post on X, the Turkish Presidential Communications Directorate said, “The allegations put forward by the Israeli Prime Ministry, which lack seriousness, aim to legitimize Israel's unlawful airstrikes targeting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.” It added, "The accusations raised stem from Netanyahu's intent to continue his expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of elections in Israel."
Turkiye said it supports the establishment of lasting peace in the region, adding that "the sole path to this lies in Netanyahu abandoning his aggressive and coercive policies and demonstrating respect for international law". "Turkey will steadfastly continue its cooperation with the Syrian Government on legitimate grounds to establish peace, stability, and prosperity in Syria, and will never allow Syria to be destabilized," it said.
The remarks came after Israel carried out airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Syria's eastern Idlib province. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said that Syria was allowing Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (local time), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the strikes "yet another very worrying violation" of Syria's territorial integrity and airspace.
Advertisement
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
In a statement, the ministry said Egypt "fully rejects" Israel's continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and warned that the strikes could further destabilise Syria at a critical time when the country requires support to restore stability and pursue political solutions. Cairo called on the international community to "assume its responsibilities" by putting an end to repeated Israeli violations and adopting firm measures to deter actions that could fuel a broader regional conflict.
Advertisement
Earlier on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel and Syria had agreed to maintain a security "status quo". In a post on X, Netanyahu's office said, "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," the statement said.
"Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added. Meanwhile, US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack expressed concern over the Israeli airstrikes, calling them an "unnecessary escalation". "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.
The airbase was targeted in four airstrikes, marking the first reported attack on the facility since the fall of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.

items.body_text:
'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
- World News
- 2 min read
Ottawa: With Ottawa and Washington continually engaged in discussions over the 50 per cent tariff on a select range of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the implementation of the tariffs has been postponed until August 21.
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
"Over the last number of weeks, Canada has engaged in intensive discussions with the United States to address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families," he said.
The Canadian Prime Minister observed that while significant headway has been made, key work remains to be done. Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done. As this work is ongoing, the United States has agreed to postpone the implementation of its 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods under Section 338 of the U.S. Tariff Act of 1930 until the end of day, August 21," he said.
Advertisement
The announcement comes in the nick of time as the Trump administration's latest round of tariffs was originally scheduled to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday.
According to Canadian public broadcaster CBC, the levies would have applied to hundreds of products worth more than USD 28 billion, from plywood and cement to wine and hockey sticks.
Advertisement
His remarks come shortly after US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) announced a three-day pause on the 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian imports that were due to take effect the following morning, saying the United States and Canada had reached a deal subject to the finalisation of documents.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, “I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for a three day period, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!”
The three-day pause is expected to provide additional time for negotiations between the two countries. Talks intensified last week, with Canadian officials holding discussions with Trump's negotiating team in Washington.

items.title: Supreme Court Seeks Replies From 20 Rebel TMC MPs On Abhishek Banerjee’s Disqualification Plea
items.summary: Supreme Court Seeks Replies From 20 Rebel TMC MPs On Abhishek Banerjee’s Disqualification Plea
items.body_text:
The Supreme Court issued notices to 20 Trinamool Congress MPs in connection with a petition seeking their disqualification. It indicated the need for proceedings to be completed within a stipulated period.
Supreme Court Seeks Replies From 20 Rebel TMC MPs On Abhishek Banerjee’s Disqualification Plea
TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee filed a petition seeking action under the anti-defection law and cancellation of the parliamentary membership of 20 rebel MPs.
- Supreme Court issued notices on 20 Trinamool MPs' disqualification.
- Speaker already issued notices; SC urges expeditious resolution.
- Abhishek Banerjee seeks MPs' disqualification for allegedly joining NCPI.
The Supreme Court has issued notices to 20 Trinamool Congress MPs who allegedly merged with the NCPI, in connection with a petition filed by TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the anti-defection law.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the MPs on Banerjee's plea seeking directions to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to conclude the proceedings expeditiously.
Speaker Has Already Issued Notices: SG
The Lok Sabha Speaker has also been made a party to the petition.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the Lok Sabha, told the bench that notices had already been issued to all 20 MPs on the disqualification petitions filed by the TMC under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
Solicitor General Mehta also submitted that no formal notice should be issued to the Speaker by the court and said he would assist the bench on the Speaker's behalf. The judges accepted the submission.
The bench, however, indicated that the issue was not merely about issuing notices but about completing the proceedings within a stipulated period.
During the hearing, the bench indicated that it was inclined to issue notices to the respondents on Banerjee's writ petition.
Mehta submitted that there was no need to issue a separate notice to the Speaker or his office, saying he would represent the Speaker before the court.
ALSO READ: 'Hijab Not Essential In Islam': Allahabad HC Rejects Plea To Wear Headscarf With School Uniform
What Has Abhishek Banerjee Sought?
In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee has sought action against the 20 MPs under the anti-defection law and cancellation of their membership of Parliament.
His petition seeks a direction to Speaker Om Birla to complete the proceedings expeditiously.
The petition alleges that despite the TMC having approached the Speaker, no action has been taken against the MPs.
The TMC has accused the MPs of abandoning the party and subsequently joining the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). Banerjee has argued that their conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.
The Lok Sabha Speaker and the House Secretary General have been made principal respondents in the petition, while the 20 MPs whose disqualification is sought have also been impleaded.
Questions Raised Over Recognition Of Rebel MPs
Banerjee has also questioned the status of the 20 MPs, arguing that they have neither been formally recognised as a separate group nor are they being treated as one.
He has sought clarity on their recognition as NCPI and questioned how their status is being handled in the Lok Sabha.
According to the petition, if the MPs are to be recognised as a separate NCPI group, a decision should be taken at the earliest. It also questions how their speaking time in the House can be deducted from the time allotted to the TMC if they are not being given a separate identity.
