items.body_text:
Bem-Estar
Qual é o perigo de pesquisar doenças no Google? Entenda quando a prática pode fazer mal
Uma dor que surge de repente, um sintoma fora do comum ou uma palavra desconhecida no resultado de um exame podem ser suficientes para despertar a curiosidade. Nesses casos, o primeiro impulso é buscar respostas na internet. De acordo com o Google, uma em cada […]
Uma dor que surge de repente, um sintoma fora do comum ou uma palavra desconhecida no resultado de um exame podem ser suficientes para despertar a curiosidade. Nesses casos, o primeiro impulso é buscar respostas na internet. De acordo com o Google, uma em cada 20 pesquisas realizadas na plataforma está relacionada à saúde. Embora esse acesso facilite a busca por informações, também pode levar a interpretações equivocadas, já que nem tudo o que está na rede é seguro ou tem respaldo científico.
“Na prática médica, é cada vez mais frequente receber pacientes que chegam ao consultório já com uma hipótese diagnóstica formulada a partir de pesquisas online. Em muitos casos, a busca por informações acaba aumentando a ansiedade. Isso porque sintomas simples podem ser associados, nos mecanismos de busca, a doenças graves, levando o paciente a acreditar que enfrenta um problema muito mais sério do que realmente apresenta”, alerta a médica e coordenadora do CTI do Hospital Badim, Inês Bissoli.
Riscos do autodiagnóstico
Os riscos do autodiagnóstico vão além da preocupação excessiva. “Acreditar em informações incorretas pode levar ao atraso na procura por atendimento médico e, consequentemente, no início do tratamento adequado”, alerta a médica.
Assim, consultar um médico é fundamental para evitar complicações. “Em doenças como câncer, diabetes e hipertensão arterial, por exemplo, o diagnóstico precoce faz toda a diferença para o controle da enfermidade e para a qualidade de vida do paciente. Quando os sintomas são ignorados ou interpretados de forma equivocada, o quadro pode evoluir silenciosamente e provocar complicações graves”, acrescenta Inês Bissoli.
Outro desafio enfrentado pelos profissionais de saúde ocorre quando o paciente chega convencido de um diagnóstico e resiste às orientações médicas. “Em algumas situações, ele pode recusar exames complementares por considerá-los desnecessários ou questionar a prescrição de medicamentos por acreditar que encontrou uma solução melhor na internet. Nesses momentos, o diálogo torna-se fundamental. A relação médico-paciente é construída com base na confiança, e uma conversa franca, capaz de esclarecer dúvidas e explicar as razões de cada conduta, é essencial para garantir um tratamento seguro e eficaz”, garante a coordenadora de CTI do Badim.
Também é comum encontrar pacientes que, após passarem por diferentes especialistas sem obter uma resposta definitiva para seus sintomas, recorrem à internet em busca de explicações. Embora essa atitude seja compreensível, ela não substitui a avaliação clínica. Cada pessoa possui características próprias, histórico de saúde específico e necessidades individuais que somente um profissional capacitado pode analisar de forma completa. Diante de qualquer dúvida, sintoma persistente ou alteração no organismo, a melhor resposta continua sendo a orientação de um médico.
Fontes confiáveis ajudam a separar informação de desinformação
Apesar de exigir cautela, a pesquisa na internet, quando feita com senso crítico e direcionada a fontes confiáveis, pode ser algo útil. “Quando realizada em fontes confiáveis, a busca por informações pode ajudar o paciente a compreender melhor sua condição, participar mais ativamente das decisões sobre o tratamento e chegar à consulta com dúvidas mais objetivas”, opina a médica.
Ela orienta que as informações sejam buscadas em bases de dados e informações confiáveis, como as de instituições de saúde reconhecidas, como a Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz), laboratórios farmacêuticos renomados, centros de pesquisa, escolas médicas e órgãos públicos.

items.summary: Five people were hospitalised after rival transport unions clashed in Ilorin, Kwara State. Learn more about the violence and ongoing dispute. Read More: https://punchng.com/five-hospitalised-as-transport-unions-clash-in-kwara/
items.body_text:
Pandemonium broke out in Ilorin, the Kwara State capital, on Monday as members of rival transport unions clashed, leaving more than five persons injured and hospitalised.
PUNCH Online gathered that the violence, which disrupted activities around the Idi-Araba and Itakudimo areas of the metropolis, was said to have followed an alleged attack on the office of the National Association of Road Transport Owners, as residents and motorists fled the area when the situation escalated.
A resident, Mubaraq Bello, said the disturbance began when some youths arrived in tricycles, armed with cutlasses and other weapons, and moved towards the NARTO office.
“We were at home when we suddenly saw some youths alighting from tricycles with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons before moving towards the NARTO office. Some of them started throwing stones at the building, and that was when the situation became tense”, Bello told our correspondent.
A member of NARTO, Abubakar Olatunbosun, accused members of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, the Road Transport Employers’ Association of Nigeria and the Tricycle Owners and Operators Association of Nigeria of attacking members of his association.
Olatunbosun alleged that the attack occurred as NARTO members were heading to the Kwara State Police Headquarters to seek intervention over the dispute. “We were on our way to the police headquarters when we were attacked by members of the other unions. More than 100 tricycles belonging to our members have also been seized, and we are appealing to the state government to intervene before the situation gets out of hand,” Olatunbosun said.
He added that the association would not resort to self-help, insisting that its members had chosen to pursue redress through lawful means. “We respect the law, and we will not take the law into our own hands. Kwara has always been known as a peaceful state, and we do not want this matter to degenerate further,” he stated.
Two persons injured during the violence, Abdulwasiu Jamiu and Lukman Iyanda, also alleged that their tricycles were forcefully taken from them. Jamiu alleged that several tricycle operators were attacked and injured during the clash. “They attacked us, took away our tricycles and injured some of our members,” Jamiu said.
Iyanda, who was said to have sustained an injury to his hand, alleged that he was attacked while operating his tricycle at Itakudimo. “I was working with my tricycle at Itakudimo when I was attacked. My hand was injured during the incident,” he said.
The clash came amid growing tension over the operation of tricycles and the activities of transport unions in parts of the state.
The Financial Secretary of the Kwara State Tricycle Riders, Abdullahi Abdulraheem, in a video obtained by PUNCH Online, alleged that tricycles operating on major roads in the state were being seized following a directive allegedly issued by the Commissioner for Transportation, Aliyu Korasabi.
Abdulraheem said the alleged development had prevented many riders from carrying out their daily business and earning a living.
“We have chosen to work for our daily bread. We do not want to engage in theft, banditry or any other illegal activity, but we are being deprived of the opportunity to work. The seizure of our tricycles has become a serious problem for our members, whose livelihoods depend on this business,” Abdulraheem said.
He further claimed that a court had previously ruled that tricycle operators should be allowed to operate without harassment or interference. “We have a court order that allows us to operate without disturbance from any agency or authority, and we are calling on the Kwara State Government to intervene before this matter escalates,” he said.

items.title: Investing in women’s health not optional, says FG
items.summary: The Federal Government declares that investing in women’s health is crucial for Nigeria’s $1tn economy. Discover why women’s health is foundational for sus Read More: https://punchng.com/investing-in-womens-health-not-optional-says-fg/
items.body_text:
The Federal Government has said investment in women’s health is critical to achieving Nigeria’s economic ambition of becoming a $1tn economy, declaring that improving the wellbeing of women must be treated as a foundation for sustainable development.
The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, stated this at the maiden edition of the Her Health, Her Power Conference Africa 2026, organised by the VickyHeldan Empowerment Foundation in Abuja.
The conference, themed “Leading with Wellness for a Sustainable Africa,” brought together stakeholders from the health, development, business, media and humanitarian sectors to discuss women’s health, empowerment and leadership.
A statement on Monday by the foundation said the Minister, who was represented by the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women’s Development, Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi, said the country’s economic aspirations could not be achieved without prioritising women’s health.
“If we are serious about a $1 trillion Nigerian economy, then investing in women’s health is not optional. It is foundational,” Suleiman-Ibrahim said.
She said the Federal Government was strengthening policies and institutional structures to promote women’s economic empowerment, gender equality, family development and protection.
The minister also called for stronger collaboration among government, the private sector, civil society organisations, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders to improve outcomes for women.
She commended the founder of the VickyHeldan Empowerment Foundation, Dr Victory Njoku, for creating a platform for stakeholders to generate commitments towards improving women’s health and empowerment.
Suleiman-Ibrahim, however, urged participants to move beyond discussions and translate ideas generated at the conference into measurable action and tangible results.
Former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, also stressed the need to link women’s health with economic development, urging political leaders and policymakers to give greater attention to women’s access to healthcare and education.
“Now, it is key not to separate women’s health from economic growth,” Amaechi said.
He said people appointed to positions of responsibility should understand the relationship between economic growth and the wellbeing of women.
Reflecting on his tenure as Rivers governor, Amaechi said his administration established health centres in every village, with each centre staffed by a medical doctor and two nurses.
He added that the administration also paid N10,000 to women who attended antenatal care.
Amaechi said political decisions had direct consequences for women, urging leaders to transform communities by providing hospitals, health centres and other facilities that could improve the quality of life of women and families.
The convener of the conference, Njoku, said the initiative was established to advance women’s health across Africa by bringing together women, innovators, healthcare practitioners and advocates.
She said the foundation would take the campaign beyond the conference through community-based outreach programmes focusing on maternal health, reproductive healthcare, mental wellness, education and leadership.
“This is just creating a conversation, but taking action, we’re going to propel into communities through our outreach programs, focused on maternal health, reproductive care, mental wellness, education and leadership,” Njoku said.
She expressed the hope that the initiative would expand beyond Nigeria into a broader African platform, while encouraging women to take their rightful place in conversations and decisions concerning their development, health and wellbeing.
Participants included healthcare practitioners, entrepreneurs, public health professionals, advocates, media practitioners and other stakeholders from across the development sector.

items.title: Morning recap: Terrorists exploit dead persons’ accounts, Obi, Amaechi, Duke clash over insecurity, other top stories
items.summary: Stay informed with our morning news recap. Top stories include terrorists exploiting dead persons’ accounts, Obi, Amaechi, and Duke clashing over insecurit Read More: https://punchng.com/morning-recap-terrorists-exploit-dead-persons-accounts-obi-amaechi-duke-clash-over-insecurity-other-top-stories/
items.body_text:
From the NFIU’s disclosure that terrorists are exploiting crowdfunding and accounts linked to deceased persons to move funds, to sharp disagreements among 2027 presidential contenders over insecurity and fuel subsidy, fresh US military training for Nigerian troops, a court battle over the stalled selection of a new Awujale, and protests over Governor Seyi Makinde’s exclusion from the flag-off of the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode road reconstruction, these are the major stories making headlines this morning.
The developments span national security, politics, traditional institutions and infrastructure, with authorities and political actors outlining their positions on issues affecting the country and the 2027 elections.
Here’s your complete morning roundup:
1. Terrorists using dead persons’ accounts, crowdfunding – NFIU
Fresh financial intelligence has revealed that terrorists are using crowdfunding networks, women’s bank accounts and SIM cards registered to deceased persons to raise and move funds for operations in Nigeria. The NFIU said foreign-based facilitators solicit donations through social media under humanitarian or educational claims before transferring the money through multiple channels.
The agency said donors typically contribute between $50 and $500, while the funds are later fragmented and sent through money-transfer operators and remittance apps to Nigerian money mules. “Terrorist facilitators use phone numbers for mobile banking or account alerts that are not registered to the account holder or the true beneficiary,” the report stated.
The NFIU said students, small-business owners and relatives were among those used as money mules, while terrorists also exploited women’s accounts as fronts to conceal the identity of male commanders and logistics managers.
Read More: https://punchng.com/terrorists-using-dead-persons-accounts-crowdfunding-nfiu/
2. 2027: Obi, Amaechi, Duke differ over insecurity, subsidy
Rising political disagreement marked the NBA conference in Port Harcourt as 2027 presidential contenders presented contrasting positions on insecurity, policing, fuel subsidy and economic management. Peter Obi advocated a security overhaul, while Rotimi Amaechi stressed intelligence and economic empowerment.
Obi said insecurity could not be separated from poverty and unemployment. “You need to do a comprehensive overhaul or study of our strategy to a security problem today,” he said. Amaechi, meanwhile, said creating an economy that puts money in Nigerians’ pockets was central to tackling crime.
Donald Duke rejected the existence of fuel subsidy, saying, “You can’t remove what doesn’t exist.” Omoyele Sowore, however, said he would retain subsidy if elected, arguing that poor Nigerians should benefit from it.
Read More: https://punchng.com/2027-obi-amaechi-duke-differ-over-insecurity-subsidy/
3. US steps up military training for Nigerian troops
Strengthened security cooperation between Nigeria and the United States has seen American forces train Nigerian troops in unmanned aircraft systems, combat casualty care, weapons familiarisation and explosive ordnance disposal in Bauchi.
The US Africa Command said the exercises also covered small-unit tactics, camouflage and water treatment. “U.S. and Nigerian forces are conducting a series of training events at Operating Location Bauchi, Nigeria, aimed at sharing military expertise, strengthening partner capacity and building relationships,” it said.
The training was tailored to areas identified by Nigerian counterparts, with unmanned aircraft systems attracting particular interest. Captain Gabriel Feingold said, “We bring them a list of several different training topics, and they select what they think would be most beneficial for them.”

items.body_text:
• CDF Munir holds meetings with Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf and Rezaei
• Iranian leaders stress commitment to Islamabad MoU; say Washington’s approach hindering regional stability, eroding trust in US
• Discussions focused on preventing further escalation, reopening of Hormuz, swift end to conflict, ISPR says
• Oman FM due in Tehran today for next round of talks on Hormuz
ISLAMABAD: The United States must take the first steps towards de-escalation by fulfilling its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Iran conveyed to Pakistan on Monday, as the latter sought to revive the diplomatic process for ending the US-Iran conflict.
The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s meetings in Tehran; with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Gen Mohsen Rezaei, as he sounded out Tehran on the possibility of reviving the June understanding.
“We are committed to implementing the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding. It is the United States that must adhere to its commitments based on the agreement,” Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir, according to an Iranian account of their meeting.
This sentiment was echoed by Gen Rezaei in his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, who was quoted by IRNA as saying: “We distrust America and it must change its behaviour”.
Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported.
According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accompanied the army chief during the one-day visit, which also included meetings with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
“Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the ways to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the disputes,” ISPR said.
The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and sincere efforts towards facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, the statement noted.
The field marshal’s visit comes as the two warring sides have returned to hostilities following the expiry of the 60-day armistice brokered under the Islamabad MoU.
Pakistan has, however, continued to regard the agreement as the available framework for a return to dialogue, while Iran has insisted that Washington must first address what Tehran considers breaches of the understanding.
The visit assumes added significance because Field Marshal Munir spoke by telephone with US President Donald Trump last week, before travelling to Tehran. The contents of that conversation have not been made public, but the contact provided Islamabad with a direct channel to carry the US position to Tehran, while seeking to assess whether Iran was prepared to re-engage.
The army chief’s trip began just before Washington announced a fresh economic pressure campaign against Iran, with sanctions and restrictions on Iranian oil exports likely to form a major part of the new measures.
Tehran has warned that further US pressure would deepen the confrontation rather than create conditions for negotiations.
Ghalibaf described Washington’s approach as “hinder[ing] regional stability and further erod[ing] trust in Washington”.
“Americans know that no one buys their bombast, the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” he said in a post on X after meeting Field Marshal Munir.
The Strait of Hormuz remains central to the impasse. Iran has been insisting that US first fulfil its commitments relating to the waterway, before it considers a wider reopening and a return to the next phase of negotiations.

items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: The ruling PML-N on Monday suffered an embarrassing setback in the National Assembly as the lower house was adjourned within minutes for lack of quorum after its estranged ally, the PPP, stayed away from the proceedings over the alleged rigging in the recently-held Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections.
The government failed to muster the required number of 84 lawmakers in the 336-member house, forcing the chair to adjourn the session without taking up any agenda item when quorum was pointed out by an opposition member from the PTI.
“No PPP, no quorum, simple,” posted PPP’s Sharmila Farooqui on her official social media account on X soon after the adjournment of the sitting.
Later, Ms Farooqui told Dawn PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had already declared the party would “no more cooperate with PML-N on quorum and legislation” in the parliament till their grievances over the alleged rigging and mismanagement in the AJK polls were addressed.
Sharmila says ‘no PPP, no quorum, simple’
Even those party MNAs who were present at the start of the Question Hour left the chamber immediately seeing only 20 to 25 PML-N members on the treasury benches, she said, adding that the PPP had been completing the quorum in the assembly previously.
Ms Farooqui made it clear that the strategy would not change until their concerns over the AJK polls issue were addressed. She, however, did not elaborate any specific demand when asked as to what steps the party wanted the PML-N to take in order to allay their concerns when the election process had already been completed.
When Speaker Ayaz Sadiq earlier announced the opening of the Question Hour, PTI’s Iqbal Afridi pointed out lack of quorum. His action came when the speaker refused him the floor to speak on a point of order.
The speaker ordered a headcount and suspended the proceedings till the completion of the quorum. Some 35 minutes later, Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah was seen in the chair when the house resumed its proceedings. He adjourned the sitting till Tuesday after finding the house still not in order due to lack of quorum.
While the PPP had supported the government in the passage of the two security-related bills last week, Mr Bhutto-Zardari, in the presence of PM Shehbaz Sharif, had objected to the manner with which the government had been doing legislation.
After developing differences with the PML-N over the issue of AJK elections, a PPP delegation headed by Mr Bhutto-Zardari called on opposition leaders and sought their cooperation on the legislation in the parliament and its committees.
Hina Javed’s murder
At the outset of the sitting, the NA speaker expressed his concerns over the brutal murder of Hina Javed in Rawalpindi and referred the matter to the relevant house committee.
Mr Sadiq disclosed that Hina Javed had been posted in the National Assembly by the National IT Board on attachment from December 2019 till June this year after which she returned to her parent department. He said though such matters generally fell under provincial jurisdiction, the case was of particular concern since she had served at the NA.
He said the manner in which Hina Javed was murdered, and the violence against women, were matters of serious concern for everyone.
He appreciated the Women Parliamentary Caucus for taking up the matter and said the NA would provide full support in monitoring the case and extending whatever assistance was required.
Minister for Law and Human Rights Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ministry was in constant contact with the Rawalpindi police regarding the murder investigations. Two suspects were on three-day physical remand, he said, expressing the confidence that the culprits would be brought to justice.
Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.body_text:
A rescue team resumed its trek at Spantik on Tuesday to recover the body of Pakistani mountaineer Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died while descending the 7,027m peak in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Shigar district.
The 34-year-old died at an altitude of around 6,250 metres on Aug 20, while descending from the mountain also known as Golden Peak, after suffering from high-altitude sickness. Her body remains at Camp 3.
Efforts to retrieve her body were earlier disrupted due to severe weather.
Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn on Monday that weather conditions were expected to improve on Tuesday, after which rescuers would make another attempt to bring Mushtaq’s body down to the base camp.
Subsequently, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar posted on X that the rescue team had resumed its operation after weather conditions improved.
“The rescue team has once again departed from the base camp and is now heading towards Camp 2. The team is moving carefully and will continue the operation as conditions permit. We pray for their safety and success,” he said.
Shigri had told Dawn that Pakistan Army helicopters were expected to airlift Mushtaq’s body to Skardu after its arrival at the base camp.
During her ascent, Mushtaq had successfully reached the 7,027-metre summit of Spantik and was in good health at the time, ACP said in statements issued on Thursday.
However, she developed a serious high-altitude medical emergency at an elevation of about 6,400 metres (21,000 feet) during the descent.
High-altitude sickness encompasses a range of pulmonary and cerebral conditions caused by hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, due to rapid ascent and inadequate acclimatisation to high altitudes.
Her mountain guide, Akbar Ali, and expedition guide, Muhammad Amin, immediately came to her assistance.
“Despite the immediate and dedicated efforts of her mountain guides, who provided every possible assistance under extremely challenging conditions, she could not survive,” Karrar Haidri, a senior vice president for ACP, said in a condolence statement.
Shigri said Mushtaq was part of a five-member Pakistani women’s expedition team that summited Spantik, which included climbers Zoni Aslam, Zaba Shigri, Shama and Sohana.

items.summary: Angel Reese breaks WNBA single-game, season rebounding records: full story insideAngel Reese, the Atlanta Dream’s superstar, has shattered another record in Monday night's win against host the Los Angeles Sparks.Reese breaks the WNBA single-game record, posting 26 rebounds...
items.body_text:
Published August 25, 2026
Angel Reese, the Atlanta Dream’s superstar, has shattered another record in Monday night's win against host the Los Angeles Sparks.
Reese breaks the WNBA single-game record, posting 26 rebounds in the Dream’s 78-71 triumph on Monday night, August 24.
The feat came as Reese moved past the WNBA’s single-season mark in the same contest.
Reese, while speaking in a postgame interview, said, “Last time I was here, I didn’t miss any shots. Tonight, I couldn’t hit—so I knew I was going be able to get them on the rebounding side.”
Reese, determined and focused with eyes on the target, added, “I just want to be consistent for my team. " Offensively, defensively, whatever it takes to win,” the determined Reese added.
On Monday, Reese posted her WNBA-leading 27th double-double with a basket that gave her her 11 points with 13.9 seconds left.
Reese’s record-breaking rebounding night on Monday happened just two days after she posted a career-high 31 points in Atlanta’s win at Phoenix on Saturday, August 22.
Reese shattered Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, registered on May 23, 2023, while playing for the Washington Mystics.
Reese, in the current season run, has so far scored 458 rebounds in 37 appearances, surpassing A’ja Wilson’s mark by seven rebounds, which was set in 2024 in 38 games.
A three-time WNBA All-Star, Reese previously posted a single-game career high in rebounding of 22, set in her first-year pro in 2024 with the Chicago Sky.
Atlanta’s win capped a perfect 4-0 sweep of the West Coast, who now sit at 25-13 as they head toward the playoffs.

North West is clearly in her experimental era — but even the 13-year-old has discovered there’s one style boundary her parents aren’t willing to cross.
In a new interview with Dazed, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West’s daughter opened up about her love of piercings and revealed the one she desperately wants but isn’t allowed to have.

Bandages in the same spots had previously sparked speculation that she had gotten the piercings.

Her ever-changing look has included blue hair, cheek studs, finger piercings, a hand dermal piercing and even a temporary blacked-out grill.
“Why is my teeth black? Are we okay?” she joked during a livestream in January before confirming the look was temporary. “I could take them out.”
Kardashian has previously defended her daughter’s fearless approach to fashion, describing North as confident and mature.
“She’s really mature in one sense where she’ll be like, ‘Mom, I saw this, and I don’t really care that they don’t like... my blue hair or this or that,’ ” Kardashian said.

North may have plenty of freedom to experiment, but apparently the bridge of her nose remains strictly under parental lockdown.

items.title: Alonso makes winning start with Chelsea as Rogers scores on debut
items.summary: Alonso makes winning start with Chelsea as Rogers scores on debut
items.body_text:
Alonso makes winning start with Chelsea as Rogers scores on debut
- By AFP -
- Aug 25, 2026
Xabi Alonso won his first game as Chelsea boss thanks to Morgan Rogers’s debut goal and Joao Pedro’s strike after just 31 seconds of a pulsating 3-2 victory against Fulham on Monday.
Alonso has been hired to revive Chelsea after their dismal 10th place finish in the Premier League last season.
The former Real Madrid boss has a point to prove after being sacked by the Spanish club following less than eight months in charge.
Alonso’s side ensured he delivered a good first impression in a chaotic west London derby at Craven Cottage.
Pedro’s opener inside the first minute was followed by a blunder from Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez that gifted an equaliser to Josh King.
Rogers put Chelsea back in front on his debut after becoming the most expensive British player in history following his £117 million ($159 million) move from Aston Villa in the close-season.
Cole Palmer increased Chelsea’s advantage after half-time and the Blues survived a frantic finale after Gonzalo Garcia bagged Fulham’s second goal following another Sanchez mistake.
On an evening when old friends were reunited on the touchline and on the pitch, Alonso emerged victorious against new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa.
The pals played together for seven years with Real Madrid and Liverpool and also starred for Spain.
Ironically, Arbeloa was promoted from Real Madrid B to replace Alonso when he was axed at the Bernabeu in January.
Rogers is also close friends with Palmer and the pair gelled immediately to lead a dynamic attacking display from Chelsea.
Rogers was deployed on the left of Chelsea’s three-man attack, with Palmer on the right and Pedro in the central role.
Palmer endured a difficult last campaign that saw him left out of England’s World Cup squad and he played as if he was determined to make amends.
Keeping Rogers and Palmer fit and firing could be the key to Chelsea climbing back into contention for Champions League qualification this season.
‘Ice-cold’ Rogers
Alonso’s reign got off to a stunning start when Levi Colwill’s header reached Palmer and he flicked a deft pass into the path of Pedro, who timed his run perfectly and clipped a composed finish past Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno.
But Sanchez is under pressure after some shaky performances last term and the error-prone Spaniard was at fault when Fulham drew level in the 23rd minute.
King’s strike was close enough for Sanchez to save but he allowed the ball to squirm into the net.
While Chelsea were often left exposed at the back by Alonso’s bold 3-4-3 formation, they attacked with poise and purpose.
Romeo Lavia’s effort was superbly saved by Leno before Rogers restored the visitors’ lead in the 41st minute.
It was a brilliant move, started by Palmer’s clever turn and pass to debutant defender Maxence Lacroix, whose unexpected burst forward produced a low cross that reached Rogers for a clinical finish from 10 yards.
Rogers celebrated with the ‘ice-cold’ gesture that Palmer popularised after borrowing it from his former Manchester City youth team colleague.
Not to be out-done by his mate, Palmer bagged Chelsea’s third goal four minutes after half-time.
Pedro did well in the build-up, holding the ball long enough for Palmer to burst into the Fulham area and plant a low shot past Leno from a tight angle.
Fulham reduced the deficit in the 54th minute thanks to another howler by Sanchez.
Timothy Castagne’s shot was weakly pushed out by the keeper and Garcia pounced to head in the rebound on his debut after signing from Real Madrid.
Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez came off the bench to deafening boos from Fulham fans after his provocative role in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final win over England.
King nearly levelled for Fulham with a long-range rocket that fizzed just wide before Antonee Robinson’s lob over Sanchez drifted narrowly wide.

- By Hassan Hafeez -

LAHORE: The Punjab government on Tuesday decided to restore sports activities in educational institutions across the province, announcing mega sports events to be held in all schools from October to December, ARY News reported.
Punjab Education Minister Rana Sikandar Hayat presided over a meeting today.
The Minister stated that the mega events will be held at the tehsil, district, division, and provincial levels.
Rana Sikandar Hayat announced that the Lahore Board will host the final event in December of this year.
He also announced an increase in reward money for the games, fixing it at Rs. 100,000, Rs. 300,000, and Rs. 500,000.
The Minister added that winning players will be provided with opportunities to compete at both national and international levels.
“No compromise will be made on the standard of the sports kits,” he stated.
He further informed that sports committees have been established in all 35,000 schools across the province.
Additionally, the Minister noted that as many as 450 schools have already been provided with sports equipment.

items.body_text:
Maryam Nawaz heads to China for four-day official visit to strengthen Punjab-Xinjiang ties
				
				
					
Maryam Nawaz Set for Key Talks With Xinjiang Party Chief Chen Xiaojiang
				
		
				 
				
					
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif left for China on Tuesday, Aug.24, for a four-day official visit aimed at strengthening ties between Punjab and China’s Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, with high-level meetings and talks planned during her stay.
Chinese Consul General Sun Yang was at the airport to see Maryam off before her departure. The visit is expected to provide an opportunity for both sides to discuss areas of mutual interest and explore ways to deepen cooperation.
Upon reaching Urumqi International Airport, Maryam will be received by senior Chinese officials. She will then begin her official engagements at Kunlun Hall in the conference center at the Xinjiang State Guest House.
During the visit, Maryam Nawaz is scheduled to meet a high-level delegation led by Chen Xiaojiang, secretary of the Communist Party of China’s Xinjiang Committee.
The Punjab chief minister will also meet He Zhongyou, deputy secretary of the Communist Party of China’s Xinjiang Committee. Maryam is also scheduled to meet a delegation from the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (XPCC).
Senior Xinjiang officials will host a formal dinner in honor of Maryam and the Punjab delegation during the visit. The chief minister will stay at the Xinjiang State Guest House as a state guest throughout her four-day official trip.
The visit comes as Pakistan and China continue efforts to expand cooperation between their regions and institutions. Punjab, Pakistan’s most populous province, has maintained close ties with Chinese partners through development, infrastructure and economic cooperation projects.
Maryam’s visit is expected to further strengthen these ties and create opportunities for broader cooperation between Punjab and Xinjiang.

items.body_text:
Health Minister Mustafa Kamal urges national strategy to tackle growing malnutrition and stunting crisis
				
				
					
Pakistan loses around 11,000 mothers to childbirth each year, while malnutrition leaves 43% of children stunted.
				
		
				 
				
					
ISLAMABAD: Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal has called for a coordinated national strategy to fight malnutrition and reduce child stunting in Pakistan, warning that the country cannot achieve its health goals without addressing poor nutrition among mothers and children.
Kamal made the remarks during a meeting with Adviser to the Federal Minister for Finance Adnan Pasha in Islamabad. Pasha briefed the health minister on a new initiative focused on improving nutrition and reducing stunting across the country.
Kamal stressed that maternal and child health is closely connected to proper nutrition. He called for nutrition programs to be prioritized and urged officials to develop practical measures to tackle the issue.
The minister said about 11,000 mothers die each year in Pakistan during childbirth, while 43% of children suffer from stunting linked to malnutrition.
Poor nutrition during pregnancy and childhood can affect physical growth and overall development, making early intervention important for long-term health.
“Proper maternal nutrition is the foundation of a healthy child, while healthy children are the foundation of a healthy and strong society,” Kamal said.
He directed officials to prepare clear and practical recommendations to address malnutrition and reduce the country’s stunting rate. He also called for a coordinated approach involving relevant government departments and institutions.
The meeting also focused on developing a strategy that could translate government plans into concrete action. Officials were asked to work together on recommendations aimed at improving nutrition and supporting healthier outcomes for families.

items.body_text:
WASHINGTON: The Trump administration on Monday proposed making permanent a more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, a move that would dramatically increase costs for a program widely used in technology, education and research sectors, even as courts have blocked the fee from being collected.
The proposed regulation from the Department of Homeland Security, published in the Federal Register, would codify a $103,265 fee that President Donald Trump first imposed temporarily last year. That temporary increase expires in September, one year after it was issued. The new rule could be finalized by the end of the year.
A federal judge ruled in June that the temporary fee was illegal and blocked the administration from enforcing it. That decision is now under review by a Boston-based appeals court, while a separate court considers whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee from a major business group.
The H-1B program allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers with specialized training and offers 65,000 visas annually, plus an additional 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees. Visas are approved for three to six years. Before Trump’s order, fees for those visas typically ranged from $2,000 to $5,000.
The new fee would not apply to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, nor to renewals of current visas.
Trump and other critics of the H-1B program argue that companies abuse the system by replacing American workers with cheaper foreign labor. But business groups and many individual companies contend the visa program is essential to fill gaps in qualified American workers for certain jobs and to recruit top global talent.
The U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers are challenging the fee. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the proposed rule once it is finalized, officials said.
In a separate action Monday, the State Department said it planned to revoke the non-immigrant visas of foreigners who have applied for or are seeking asylum in the United States.
A State Department spokesman said the agency is coordinating with the Department of Homeland Security “to identify and revoke the non-immigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently.”
The statement did not specify how many visas would be revoked. However, The Associated Press, citing State Department documents and two U.S. officials, reported that the administration plans to revoke up to 200,000 business and tourism visas, a move that, if carried out, would mark the largest single mass visa revocation in U.S. history.
The AP reported that the State Department will revoke so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought or are currently seeking asylum. B1 and B2 visas are non-immigrant visas issued for business and tourism travel.

items.title: German GDP growth revised upwards, defying Iran war turmoil
items.summary: German growth rose faster than previously estimated in the second quarter thanks to strong exports, official data showed Tuesday, as Europe's biggest economy defied the turmoil... The post German GDP growth revised upwards, defying Iran war turmoil appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
German GDP growth revised upwards, defying Iran war turmoil
Frankfurt – German growth rose faster than previously estimated in the second quarter thanks to strong exports, official data showed Tuesday, as Europe’s biggest economy defied the turmoil unleashed by the Iran war.
Gross domestic product grew 0.3 percent from April to June compared with the first three months of the year, according to revised data from the statistics office Destatis.
A first estimate in July had put growth at 0.2 percent.
“The German economy is maintaining the growth momentum seen at the start of the year”, said Destatis’s chief Ruth Brand, adding that “growth was primarily driven by the positive development of exports”.
The economy expanded 0.4 percent in the first quarter.
The revision to second-quarter growth is another sign that the eurozone’s manufacturing powerhouse may be weathering the energy shock unleashed by the United States and Israel’s war against Iran better than feared.
Factory output and exports have also been ticking up in recent months despite the fallout from the conflict.
The revised GDP data showed that exports rose two percent in the second quarter from the first, while imports were also up substantially.
Investment fell slightly, dragged down by a hefty fall in the field of machinery and equipment. Spending by both households and governments registered a small increase.
The German economy has stagnated for several years due to high energy costs, growing competition from China and US President Donald Trump’s tariffs.
Hopes had been high at the start of the year that it would stage a strong rebound thanks to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s spending blitz on defence and infrastructure.
The outbreak of the Middle East war has dimmed those expectations after the hit to energy-intensive manufacturers, with the government now expecting growth of just 0.5 for 2026 as a whole.

items.title: Hyundai reaches tentative deal with workers after strike
items.summary: South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor and the union representing its workers have reached a tentative deal on wages and bonuses, both sides said on Tuesday... The post Hyundai reaches tentative deal with workers after strike appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Hyundai reaches tentative deal with workers after strike
Seoul – South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor and the union representing its workers have reached a tentative deal on wages and bonuses, both sides said on Tuesday after a rare full-day strike.
Around 40,000 employees of a roughly 73,000-strong domestic workforce at the country’s largest carmaker walked off the job on Friday, according to union figures, in the first such action for a decade.
The union said on Monday that it had returned to talks with the company and had postponed shorter strikes planned for this week.
Hyundai said on Tuesday that the two sides had struck a “tentative agreement”, while the union indicated that the firm had agreed to partly meet its demands.
“We agreed to increase the basic monthly salary by 100,000 won ($72) and pay a bonus equivalent to four months’ salary,” the union told AFP in a statement.
The company would also meet another demand to raise the retirement age once the government passes legislation on a nationwide hike from 60 years to 65.
Hyundai will not apply the wage peak system, which gradually reduces the salaries of older workers in their final years, after the retirement age is extended, the union said.
Union members will vote on the proposals on August 31.
“We acknowledge the commitment of our employees and appreciate the efforts of our negotiating teams in reaching this tentative agreement,” a Hyundai spokesman told AFP.
He also said both parties recognised that advanced technologies such as “physical AI and robotics are essential part” of the future of mobility.
The company’s workers have staged a total of 60 hours of strikes this year, causing estimated losses of around $1.6 billion, according to calculations by local news agency Newsis.
Hyundai posted record second-quarter revenue of 49.2 trillion won, although operating profit fell 20.8 percent year-on-year amid weaker sales.

items.summary: Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier... The post Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
Paris – Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.
– Only a few transits per day –
Before Iran blocked the strait in response to joint US-Israeli strikes in February, around one fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas exports passed through the waterway.
Iran’s Guards have also warned of a “danger zone” covering 1,400 square kilometres where mines may be present.
After Iran closed the strait on March 1, commodity carrier traffic plummeted to an average of 10 transits per day, compared with a daily average of 95 in February, according to an AFP analysis of data from maritime tracker Kpler.
An agreement signed by the United States and Iran in June led to a temporary rebound to 36 transits per day, before they dropped back to an average of 15 between the resumption of hostilities on July 8 and August 22.
– New routes, ‘dark’ transits –
Before the war, vessels crossed the strait freely via a route through the centre of the waterway adopted by the International Maritime Organization (IMO).
There are now two distinct routes: one to the north, near the Iranian coast — the only one approved by Tehran — and another to the south, between the Omani coast and potentially mined areas.
During the relatively calm period between June 17 and July 7, an average of nine ships per day used the Iranian route and eight the Omani one. The rest transited via unidentified routes or the traditional IMO corridor.
Ever since the ceasefire collapsed on July 8, two-thirds of transits have become “dark”, or unknown, compared with less than one percent before the war, according to Kpler.
These transits involve vessels whose exact route cannot be confirmed due to insufficient data stemming from disabled transponders, jammed signals or missing satellite imagery.
– Thousands of sailors stranded –
Some 6,000 sailors and 500 ships have remained stuck in the Gulf since the beginning of the conflict, the IMO told AFP.
The organisation said there were “ongoing discussions” to ensure a secure maritime route, adding that their outcome “depends on de-escalation in the region”.
The IMO had begun an initiative in June to evacuate more than 11,000 seafarers stuck in the Gulf, but the effort was soon suspended following an attack on a vessel.
Over the past six months, at least 20 sailors and dockworkers have been killed in incidents or attacks in the region, according to the IMO.

items.body_text:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Monday that the Trump administration is not ruling out the use of military force against Iran, even after Washington announced a “decisive economic attack” on Tehran.
“We are not ruling out, under any circumstances, the use of military strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or throughout Iran,” Hegseth told reporters, adding that Tehran cannot withstand the economic pressure being imposed on it.
The US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on nearly 60 entities, individuals, and vessels linked to Iran in the nuclear energy, missile, cyber, and oil sectors.
The Treasury Department targeted five sectors for potential secondary sanctions: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping.
It also suspended general licenses that had allowed certain financial transactions to Iran.
The US Treasury Secretary said, “President Trump is in telephone conversations with world leaders to sever economic ties with Iran. Each country has a specific timeline for halting the activities we have identified, and if these countries do not take action, we will take unilateral measures through the Treasury Department’s authorities.”

items.body_text:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) expects temperatures to continue rising until the end of this week.
The country is experiencing a new heat wave, with temperatures peaking from Tuesday until Thursday.
Temperatures in Cairo are expected to range between 37C and 38C.
The EMA warned that high humidity levels will contribute to a two-degree increase in perceived temperature, making it feel closer to 40C, especially during peak hours.
The weather will be very hot and humid during the day across most of the country, and hot and humid along the northern coast.
At night, the weather will be slightly hot and humid across most of the country.
High humidity levels are expected overnight, reaching approximately 80 to 85 percent in Cairo and the Lower Egypt, and 90 to 95 percent along the northern coast, exacerbating the perceived temperature.
Humidity levels will decrease relatively during the daytime.
The EMA advised citizens to follow daily weather updates and take necessary precautions to deal the weather, especially while driving during fog.
Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

items.title: Quiet on set. How AI transformed China’s microdrama scene
items.summary: Hengdian, China — Everything seemed to be business as usual as filming got underway on a dimly lit set in a basement in Hengdian, a town nicknamed “China’s Hollywood” for its sprawling complex of film studios. Cameramen raced around hectically setting up lights and checking shots as choreographers ran through fight sequences and a prop team … The post Quiet on set. How AI transformed China’s microdrama scene appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Everything seemed to be business as usual as filming got underway on a dimly lit set in a basement in Hengdian, a town nicknamed “China’s Hollywood” for its sprawling complex of film studios.
Cameramen raced around hectically setting up lights and checking shots as choreographers ran through fight sequences and a prop team worked out how to hoist a net that would later restrain a hostage.
Actors, most dressed as assassins and hitmen, milled about or squatted, smoking cigarettes and getting occasional touch-ups from roving hair stylists and make-up artists as they waited for their scene to start.
But behind the bustle was a new reality: while just a few months ago, production of these so-called “microdramas” was flourishing in Hengdian and other hubs – today, these sets are falling quiet.
Seemingly overnight, new AI-video generation tools have taken over the microdrama industry, able to produce these popular, vertical shows at a fraction of the cost, decimating the number of live-action productions across the country and flooding platforms with AI-made content. More than 120,000 microdramas were released in the first three months of this year — with 95 percent of those generated by AI, according to Chinese state media.
That’s made the industry one of the most visible examples of how China’s breakneck AI transformation is impacting people’s livelihoods — wiping out jobs and creating new ones, leaving everyone unsure what’s next. It’s the kind of technological disruption that many creatives fear could upend movie-making far beyond China.
Between takes actor Junlin, who asked to be identified by her stage name, talks about how she’s struggling to stay afloat as a “bitter winter” has arrived for productions like hers.
“With fewer productions hiring, your space for survival is constantly squeezed,” said the 24-year-old, dressed in combat boots and a high ponytail to play a head assassin who storms around with a posse of hitmen in an upcoming microdrama.
She’d worked only seven days in June, a sharp fall from the spring when she’d been filming 25 out of about 30 days per month in Hengdian and other cities. “I’m someone who gets anxious easily,” she said. “If I’m not on set, I would be in a constant state of anxiety.”
Boom time
Hengdian, a town of just over 200,000 tucked in a rural part of eastern China’s Zhejiang province, had been booming with the rise of the microdrama industry in recent years.
Broken into roughly 90-second episodes, microdramas first emerged during the pandemic, capitalizing on the popularity of short video apps like Douyin and Kuaishou as cinemas and studios closed.
While each episode is designed to be quick to consume on a mobile phone, together the clips weave together plotlines that can stretch the length of a feature film.
These microdramas — and their often soapy or outlandish plots about wicked mother-in-laws, mistaken identities, wartime heroics and wronged lovers — have since proliferated in China and spread to audiences overseas, where they’ve spawned a fast-growing, multi-billion-dollar industry.
They’ve also caught the attention of China’s censors, who are tightening oversight of microdramas with new rules set to take effect in September. Plotlines, for example, will need to “adhere to correct political direction.”
Last year, the domestic microdrama industry was valued at nearly $15 billion, according to market research firm DataEye, almost double the market size for box-office feature films in the country. Its rise ushered in a welcome heyday for young creatives at a time of high youth unemployment in China.
“Once microdramas took off, there was a nonstop stream of roles I could take on as long as I wanted to film,” said Bi Zhiqiang, 27, another actor living in Hengdian, who quickly built a career after moving there in 2021 as the industry was taking shape.
“Many people who didn’t even study acting or film and television joined because there were more and more opportunities.”
The lure drew thousands

In an Armed Forces Day speech on August 14, Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan offered temporary immunity to participants in the intra-Sudanese dialogue his government is now rushing to launch, including a suspension of criminal proceedings against those facing charges while they take part.
The move is largely aimed at clearing the legal obstacle facing leaders of the opposition Sumud coalition, the civilian coalition led by former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok that was formed on the back of a factional split in the the Civil Front for Democracy, a previous anti-war civilian front. The charges stem from that earlier coalition over what the military saw as proximity to the Rapid Support Forces.
But the legal cases are only one obstacle. Civilian forces want the dialogue to follow a halt in fighting, input on how its preparatory arrangements are made and to know whether whatever comes out of the process will bind state institutions. The military is showing no sign of halting its campaign, while Burhan’s central role in building the dialogue and his apparent ambitions for it do little to settle questions about its independence.
Moreover, Khartoum cannot entirely escape the regional and international tracks it is trying to outpace. An African Union diplomat told Mada Masr that any internal dialogue would ultimately need to connect with those tracks and gain acceptance from them.
Khartoum may have seen an opening for some African cover. Just hours after Burhan’s speech, a delegation from the African Union’s Peace and Security Council arrived in Port Sudan before travelling to Khartoum for its first field visit to the capital since the outbreak of the war.
Sudan has been trying to repair its relationship with the AU since 2021, when the bloc suspended its membership after the military and Rapid Support Forces jointly ousted the civilian wing of the government. Now, with state institutions back in Khartoum, a civilian government appointed last year and a domestic dialogue being hurried toward a September launch, authorities are looking for the AU’s renewed attention to translate into a role in the political process and the restoration of Sudan’s membership.
But the visit is not quite the diplomatic endorsement Khartoum might want. Another AU diplomat told Mada Masr that the union is still assessing, speaking to multiple sides and gathering information. There is a lot the bloc needs to know, the diplomat said, and the AU is not prepared to give any political process a “blank check.”
Monday was a busy day for what a Sudanese political source described as Khartoum’s effort to “rearrange its foreign relations during the war and beyond.”

Turkey’s existing defense relationship with Sudan and its experience in areas where the military needs help make it one of the easier partnerships for Khartoum to deepen, one of the military sources said.

items.title: Why prescribe drugs by brand name? Pharmacists call for change after child endangered by drug dispensing error
items.summary: The problem is the widespread use of commercial, rather than generic drug names, sources say The post Why prescribe drugs by brand name? Pharmacists call for change after child endangered by drug dispensing error first appeared on Mada Masr.
items.body_text:
Why prescribe drugs by brand name? Pharmacists call for change after child endangered by drug dispensing error                    
                Last week, seven-year-old Mecca came down with a cold and a sore throat. She visited her doctor for examination, and was prescribed a nutritional supplement to help with the symptoms. Her family sent a photo of the prescription to a pharmacy in Zahraa al-Maadi for home delivery, and the drug was delivered around 11:30 pm.
After ingesting a 6-ml dose of the drug, however, Mecca “suffered something akin to paralysis,” her mother, Samia, tells Mada Masr.
“My daughter was suffering from a simple cold,” says Samia. “But the pharmacist confused the last two letters [of the drug’s name] and dispensed an epilepsy medication instead.”
Samia rushed her daughter to the Poison Control Center, which refused to admit Mecca, as did several hospitals afterward, with all of them telling the mother that, since it had been 24 hours since the medication was administered, she needed to go to the intensive care unit at Demerdash Hospital, where the specialized care unit is located.
Mecca remained sick for a day and a half, “no longer able to move her hands, legs or eyes,” Samia says. She remained in this condition for four days before eventually recovering.
Soon after the life-threatening incident, the family filed a lawsuit against the pharmacy and submitted complaints to the Egyptian Drug Authority — the body responsible for pharmacy inspections — as well as to the Pharmacists Syndicate and the public prosecutor.
But professionals working in the pharmacy sector and syndicate officials who spoke to Mada Masr say Mecca’s case is not the first time a patient has faced dangerous consequences as a result of mistakes in interpreting prescriptions.
For them, complaints and investigations into each individual incident — while important for establishing liability and holding the responsible party accountable — will fail to address the root cause of the problem or prevent its recurrence, leaving patients exposed to the same danger.
They believe the true solution lies in changing prescribing practices: mandating that physicians prescribe medications by their generic, non-proprietary names to reduce the likelihood that pharmacists will confuse the commercial names of popular drugs, a demand that pharmacists have put to the Health Ministry in recent days and which has already been recommended in a 2024 prime ministerial directive.
However, doctors have expressed unwillingness to adhere to the recommendation — a stance that several sources who spoke to Mada Masr attribute to the strong financial and professional incentives offered by pharmaceutical companies to doctors, part of marketing arrangements that generate billions in revenue.
***
Mistakes in drug dispensation of the kind that endangered Samia’s daughter are easily made when doctors prescribe drugs by their commercial name, according to two pharmacists who spoke to Mada Masr.
A Pharmacists Syndicate official, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Mecca would not have been endangered had the generic name been used. The confusion originated due to a confusion between the name of the prescribed drug and a different drug with a similar name, he says.
“The active ingredient in the first medication, Acetylcysteine, is completely different from the one in the second medication, Risperidone, which is used to treat certain psychiatric and neurological disorders,” he explains.
A pharmacy manager notes that by contrast the trade name for the prescribed drug, Respidep, is very similar to Risperdal, the brand name of the antipsychotic that was dispensed.
“Similar incidents have occurred many times,” says the pharmacy manager. “One case that stands out in my memory involved a pharmacist who mistakenly dispensed a neurological medication: the difference between the name written on the prescription and the drug actually dispensed was just two letters.”
A

items.title: As US funding cut for AU mission looms, Somalia faces reckoning it isn’t ready for
items.summary: What could the future of security in Somalia look? The post As US funding cut for AU mission looms, Somalia faces reckoning it isn’t ready for first appeared on Mada Masr.
items.body_text:
As US funding cut for AU mission looms, Somalia faces reckoning it isn’t ready for                    
                In 2023, Somalia’s government launched its most ambitious military campaign in years against Al-Shabab, a Somali armed group linked to Al-Qaeda. Somali troops and allied clan fighters pushed the group’s fighters out of large parts of central Somalia, and officials in Mogadishu, the capital, spoke confidently of finishing the group off within a year or two.
By the spring of 2025, almost all of that ground was gone. Al-Shabab, moving carefully rather than charging back in, retook town after town during an offensive timed to the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, restoring a map of control that looked much like it had before the government’s push began.
The reversal captures a dynamic that has defined this war for two decades. While Somali forces can clear territory of Al-Shabab, holding it is another matter — one heavily dependent on a multinational African Union peacekeeping force that now risks losing the funding that keeps it in the field.
In early July, a leaked internal diplomatic note showed that the United States plans to block United Nations funding for the agency that supplies, caters for and moves the force around the country. Somali and regional officials, apparently caught off guard, have spent the weeks since scrambling for a way to keep the mission afloat.
Somalia’s importance goes well beyond its own fight with Al-Shabab. The country hugs the coast of the Horn of Africa, along the southern edge of one of the world’s busiest shipping corridors, connecting the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. General Dagvin Anderson, the top American general overseeing US military operations in Africa, has described Somalia as sitting on “key terrain” for exactly this reason, adding that the location alone “makes it important.”
An Al-Shabab that controls Somalia’s coastline, as far as regional actors are concerned, threatens not just Somalia’s neighbours but potentially the security of those waterways. This is a large part of why so many outside powers have poured money and troops into propping up Somalia’s government over the past two decades, and why the funding crisis facing the African Union mission is not simply a Somali problem for them.
…
Washington has been remarkably direct about this calculation in the past, particularly when the stakes were high. In May 2009, as Somalia’s internationally-backed transitional government came close to being overrun by an earlier Al-Shabab attack, the US ambassador to Kenya sent a diplomatic cable to then-Secretary of State Hillary Clinton saying the government’s collapse would be “a major setback for US interests,” and that an Al-Shabab takeover, or a slide back into the lawlessness of Somalia’s earlier warlord years, would be treated as a threat to the US.
Clinton immediately released emergency funds to the government and pushed the United Nations for a waiver to its arms embargo so more weapons could reach it.
The US has its own concerns about the prospect of the Somali government collapsing and has been willing to take steps to prevent it. Part of that effort has involved an intense drone campaign targeting Al-Shabab and, more recently, Islamic State-Somalia. The US also has troops stationed in the country, including an expanded security presence along the Gulf of Aden and in Jubaland, along Somalia’s border with Kenya, where it operates a large base, a Somali defense official says.
Other countries have also built significant relationships with Somalia’s federal government and its member states, giving them their own stakes in preventing an Al-Shabab takeover. While these interests vary, from security and military access to trade, infrastructure and regional influence, they mean that Somalia’s survival matters well beyond Washington. items.title: US prepares ‘largest financial attack ever’ as Trump claims Iran is collapsing
items.summary: The United States is preparing to launch “the largest financial attack ever mounted against an adversary,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, as President Donald Trump declared that Iran is “collapsing” hours before Washington announces a major sanctions package. Writing in the Financial Times ahead of a press conference scheduled for Monday to outline the […] The post US prepares ‘largest financial attack ever’ as Trump claims Iran is collapsing first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
The United States is preparing to launch “the largest financial attack ever mounted against an adversary,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, as President Donald Trump declared that Iran is “collapsing” hours before Washington announces a major sanctions package.
Writing in the Financial Times ahead of a press conference scheduled for Monday to outline the new economic measures, Bessent stated that the conflict with Tehran has reached a “final phase” that will begin with an “economic landing.” Invoking the 1943 Tehran conference where Allied leaders mapped out the military campaign that led to the Normandy landings in the Second World War, Bessent said Trump and American military force have largely dismantled Iran’s military capabilities and weakened its nuclear programme, leaving the administration ready to exert maximum economic pressure.
The impending measures have already driven the Iranian currency to historic lows, with exchange rate monitoring websites reporting that the rial fell past an unprecedented 2 million to the US dollar amid threats of a financial blockade. A source familiar with US Treasury plans told Reuters that Washington is expected to expand the scope of secondary sanctions to target foreign entities and countries maintaining commercial ties with Tehran as part of the escalated pressure campaign.
Bessent characterised the Iranian government as a malign force for 47 years that has driven a potentially strong economy into decline, repressed its population, and maintained a network of regional proxies to spread terrorism. He said Trump has brought the Iranian economy to a point of historic weakness marked by severe inflation and currency degradation, leaving Tehran reliant on foreign nations that mistakenly believe accommodating aggression will secure lasting peace.
While acknowledging that the United States has paid a heavy price in countering Tehran and often stands alone in demonstrating the resolve to end the threat rather than manage it, Bessent affirmed that Washington will press forward with full determination.
As the United States escalates its economic offensive, global powers and neighbouring countries are engaging in parallel diplomatic efforts. In Beijing, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for a “diplomatic” solution to the Middle East crisis during talks with Jordan’s King Abdullah.
Xi emphasised that the sovereignty and security of regional countries, including Jordan, must be respected, according to a Chinese foreign ministry statement. Highlighting Jordan’s “unique and important role in the region,” Xi reiterated that China has always advocated for a comprehensive ceasefire and resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means. The Jordanian monarch, whose US-allied kingdom has been caught in the middle of Washington’s months-long war with Tehran, has been on an official visit to China since August 18, marking his ninth trip to the country since taking the throne in 1999.
Meanwhile, diplomatic engagements continued in Tehran, where Pakistani Army Chief Asim Munir arrived on Monday for talks with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni. Munir was accompanied on the visit by Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

As a member of the Ministerial Group for Entrepreneurship, MSMEDA is committed to contributing to the implementation of the Startup Charter and providing practical mechanisms to support entrepreneurs throughout different stages of their development.
Under the terms of the memorandum, MSMEDA will implement initiatives aimed at providing startups with technical and institutional assistance to help them improve efficiency and strengthen competitiveness. Cooperation will include specialised training programmes to develop the skills of business owners, as well as access to financing and technical services designed to help startups refine their business models and enhance managerial, technical, and marketing capabilities to ensure sustainability and growth.
The partnership represents an important step towards coordinating efforts among organisations working in entrepreneurship, building a more effective ecosystem to help startups expand within the Egyptian market and enter new international markets, Hassan added.
Ghoneima noted that Startup Egypt was established to serve as a key connector linking entrepreneurs with public and private sources of support. Egyptian Aladdin Farouk, Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, received a high-level delegation from China’s Institute for the Control of Agrochemicals (ICAMA), the government authority responsible for the regulation, registration and oversight of pesticides in China. The delegation was headed by Huang Xiujie, Director of ICAMA, and included Yang Mao, Director of the General Office, as well as representatives of a number of Chinese and Egyptian companies.
The attendees included Adel Abdel Azim, Chairman of the Agricultural Research Centre; Hala Abo Youssef, Head of the Agricultural Pesticides Committee; Saad Moussa, Vice Chairman of the Centre; Mohamed Abdullah Saleh, Secretary-General of the Pesticides Committee; and a number of ministry officials and senior manufacturers and representatives of private-sector pesticide companies.
The visit falls within the efforts to strengthen scientific, technical and technological cooperation between ICAMA and the Ministry’s Agricultural Pesticides Committee, and to consolidate the strategic partnership between Egypt and China in the management, registration and monitoring of agricultural pesticides.
During the meeting, the Agriculture Minister said that the partnership with China is a key pillar of the Ministry’s strategy to develop the agricultural sector. He stressed the Egyptian state’s efforts to create a favourable investment climate and provide all necessary facilities to attract and empower investment, with a focus on areas related to the agricultural sector, including pesticides and agricultural inputs.
Farouk added that Egypt attaches great importance to strengthening the role of the private sector, promoting local manufacturing and encouraging joint investment. He noted that transferring and localising modern technologies in cooperation with Chinese expertise would help build a national industrial base for producing high-quality pesticides in line with international standards, thereby supporting self-sufficiency and reducing the import bill.
He also explained that investing in human capital and training young people is top priority for the the Ministry. The cooperation will include specialised training programmes and the transfer of modern knowledge to young engineers and researchers to enhance pesticide monitoring and integrated pest management systems in line with the latest international practices, he said.
The Agriculture Minister also praised the efforts of the Agricultural Pesticides Committee. He stressedthat the Ministry will continue to open up new avenues for technical and industrial integration and cooperation with China. Such efforts will support sustainable agricultural development plans and strengthen food security, he noted.
During the meeting, Hala Abo Youssef, Head of the Agricultural Pesticides Committee, presented a draft memorandum of understanding between Egypt’s Agricultural Pesticides Committee and China’s ICAMA, paving the way for the necessary procedures for its signing. items.title: Life Sentence Closes Chapter on Ahmad Hassoun: Former Assad Mufti Behind Bars
items.summary: Hassoun was one of the most prominent religious figures defending Bashar al-Assad during the war, using his official position to endorse military operations, al-Hal writes. The post Life Sentence Closes Chapter on Ahmad Hassoun: Former Assad Mufti Behind Bars first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
The Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus on Monday sentenced former Grand Mufti Ahmad Badr al-Din Hassoun to life imprisonment, ordering the confiscation of all his movable and immovable assets. The ruling followed a six-session trial examining charges of inciting violence, justifying killing, and providing religious cover for the former regime’s policies.
The government framed the verdict as a landmark moment in Syria’s transitional justice process. Human rights organizations, however, raised concerns about transparency and fair-trial guarantees.
Life Sentence and Asset Seizure
Hassoun, who served as Grand Mufti from 2005 to 2021, received a presence-based life sentence, according to the official Syrian news agency (SANA). His property was ordered seized for the benefit of the public treasury.
SANA reported that the court convicted Hassoun of crimes against humanity and war crimes, in addition to charges of inciting violence, justifying murder, and exploiting his religious authority. The case examined his ties to security and military leaders and pro-regime militias, as well as his speeches delivered to regime troops and officers.
Hassoun was one of the most prominent religious figures defending Bashar al-Assad during the war, using his official position to endorse military operations. According to the Associated Press, the charges included inciting violence, justifying murder, and supporting the use of barrel bombs against civilian areas—stances that fueled controversy over his role in legitimizing state violence.
Sentence Reduced from Capital Punishment
The trial began on June 25 and unfolded over six sessions, during which the court reviewed the indictment, witness testimony, documents, and video evidence. At one point, the defense requested a technical review of the video material to verify its integrity—a request the court granted.
Independent reporting noted that the sessions explored Hassoun’s connections with security chiefs, military commanders, and loyalist militias, as well as evidence that he weaponized religious authority to reinforce regime power. In the penultimate session, the prosecution requested the death penalty. The court ultimately opted for a life sentence and asset confiscation.
The case is notable because it does not target a military official accused of issuing orders or carrying out killings, but rather a high-profile religious figure accused of using the pulpit, rhetoric, and symbolic authority to incite violence and rationalize atrocities.
A Test for Transitional Justice Amid Rights Concerns
The proceedings were not free of criticism. Human Rights Watch described the initial trials of former regime figures as a crucial test for Syria’s justice system. The organization noted the limited public information available about procedural details, despite allowing brief attendance for select media and civil society representatives.
Human Rights Watch urged authorities to publish written rulings, clarify the legal basis and evidence behind convictions, and ensure fair-trial standards. Genuine justice, the organization stressed, requires transparent procedures and an independent judiciary capable of holding perpetrators of grave international crimes accountable.
Hassoun’s sentencing therefore carries significance beyond the individual case. It serves as an early indicator of how Syria’s new authorities intend to handle transitional justice—balancing public demands for accountability with concerns that trials must not fall short of legal guarantees or transparency. That balance will be tested further as additional cases move toward the courts.

items.title: A Deal on Paper, Dead on Arrival: What Syria and Israel Actually Agreed To
