items.title: MS-13 gang members say they buried 200 people in Bukele’s political cradle
items.summary: An indictment by Salvadoran prosecutors reveals the discovery of more than 20 clandestine graves in Nuevo Cuscatlán, the town the president once held up as a model of public safety during his time as mayor
items.body_text:
MS-13 gang members say they buried 200 people in Bukele’s political cradle
An indictment by Salvadoran prosecutors reveals the discovery of more than 20 clandestine graves in Nuevo Cuscatlán, the town the president once held up as a model of public safety during his time as mayor
Three members of the Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) gang, testifying under a cooperation agreement with Salvadoran prosecutors, admitted during the mass trial of 486 alleged leaders of the criminal organization that between 2013 and 2021 they tortured, murdered and buried more than 200 people at Finca Suiza. The wooded area, located in the municipality of Nuevo Cuscatlán, occupies a unique place in El Salvador’s political history: it was there that Nayib Bukele’s political career began in 2012 and where part of the movement that would later carry him to the presidency took shape.
The site may contain the largest known clandestine cemetery in El Salvador. On that very land, where authorities themselves say 21 bodies and an undetermined number of skeletal remains have already been found, a luxury housing development has been under construction for several years.
Although the government itself classified all trials and judicial proceedings conducted under the state of exception, authorities turned the mass trial of the alleged gang leaders into a media event, allowing access to several news outlets and social media influencers. Other hearings involving people accused of collaborating with the gang, among whom human rights organizations say there could be thousands of innocent individuals, continue to be held behind closed doors.
EL PAÍS obtained a copy of the prosecution’s indictment, which includes the full testimony of three witnesses identified by the code names Bosnia, Berlin and Sweden. All three have been identified as members of MS-13, specifically of the Teclas Locos Salvatruchos clique, or cell, which operated in the northern part of the San Salvador metropolitan area, including the municipality of Nuevo Cuscatlán.
In their confessions, key witnesses Berlin and Bosnia say that, in mid-2012, during the so-called truce between the gangs and the government of then-president Mauricio Funes, the MS-13 leadership, known as the Ranfla Nacional, agreed to bury the bodies of their victims in order to keep murder statistics artificially low. According to their testimony, gang members dubbed the practice “Cultivated Homicide,” or “H1,” a reference to a type of fertilizer.
At the time, Nuevo Cuscatlán was little known on El Salvador’s political stage and had relatively low levels of crime. But because of its heavily wooded terrain, the gang chose it as a dumping ground for victims from neighboring municipalities across the San Salvador metropolitan area. “The leaders faced the problem that the gang’s backlog of unsolved homicides was growing nationwide, and they could not leave bodies in the streets. So they decided the best way to maintain control was to hide the corpses,” Berlin and Bosnia said in their statements.
After Bukele became mayor in May 2012, Nuevo Cuscatlán began to gain prominence on El Salvador’s political map. Projecting a fresh and youthful image, the then-rising politician used the small municipality to boost his national profile and presented it as a model for the rest of the country. During his tenure, Bukele highlighted the low, or even nonexistent, homicide rate and attributed it to his policies for preventing and combating violence.
In reality, Nuevo Cuscatlán was, and remains, a small municipality covering just six square miles and inhabited by a relatively affluent population. Historically, this placed it well below the national average for violence, with only one or two homicides a year on average. Bukele, however, frequently touted the fact that he had kept the homicide rate at zero for more than two years.

items.title: New phishing scam alert: Fake email from iDeal-WeroNL doing the rounds
items.summary: The Fraud Helpdesk issued a warning to the Dutch public about a fake email from iDEAL-WeroNL.
items.body_text:
New phishing scam alert: Fake email from iDeal-WeroNL doing the rounds
The Fraud Helpdesk issued a warning to the Dutch public about a fake email from iDEAL-WeroNL. The helpdesk has received reports from many people who received fake emails stating that they need to receive a refund and must verify their identity.
The email states that people must complete the verification, with a link to do so, this week and will receive their money back no later than the next business day. The email is fake and not from iDEAL-WeroNL. The Fraud Helpdesk advises recipients to delete it.
iDEAL was rebranded as iDEAL | Wero this year, as part of a gradual transition to Wero, the European digital wallet. The fake email states that the online payment system recently checked its transaction records in preparation for this transition. “During this extensive check, we determined that there is still an outstanding refund from Worldplay B.V. for you,” the fake message reads.
iDEAL reports that multiple phishing campaigns are currently active, in which fraudsters impersonate iDEAL or act as part of the transition. "iDEAL never asks you via email to confirm personal data, start a verification, or activate software," the organization stressed.
The company advises people not to click on links and attachments in these types of emails, not to share any data, and to report the email to the bank.
Reporting by ANP

items.title: Dutch kids get their first smartphone at age 10 on average
items.summary: Children in the Netherlands are getting their first smartphones at increasingly young ages.
items.body_text:
Dutch kids get their first smartphone at age 10 on average
Children in the Netherlands are getting their first smartphones at increasingly young ages. Age 10 is the current average, according to a survey commissioned by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. The government launched a new campaign to encourage parents to talk to their children about what they may experience online and what to do when they see something scary.
The Ministry surveyed children aged 10 to 15. Half said that they sometimes see posts or messages that make them scared or sad, most often on Snapchat and TikTok. At the same time, most children don’t talk to their parents about the unpleasant things they encounter, sometimes due to shame or because they worry their parents would get mad at them.
“Smartphones and social media offer children many opportunities, but they also entail risks, such as online bullying, addiction, and viewing shocking images,” said State Secretary Willemijn Aerdts of Digital Economy. “Platforms are responsible for making their services safer, and I hold them accountable for this. At the same time, I want to help parents guide their children effectively by talking to them at a young age and being involved in their online lives.”
Hence the Blijf in Beeld campaign, aimed at parents who are about to give their child their first smartphone. The campaign provides tips and information about how to talk to their child about smartphone use and what they might experience online. It also includes an agreement card that parents and children can fill out together with agreements on how and when the smartphone is used and what to do when the child encounters something that makes them sad or scared.
“By starting these conversations early, it is easier to make agreements together and to continue the dialogue at a later age,” the Ministry said. In the survey, 89.4 percent of surveyed children said they understand why such agreements are important, and half said they appreciate the agreements.

items.title: Long lines at Schiphol; Security holding short strikes for better working conditions
items.summary: Long lines are expected at security checks at Schiphol Airport today.
items.body_text:
Long lines at Schiphol; Security holding short strikes for better working conditions
Long lines are expected at security checks at Schiphol Airport today. Security staff will hold three short strikes throughout the day. They are protesting for better working conditions following the airport’s reorganization of its security department.
“As a result of industrial action by security staff, travellers at Schiphol may experience longer waiting times than usual at security,” Schiphol warned on its website. “This can have an impact on the flow of travellers. We are doing our best, together with the parties involved, to keep any disruption to a minimum.”
The labor action was organized by trade unions CNV and FNV. Today, Tuesday, security workers will hold three 15-minute-long strikes at 10:00 a.m., 2:00 p.m., and 7:00 p.m. On Wednesday, there will be five strikes, at the same times as today, plus noon and 4:00 p.m. The strikes will take place in areas where travelers are checked, staff entrances, in the baggage handling area, and outside the airport.
“In concrete terms, this means, for example, that passengers will have to wait longer at security checks,” CNV negotiator André Quint told RTL Nieuws. Security workers aren’t asking for much, according to the unions. They want “normal breaks,” better schedules, and sufficient recovery time, among other things.
Security workers are under massive work pressure since the reorganization, and that is causing rising absenteeism. “They experience the consequences of choices made at Schiphol every day. We have given Schiphol ample opportunity to come up with concrete solutions. Insufficient ones have materialized. That is why we are now increasing the pressure,” Quint said.
He stressed that no one strikes for fun. “But if talks do not lead to concrete improvements, we must take the next step. With the work stoppages, we want to send a clear signal.”

items.title: Health inspectors ban webshop from selling weight loss drugs
items.summary: Health inspectors have banned a website from selling unlicensed weight loss drugs that it advertised on social media. De Peptidekoning...
items.body_text:
Health inspectors ban webshop from selling weight loss drugs
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Health inspectors have banned a website from selling unlicensed weight loss drugs that it advertised on social media.
De Peptidekoning sold two medicines prescribed to treat diabetes, semaglutide and tirzepatide, and a third, retatrutide, which is an experimental drug that has not been licensed in any country.
The Health and Youth Care Inspectorate (IGJ) ordered the owners of the website to stop selling all three substances and warned patients not to risk their health with experimental treatments.
It said De Peptidekoning, which trades through several websites including puritybase.com, did not have a license to sell the medicines. “They have not adequately ensured that the medicines meet standards for quality, safety and effectiveness,” the IGJ said.
“The way in which the medicines were offered for sale does not give enough reassurances, which creates risks for public health.”
RTL Nieuws reported that unauthorised traders were profiting from a black market in slimming treatments for people who were not prescribed medicines such as Ozempic, which are only available in the Netherlands to treat diabetes.
Marloes Dankers, of the Utrecht-based Dutch Institute for the Rational Use of Medicine, an advisory body set up by doctors and pharmacists, said: “People are making guinea-pigs of themselves.
“These medicines are still being researched and we don’t know what exactly the risks are. That’s the reason for doing the research.”
Eli Lilly, the American manufacturer developing retratrutide, also urged people not to buy the drug online.
“What is being sold on the black market is not a medicine, it has not been approved or verified in any way and it is not worth the risk,” the company said.

items.body_text:
Both Dutch teams reach hockey World Cup semi-finals
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The Dutch men’s hockey team moved into the semi-finals of the World Cup in Amstelveen on Monday evening with a 2-2 draw against England in what was a tense and physical game.
The Dutch needed at least a draw to be sure of progressing to the next round, while England were chasing a win by a two-goal margin.
Playing in bright sunlight in a packed Wagener Stadium, England opened the scoring after five minutes, with the Dutch equalising with just 40 seconds remaining before the end of the first half.
England went into the lead again 90 seconds into the second half but the Netherlands drew level once more. England took off their goalkeeper with seven minutes to go, but despite piling on the pressure, the Dutch kept them at bay, much to the delight of the largely orange-clad crowd.
The 2-2 draw was enough to put the Netherlands at the top of their group, with Argentina, who beat India 5-3, in second place. The Netherlands will now meet Spain in the semi-finals in Amstelveen on Friday, while Argentina will play Germany in Belgium, which is co-hosting the tournament.
In the women’s competition, the Netherlands are hot favourites and will meet Belgium in the first semi-final on Thursday at the Wagener Stadium. They beat China 4-1 on Sunday to reach the next stage. Argentina will play Spain in Belgium.

items.title: NS offers cheaper tickets to ease busy morning trains
items.summary: NS is making some rush-hour train tickets cheaper from Tuesday, in an effort to ease its busiest morning services and...
items.body_text:
NS offers cheaper tickets to ease busy morning trains
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
NS is making some rush-hour train tickets cheaper from Tuesday, in an effort to ease its busiest morning services and free up seats.
The national rail operator is extending its PrijsTijd Deals – advance-purchase tickets that give a discount for travelling on quieter trains – to the edges of the morning peak. Discounts there will average around 30%, against up to 60% in the quietest off-peak hours. The tickets must be bought at least a day ahead.
The move is separate from the €49 summer pass for unlimited off-peak travel, which runs until September 1. It is also exactly the same as an earlier NS plan to add a surcharge to peak fares, which MPs blocked in 2023.
NS says the crush is worst on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, when large numbers of passengers travel within a single hour. Nudging even a fraction of them onto a train 15 or 30 minutes earlier or later, it argues, spreads the load and means more people get a seat.
“The NS, like electricity grid operators for example, has to deal with peak load,” said NS timetabling director Tijmen Voet. “But if a small percentage of travellers choose a less busy alternative, passengers have to stand far less often.”
Limited reach
 Rail passengers’ association Rover welcomed the extension but said more was needed to make a real difference. It has long argued the discounts should also be bookable on the day of travel, rather than only up to a day ahead.
The reach is likely to stay limited, a Rover spokesperson said, because many hyper-peak travellers hold season tickets paid for by their employer and feel no price incentive. Others cannot shift their journey because of fixed school or work hours.
An NS trial last year found a fifth of passengers would take a quieter train in return for a discount, with most willing to wait up to half an hour. That, Voet said, lets the operator run fewer long trains for peak crowds that otherwise travel largely empty for the rest of the day.

items.title: Poland’s Mesko signs €1.9bn deal to supply Piorun air-defence systems to four NATO countries
items.summary: It is the largest ever order for Pioruns, which have been in demand since proving their worth in Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Polish state defence firm Mesko has signed an 8 billion zloty (€1.9 billion) agreement to supply its Piorun man-portable air-defence systems to the armed forces of Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia. The deal is being financed through the European Union’s SAFE mechanism.
The agreement represents the largest-ever purchase of Pioruns, which have become an export hit for Mesko after proving their worth during Ukraine’s defence against Russian aggression. Previous buyers include Sweden, the United States, Belgium, Estonia and Norway itself.

— Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) August 24, 2026
The deal will see the firm provide “several hundred” launchers and “several thousand” missiles for its shoulder-fired Piorun systems, which target low-flying aircraft such as planes, helicopters and drones. Over 80% will be supplied to Poland’s armed forces, with the remainder going to its three NATO allies.
The purchase is being funded through SAFE, which provides loans at preferential terms for defence spending. While SAFE can be used individually by countries to make purchases for their own armed forces, some funds are designated for joint procurement by groups of countries (including non-EU member Norway).
“Our partners from Lithuania, Latvia and Norway have decided to purchase from Poland,” declared deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who oversees Poland’s participation in SAFE.
“We are a leader in the SAFE mechanism and are the first to create such agreements. For the first time, the [Polish defence ministry’s] Armaments Agency is making purchases not only for the Polish armed forces, but also for those of our allies.”
“This is a measure of the success of the Polish arms industry,” declared defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, as the deal was announced on Monday. “This is the moment when Poland can proudly say: we are a European leader.”
He noted that Mesko’s production capacity is now 2.5 times larger than it was when the current government took power in December 2023. Since SAFE launched in May, the firm’s staffing has increased by around 200.
Poland is by far the largest recipient of SAFE funds, with around €44 billion. The government says that SAFE will not only bolster Poland’s defence capabilities but also provide a boost to the domestic defence industry, where around 90% of the funds will be spent.

All registry offices in Poland can now recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other European Union countries, after a government regulation issued in May went into force. The decision came in response to a ruling by the Court of Justice of the EU (CJEU) requiring Poland to recognise such unions.
Deputy prime minister Krzysztof Gawkowski expressed his “great joy, because finally in Poland we have a law that gives the right to dignity”. The government’s plenipotentiary for equality, Katarzyna Kotula, warned local authorities that they will be breaking the law if they refuse to comply with the new rules.
However, the mayor of one town in a conservative region has already declared that his administration will not recognise such marriages. He argues that doing so would violate Poland’s constitution, which mentions marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

Nowe wzory aktów małżeństwa umożliwią transkrypcję zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych z pełnym szacunkiem dla par. To koniec administracyjnej fikcji i niepewności, z którą przez lata… pic.twitter.com/mRZYkEg9W4
— Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 22, 2026
Polish domestic law still does not allow any form of same-sex unions to be formed. However, last year, the CJEU ordered that the country recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other EU member states. That was followed by a similar ruling from Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA).
One obstacle to implementing those decisions was that, previously, Poland’s civil registry only allowed male-female marriages to be entered. But, under a regulation issued by the government in May, the system now allows either mixed-sex or same-sex marriages.
Even before that went into force on Sunday, some Polish cities, starting with Warsaw and Wrocław, had already begun transcribing same-sex marriages conducted abroad into their registries. They simply listed one spouse in the “man” section and the other as a “woman”, even though that was not accurate for one of them.
But some local authorities have refused to do so, pointing to article 18 of Poland’s constitution, which states that: “Marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, as well as the family, motherhood and parenthood, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland.”
Such doubts were cited by the mayor of Zakopane, a town in southern Poland, last week when he announced that his administration did not intend to begin recognising foreign same-sex marriages after the regulation came into force.
“We will not be issuing such transcriptions in Zakopane,” said Łukasz Filipowski, quoted by local news service Nasze Miasto. He argued that doing so would “not be in accordance with the constitution”, adding that, while Zakopane is “tolerant”, it “promotes the traditional family model…[as] our foundation”.
Filipowski pointed to a ruling in July by the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which found that the government’s regulation conflicts with the constitution’s definition of marriage. However, the government considers the TK to be improperly constituted and therefore regards its rulings as invalid.

items.title: Ukraine to establish new national pantheon as Poland warns against honouring massacre figures
items.summary: President Zelensky reiterated that "only Ukrainians will decide who is a hero to us".
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
President Volodymyr Zelensky has signed a law establishing a new national pantheon to commemorate Ukrainian historical heroes. While it is not yet known which figures will be honoured there, Poland has expressed concern that they will include nationalist leaders associated with massacres of Poles in World War Two.
On Sunday, a Polish deputy foreign minister warned that Kyiv “will have a huge problem” integrating with the European Union if it celebrates such individuals. But Zelensky reiterated that “only Ukrainians will decide who is a hero to us”.
The establishment of the pantheon has taken place against the backdrop of a diplomatic crisis triggered in May by Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”.
Parts of the UPA were responsible for the so-called Volhynia massacres during World War Two, in which Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, as part of an ethnic cleansing operation.
Poland regards the episode as a genocide, though Ukraine strongly rejects that label. Many Ukrainians hold the UPA in high regard for the role that it played in fighting for independence from Moscow-backed Soviet rule.
Poland condemned Zelensky’s decision and stripped him of the country’s highest honour, the Order of the White Eagle. In response, the Ukrainian president announced in late June that he would seek to create a new national pantheon, because “no one will dictate which heroes we should honour”.
A bill creating the pantheon was subsequently approved by the Ukrainian parliament in July, and, on Saturday, Zelensky signed it into law, just ahead of today’s celebrations of Ukrainian independence day.
“A Ukrainian pantheon will definitely be established, and only Ukrainians will decide for themselves who our heroes are,” declared Zelensky at a meeting with military veterans on Saturday. “All our true heroes…who fought for Ukraine, for our independence…deserve due honour.”
However, the introduction of the law only now begins the process of building the pantheon itself – where the remains of those chosen as national heroes will be reburied – and the establishment of an advisory body that will decide which figures should receive such an honour.
It therefore remains unknown for now who will be included in the pantheon. However, on Sunday, Polish deputy foreign minister Marcin Bosacki warned against honouring figures associated with the Volhynia massacres.
“Every nation and its government has the right to choose the heroes they deem appropriate,” emphasised Bosacki in an interview with broadcaster TVP.
“However, if individuals responsible for mass crimes against civilians, such as [Stepan] Bandera or [Roman] Shukhevych, are included in Ukraine’s national pantheon, it would significantly worsen Ukraine’s relations not only with Poland but with Europe in general,” he added.
Bandera was the leader of a faction of the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN-B), which in turn founded the UPA. Shukhevych was a military leader of the UPA. Both figures continue to be honoured in Ukraine, often prompting protests from Poland.

items.title: Planned Amazon Warehouse in Czechia Faces Local Resistance, Again
items.summary: Locals in South Bohemia fear private developers are trying to strong-arm them into hosting a massive new warehouse of US retail and tech giant Amazon.
items.body_text:
“Some people call me naïve, but I believe we have to fight for the areas we live in,” says Eva Horakova in a phone interview with BIRN.
A microbiologist at the Czech Academy of Sciences, Horakova has lived in Borsov nad Vltavou, a small town of about 2,000 inhabitants just south-west of Ceske Budejovice, in southern Bohemia, for more than 15 years.
When she started noticing factual discrepancies and contradictory statements over what private developers were planning for one of her city’s logistics and industrial parks, she felt she had to do something about it and went on to found the Hlas Borsova (“Voice of Borsov”) citizens’ initiative with other neighbours and locals.
According to Horakova, who is also running as the Christian Democratic KDU-CSL party's lead in the upcoming October municipal elections: “Many people here are scared. They think that if we don’t accept Amazon, we’ll end up in a worse situation.”
Amazon eyes Czech expansion
Last year, US online retail giant Amazon celebrated 10 years of presence in the Czech Republic since the opening of its first logistics centre in Dobroviz, just west of Prague’s International Airport. This project was followed in 2023 by the launch of a robotics logistics centre in Kojetin, in the region of Moravia. Amazon also has a corporate office in the Czech capital and claims it has invested 45 billion Czech crowns (around 1.7 billion euros) in the country over the past decade.
“We are proud that Amazon is helping not only the business grown in the Czech Republic, but also the communities in which it operates,” Slawomir Plonka, Amazon’s regional director for Central and Eastern Europe, said at the time of the 10-year anniversary.
It hasn’t, however, all been plain sailing. In Dobroviz, local opposition to the arrival of Bezos’s 95,000-square-metre mega-warehouse sparked significant media and political attention, delaying its opening by several months and forcing Amazon to miss out on the 2014 Christmas season.
The construction finally went ahead after the developer Panattoni Europe signed two separate cooperation agreements with both the municipality and a local civic association, binding them to an annual contribution of 1 million crowns and to invest in several local infrastructure upgrades, like the modernisation of the municipal wastewater treatment plant, noise barriers and the construction of a bypass.
Meanwhile, Amazon was forced to withdraw plans to open its second distribution centre in Brno, Czechia’s second-largest city, after local opposition and repeated delays.
Eva Horakova fears that what happened in Dobroviz more than ten years ago, when Amazon managed to override local grievances and concerns about the warehouse’s local impact, is about to repeat itself in Borsov nad Vltavou.
“The pressure is insane. Developers are doing their maximum to have it signed before the October local elections,” she tells BIRN.
August deadline
Now being developed by investors Accolade and Garbe, the land of the Borsov Economic Development Zone I was purchased in 1998, with initial zoning plans banking on the construction of a large shopping centre.
This never materialised, and in 2020 developers received zoning approval for the construction of four smaller, separate industrial halls – two of which already have building permits – for a total built area of over 148,000 square metres. Now, the modalities have changed again.
Accolade and Garbe redesigned the entire project into a single, larger building (77,000 square metres in size, about 500 metres long and 15 metres high) specifically for a single tenant – Amazon – on an expected 20-year-lease agreement. About 2,500 people could be employed there, working on a two-shift rotation running almost non-stop from 06:30 to 04:30.

items.title: Across the Balkans, Foreign-Backed Luxury Developments Cause Local Anger
items.summary: Albanian protesters’ campaign to halt a Trump-connected luxury development echoes discontent across the Balkans about outside investors’ mega-projects - with increasingly vocal demands for more public input and transparency.
items.body_text:
Since Albania’s ‘Flamingo Revolution’ protests began in May, they have attracted worldwide attention and sparked debate within and outside the Balkans about high-profile investors’ mega-projects.
The protests began in response to the proposed luxury tourism projects on Albania’s Sazan Island and the Zvernec protected coastline. The 1.4 and 4.7 billion euro investments are being led by Affinity Partners, an investment firm run by Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Kushner and his wife Ivanka Trump first visited Albania in 2021 and announced plans for the development in 2024.
There has been much to anger locals about the projects, including comments Ivanka Trump made on a podcast where she referred to “discovering” Sazan Island and called the state-owned land a “private island”.
Another more substantive issue is that the Albanian government amended the laws on protected areas on February 22, 2024, allowing five-star hotels to be built inside protected areas. This occurred a month before Kushner’s Albanian projects were announced.

items.title: As Turkey Makes Peace, Kurdish Villagers Who Fled Conflict Contemplate Return
items.summary: As the Turkish authorities take steps to end the four-decade-long conflict with the Kurdish militant group PKK, people who fled their villages are revisiting their abandoned homes – but rebuilding normal life there will be a major challenge.
items.body_text:
“It was the biggest breaking point in my life,” said Aydin Kurdis, remembering the day he and his family left their village 32 years ago.
In the early 1990s, the village of Golord, known officially as Bostancik, was home to around 200 families. Its stone houses sat among hills covered with walnut and fruit trees. Villagers made a living raising livestock, while the orchards provided much of what families needed.
“Before we left the village, I didn't know what pain was. I didn't know what poverty was,” Kurdis said, sitting in front of the house where he was born and eating cucumbers just pulled from the garden down the slope on an August afternoon. “Life was hard on us after we moved to the city.”
Kurdis, 52, lives in Yuksekova, the largest district in Turkey’s southeastern Hakkari province, near the Iranian border. Golord is only a 45-minute drive away, but the final 10 kilometres are unpaved, with potholes dotting the dusty mountain road.

items.title: Air Force Pilot to Undergo Surgery After Injury During Ejection with Catapult
items.summary: The pilot of the SAAB Gripen jet that crashed near Szolnok (central-eastern Hungary) suffered a spinal injury during the ejection and will undergo surgery, the Central Hospital of Northern Pest–Military Hospital told MTI on Monday. “The fighter jet pilot is doing well.” Medical examinations showed that he suffered a spinal injury during the ejection and […] The post Air Force Pilot to Undergo Surgery After Injury During Ejection with Catapult appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The pilot ejected safely and is hospitalized in stable condition as authorities investigate the cause of the crash. Continue reading
The pilot of the SAAB Gripen jet that crashed near Szolnok (central-eastern Hungary) suffered a spinal injury during the ejection and will undergo surgery, the Central Hospital of Northern Pest–Military Hospital told MTI on Monday.
“The fighter jet pilot is doing well.” Medical examinations showed that he suffered a spinal injury during the ejection and therefore requires surgery, which is scheduled to be performed on Tuesday by specialists at the Military Hospital, they said.
The minor spinal surgery is most likely to ensure the full recovery of the Gripen pilot who was involved in the accident,”
said György Székely, a neurosurgeon at the hospital. The doctor stated that the pilot was admitted to the hospital in “very good condition.”
He noted that from a medical standpoint, ejection is dangerous because the launch involves high acceleration, which places extreme strain on the body; the spine is particularly vulnerable to injury in such situations.
As Hungary Today reported, an Air Force Saab Gripen fighter jet belonging to the Hungarian Defense Forces crashed near Szolnok for unknown reasons and the pilot successfully ejected. The Gripen crashed while fully loaded with combat equipment, including missiles and ammunition, as well as a full auxiliary fuel tank. Based on some reports, the Gripen fighter jets were returning in formation to the base in Kecskemét (central Hungary) following an alert.
An expert who spoke to Magyar Nemzet ruled out the possibility of pilot error based on the initial information. As he said, it could have been a technical malfunction, or the plane may have struck a bird. He emphasized, however, that the investigation will determine the exact cause.
Via MTI, Magyar Nemzet; Featured photo: Honvedelem.hu (Illustration)
items.normalised_title: air force pilot to undergo surgery after injury during ejection with catapult

items.title: Teachers’ Union Threatens With Strikes After Bold Pre-election Salary Promises Not Met
items.summary: In previous years some teachers have aligned themselves with the strongly politicized, anti-Orbán radical movement “Tanítanék” Despite a very significant salary increase for teachers in February this year, most education professionals are believed to have voted for Péter Magyar’s TISZA party in April, who have actively campaigned with the promise of higher salaries and more […] The post Teachers’ Union Threatens With Strikes After Bold Pre-election Salary Promises Not Met appeared first on Hunga
items.body_text:
Three civil society organizations are set to advise TISZA officials in selecting the new leadership. Continue reading
Despite a very significant salary increase for teachers in February this year, most education professionals are believed to have voted for Péter Magyar’s TISZA party in April, who have actively campaigned with the promise of higher salaries and more autonomy for schools. Similarly to other segments of public service workers, such as police officers, they are now chasing the election campaign promises with growing frustration.
January of this year marked the fifth wage increase since 2020 in vocational training, which means that during the Orbán government teachers’ salaries have increased two and a half times on average compared to 2020. As many as 24,000 teachers were affected by the latest 10% rise. The starting salary for teachers is currently around 775,000 forints gross per month (around 2,000 euros; 1 euro = 380 forints), with most earning 890,000 forints gross, while those who have been teaching for longer can earn up to 1 million forints gross.
Yet today another conflict looms in public education after it was revealed that the wages of educational support staff lag drastically behind those of teachers.
The government has acknowledged the validity of the issue but stated that there is no money to address it,
reported vadhajtasok.hu.
A work stoppage could occur in Hungarian schools if the government does not take action soon to raise the wages of colleagues who directly support education and instruction, warned Tamás Totyik, president of the Teachers’ Union (PSZ), on Inforádió. The salaries of staff members employed in non-teaching roles who perform support and administrative tasks are typically aligned with the minimum wage or the guaranteed minimum wage, differing from it by only 7 percent. This situation creates enormous wage disparities within institutions, as teachers’ wages have recently reached a “relatively acceptable level,” while the wages of the support staff who assist them lag far behind.
These workers play a key role in the day-to-day operation of schools, and often perform work that is extremely demanding both physically and mentally. Totyik illustrated the heavy workload in Hungary using an example from Finland: while in Finland there is one teaching assistant for every three children, in Hungary a single assistant may be responsible for as many as 250 children.
Although the education authorities acknowledged the situation during negotiations,
and the government’s program had previously called for a 25 percent pay raise for them, they informed the union at the most recent meeting that there is simply no funding for this measure in the current budget.
The newly created Ministry of Education is currently lead by Judit Lannert, a pro-LGBTQ sympathiser, who has not been able to present any tangible plans for a comprehensive reform of Hungary’s education system.
The union leader also assessed the status of the right to strike. He explained that while teachers have regained some of their rights, they still cannot fully exercise the right to strike.
Via Vadhajtasok; Featured Image: Facebook Tanítanék Mozgalom

items.title: Let the Looting Begin: Far Left Soros NGOs to Nominate Members of Controversial “Asset Recovery Office”
items.summary: George Soros, chair of Soros Fund Management LLC It may soon become clear who will take the helm of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH), which has been dubbed the “new Stasi” in reference to the notorious East German secret police. Three well-known organizations will assist TISZA officials in making a decision, […] The post Let the Looting Begin: Far Left Soros NGOs to Nominate Members of Controversial “Asset Recovery Office” appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The new Foreign Minister faces criticism over crisis management, diplomatic reshuffles, and a growing focus on image over tangible results.Continue reading
It may soon become clear who will take the helm of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH), which has been dubbed the “new Stasi” in reference to the notorious East German secret police. Three well-known organizations will assist TISZA officials in making a decision, Magyar Nemzet reported.
The chair of the Parliament’s Justice Committee, István Hantosi (TISZA) shared the schedule on Sunday, noting that the selection process will reach its most critical phase this week after the applications received for the positions of chair and vice chair of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH) have been evaluated. On Monday, he announced that only three candidates—Miklós Ligeti, Anna Róza Unger, and Dávid Jancsics—remain in the running for the presidency of the NVVH.
The finalists come from diverse professional backgrounds. Miklós Ligeti is a lawyer and the legal director of Transparency International Hungary, a self-declared “anti-corruption” organization linked to the Soros network. Anna Róza Unger is a political scientist and associate professor at the Faculty of Social Sciences at Eötvös Loránd University. Her research focuses on direct democracy, electoral systems, and political financing. In recent years, she has also contributed to programs on the Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, a liberal-leaning international broadcaster, and the radical left-leaning Partizán. Dávid Jancsics is a sociologist and “corruption researcher” who lives and works in the United States, he is currently a professor at San Diego State University.
“To ensure genuine public oversight and professional safeguards, we consider the involvement of civil society to be crucial. The invited civil society organizations directly help us make the best possible decision through their expertise, independent perspectives, and professional knowledge, and their presence ensures the highest level of transparency toward the public,” Hantosi explained. He then revealed which three civil society organizations will consult with them prior to the selection process: the Hungarian Civil Liberties Union (TASZ), the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, and the nonprofit organization K-Monitor.
All three are strongly left-leaning NGOs with diverse ties to the Soros network, known for their long track-record of attacking the previous conservative government of Viktor Orbán.
Hantosi also emphasized that Prime Minister Péter Magyar will not have the right to veto the selection process.
The FIDESZ parliamentary group had previously announced that it would not participate in the nomination and selection of NVVH leaders because it considers the regulations governing the agency to be unconstitutional in several respects. Gábor Szűcs, a FIDESZ member of parliament, also reaffirmed the party’s position in a Facebook post on Monday.
He stated that FIDESZ will appeal to the Constitutional Court regarding the “the secret police law,” since “the entire organization is merely a tool of Péter Magyar’s autocracy,” whose goal is to settle political scores with his opponents.
The main criticism of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office is that it creates a “super-agency” unprecedented in the Hungarian legal system.
Since the agency is to be granted hybrid powers—combining administrative, investigative, and prosecutorial (prosecutor’s office) authorities—the proposal is facing sharp criticism from multiple quarters.
János Bóka, the FIDESZ parliamentary group leader, had particularly harsh words. “If you think you can turn to another authority to challenge the arbitrariness or abuses of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office, you are sorely mistaken. The agency can take over any proceeding at any time, and there is no legal remedy against this decision,” the politician warned.
Já

items.title: Ruppert Murdoch családi utódlási viszálya tényleg annyira kínos volt, mint az Utódlásban
items.summary: Ez derült ki a most nyilvánosságra hozott bírósági dokumentumokból.
items.body_text:
Ruppert Murdoch családi utódlási viszálya tényleg annyira kínos volt, mint az Utódlásban
Rupert Murdoch ausztrál-amerikai médiamogul tavaly tett pontot a régóta húzódó családi vitája végére, amikor eldőlt, hogy a gyerekei közül ki irányíthatja majd hatalmas médiabirodalmát. Az HBO Utódlás című sorozatához kísértetiesen hasonló folyamatban végül a legidősebb fia, Lachlan kapta meg a pozíciót.
Egy nevadai bírósági tisztviselő által nemrég nyilvánosságra hozott, 2024 végén született bírósági dokumentumból az derült ki, hogy a Murdoch-örökösök közötti viszályt valóban szinte lemásolta a drámasorozat.
A médiamogul James nevű, kisebbik fiát a nagy hatalmú apa például bajkeverőnek tartotta, és úgy gondolta, ki kell zárni őt az üzletből. De részletes bepillantást kaphatunk a négy idősebb Murdoch-gyerek közti feszültségekbe is, és ahogyan „apró sérelmeiknek” adtak hangot apjukkal szemben.
A családi per még 2024 szeptemberében indult, miután Murdoch azt tervezte, hogy legidősebb fia, Lachlan úgy vegye át tőle a cégbirodalmat, hogy abba a három másik testvér, Prudence, Elisabeth és James ne tudjon beavatkozni. A nevadai bíróság viszont elutasította a milliárdos kérelmét, a döntés szerint Rupert Murdoch és Lachlan Murdoch „rosszhiszeműen” cselekedtek, ezért a bíróság „gondosan kidolgozott színjátéknak” nevezte a törekvéseiket.
A bíróságnak átadott levelezésben a 95 éves üzletember kijelentette, hogy katasztrófa lenne, ha a vagyona „rossz kezekbe” kerülne, a (trumpista) Fox News hangja pedig szerinte „elengedhetetlen a demokráciák számára”. Murdoch már 2019-ben arra próbálta rávenni Lachlant, hogy vásárolja ki testvérei részesedését, hogy a halála után ő vehesse át a vezetést. A dokumentumok szerint mindannyian hajlandóak lettek volna eladni a részesedésüket, csakhogy Lachlan ajánlatát túl alacsonynak tartották.
Murdoch a bíróságnak azért azt is elmondta: „Mindegyik gyerekemet szeretem – az, hogy Lachlant támogatom, nem jelenti, hogy ez ne így lenne. De ezeknek a vállalatoknak megfelelő vezetőre van szükségük, és Lachlan ez a vezető.”
A Murdoch család érdekeltségei közé számos médiavállalkozás tartozik, többek között a Fox News, a Wall Street Journal, a brit Times, valamint több ausztrál lap, köztük az Australian, a news.com.au és a News24 (korábban Sky).

items.title: Kizárta egy már megnyert pályázatból Mészáros Lőrinc pulykafeldolgozóját az agrárminisztérium, jogi lépéseket tervez a Gallicoop
items.summary: A cég szerint márciusban értesítették őket, hogy elnyerték az üzem- és kapacitásbővítésre kiírt támogatást, ezt azonban júliusban visszavonta a minisztérium.
items.body_text:
Kizárta egy már megnyert pályázatból Mészáros Lőrinc pulykafeldolgozóját az agrárminisztérium, jogi lépéseket tervez a Gallicoop
Visszavonta a támogatást, és kizárta egy korábban már megnyert pályázatból a Mészáros Lőrinc érdekeltségébe tartozó Gallicoop Zrt.-t az Agrár- és Élelmiszergazdaságért Felelős Minisztérium – írja közleményében a cég.
A magyar húsipar egyik legnagyobb szereplőjének számító pulykafeldolgozó céget a közlemény szerint a választás előtt, március 4-én értesítette az agrárminisztérium, hogy elnyerte a pályázatban kiírt uniós forrásokat. Az Élelmiszeripar Bajnokai programban részt vevő vállalkozások üzemeinek fejlesztésére megítélt támogatást azonban július 23-án visszavonta a minisztérium, és kizárta a Mészáros-csoport érdekeltségébe tartozó céget a pályázatból.
A Gallicoop a döntést jogi úton kívánja megtámadni, és „a rendelkezésére álló valamennyi jogorvoslati lehetőséggel élni fog”. „A téves híresztelésekkel ellentétben bármely pályázaton elnyert támogatás semmilyen esetben sem a tulajdonosi kör pénztárcájába kerül. A pályázati támogatások mindig szigorúan meghatározott beruházásokra fordíthatóak” – írják. A cég szerint vágóhídi, üzemi kapacitásbővítésre, valamint ezekhez kapcsolódó technológiai, és beszállítói fejlesztésekre költötték volna az összeget.
Azzal kapcsolatban, hogy mi indokolta a kizárást, az agrárminisztériumnak is küldtünk kérdéseket. Ha válaszoltak, frissítjük cikkünket.

items.title: Ruszin-Szendi: A pilóta az utolsó pillanatig, az életét kockáztatva próbálta menteni a Gripent
items.summary: A gép műszerei elsötétültek, de a pilóták tudtak egymással kommunikálni. A miniszter szerint mindkettőjüket óriási dicséret illeti.
items.body_text:
Ruszin-Szendi: A pilóta az utolsó pillanatig, az életét kockáztatva próbálta menteni a Gripent
Egy 51 éves, tapasztalt, rendkívül jó fizikai állapotban lévő pilóta vezette azt a Gripent, amelyik balesetet szenvedett a szolnoki katonai repülőtéren hétfőn. Eddig több mint kétezer órát repült, nemzetközi műveletekben is részt vett. Ezt Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz honvédelmi miniszter mondta a Retro rádió reggeli műsorában a műsorvezető, Bochkor Gábor kérdésére. A pilóta gerince megsérült, kedden műtik a Honvédkórházban, „11 és 14 óra között kell érte szorítani”, tette hozzá a miniszter.
Nagy sebességű elfogást gyakoroltak, amikor a baleset bekövetkezett. Kecskemétről szálltak fel, oda-vissza megcsinálták a gyakorlatot, majd a második elfogás végén jöttek folyamatosan a hibaüzenetek, és elsötétültek a műszerek. A műsorban elmondták, hogy a Gripenekben nincsenek analóg műszerek, ami azt jelenti, hogy egy ilyen esetnél a pilóta nem tudja, milyen sebességgel megy, milyen magasságban van, „csak az alapján tud vezetni, amit lát”.
Szerencsére a gépek közötti kommunikáció nem szakadt meg, így a kísérő segítségével el tudott jutni a szolnoki repülőtérre. Le tudott szállni, ám a gép már a betonon elkezdett kitörni jobbra, és a pilóta akkor katapultált, amikor látta, hogy már nem tudja megfogni.
„Az utolsó pillanatig, az életét is kockáztatva próbálta megmenteni a gépet, ezt az óriási, 30 milliárd forintos értéket. Mindkét pilótát óriási dicséret illeti”
– mondta a miniszter.
A katapultálásról is szó volt. Ilyenkor óriási, akár 15-20 G-s terhelés is érheti a szervezetet, önmagában a kilövéstől is megsérülhet a gerinc. A pilóta a katapultálás után a betonra érkezett, ami szintén ronthatott a helyzetén.
Mi történik ezután, hogyan pótoljuk a kiesett gépet? Ezt majd a vizsgálat eredménye dönti el, a svéd gyártó is szeretné mielőbb kideríteni, mi történt. „Nagyon jó velük a kapcsolatunk”, de az ártárgyalás egy másik történet lesz Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz szerint.
A gépen levegő-levegő rakéták és gépágyúlőszerek is voltak. A miniszter szerint ha a tűzoltók nem végezték volna hatékonyan a munkájukat, akkor nagyobb baj is történhetett volna. A feketedobozok kiértékelése még hátravan, és a további fejleményekről is be fognak számolni.

items.body_text:
ASEAN Plus Three Film Festival Returns to Prague for Its Fifth Edition
Prague Morning
The ASEAN Committee in Prague (ACP), representing the embassies of ASEAN member states, together with the embassies of China, Japan and the Republic of Korea, will host the fifth edition of the ASEAN Plus Three Film Festival (APTFF).
The festival will begin on Monday, September 7, 2026, at the Municipal Library of Prague.
Organised in cooperation with the Municipal Library of Prague, the festival will run until September 14 and feature seven full-length films, alongside a curated selection of short films from across the ASEAN Plus Three region.
Since its launch in 2022, the APTFF has introduced Czech audiences to the diverse cultures and cinematic voices of ASEAN and its Plus Three partners.
Previous editions have featured acclaimed films including Escape from Mogadishu (Republic of Korea), Father and Son (Viet Nam) and Yuni (Indonesia).
This year’s programme includes Solata: Friends Are the Family We Choose (Indonesia), Babah (Malaysia), The Beginning (Myanmar), I’m Perfect (the Philippines), 4 Tigers (Thailand), Song of the South (Viet Nam) and One and Only (China).
A selection of short films will also be screened during the opening night on September 7.
The programme includes Mbiyodo/Communal Work (Indonesia), Ninavau (Malaysia), Myanmar Be Enchanted (Myanmar), Lola Loleng/Grandma Loleng (the Philippines), Give to Getters (Thailand), Welcome to Viet Nam (Viet Nam), My Chinese Ecological Notes (China), Pukkulapottas and Hours in the Forest (Japan), and Persona (Republic of Korea).
Beyond its cultural programme, the festival is part of a broader effort by ASEAN and its Plus Three partners to introduce Czech audiences to the region, its societies and creative industries, as well as its shared identity as a community of more than 690 million people.
All screenings are open to the public and free of charge. Films will be shown in their original languages with English and Czech subtitles.
The full programme and schedule are available on the Municipal Library of Prague website.

items.body_text:
GALLERY: Light Installation "Synapse" Coming to Florenc Metro Station
Prague Morning
Jan Poš light installation Synapse will go on display in the Florenc Line C metro passage at the end of September.
The artwork will track passengers’ movements and complement the existing Battle of Sokolovo mosaic. Prague city councillors approved around CZK 1.38 million in funding to complete and install the artwork.
“Synapse” is a light-based installation by visual artist Jan Poš (1996) and the winning entry in the “Light for the Metro” competition held in 2023.
The aim was to create a light artwork for the passage connecting the north and south concourses of Florenc metro station. A total of 23 artists and teams submitted proposals, with four advancing to the final stage, which was conducted as a competitive dialogue.
The five-member jury considered the artwork’s long-term maintenance and its ability to withstand demanding operating conditions.
According to Poš, the artwork, installed on the wall opposite the underpass’s main staircase, comes into view as metro passengers ascend or descend the stairs.
It becomes part of their daily journey while remaining elegantly set apart, creating a space where it can stand on its own and offer a moment of respite from the hustle and bustle.
Poš says the work’s format and style enliven and build on the Battle of Sokolovo mosaic, creating a bridge between the past and present of the city.
The artwork was originally due to be installed alongside the completion of the reconstruction of the station’s ceiling slab. Prague’s public transport operator, DPP, has been repairing the structure since 2022 due to corrosion.

items.body_text:
Partial Lunar Eclipse to Be Visible From Prague at Dawn on August 28
Prague Morning
Prague residents willing to get up early on Friday, August 28, will have a chance to witness a partial lunar eclipse, with almost the entire Moon passing into Earth’s shadow shortly before it sets.
The eclipse will reach its maximum at 6:12 a.m. CEST. By then, only a narrow section along the Moon’s northern edge will remain illuminated.
In Prague, the Moon is expected to set at approximately 6:17 a.m., leaving only a few minutes to observe the eclipse at its peak.
The partial phase will begin at 4:33 a.m. As the event progresses, Earth’s shadow will gradually cover the lunar surface, reducing the bright portion of the Moon until only a thin illuminated crescent remains visible.
Astronomers at the Silesian University in Opava say observers will need an unobstructed view towards the southwest, as the Moon will be low above the horizon throughout the most important part of the event.
The eclipse follows another major astronomical event visible from the Czech Republic earlier this month, giving skywatchers a second opportunity to observe a rare celestial phenomenon within a short period.
Unlike a solar eclipse, observing the Moon does not require protective eyewear. The eclipse can be seen with the naked eye, while binoculars or a camera may provide a closer view.
For the best chance of seeing the maximum phase, observers should choose a location with a clear southwestern horizon and arrive before dawn. Weather conditions will also play a decisive role in whether the eclipse is visible.

items.body_text:
Family Suspects Murder in Death of 21-Year-Old Trans Man in Batumi
Dmitry Menyaev, a 21-year-old transgender man and Russian citizen, was found dead in his brother’s apartment in Batumi on August 15.
Authorities are investigating the case under the “incitement to suicide” provision, which is commonly applied in Georgia when a person is found dead under unclear circumstances. Menyaev’s family, however, suspects that other people may have been involved in his death.
“The family maintains that his death was not related to suicide and assumes that other persons may have been involved in his death,” Zviad Markoidze, the family lawyer, told Interpressnews. “The family suspects murder rather than suicide,” he said in separate remarks with RFE/RL’s Georgian Service.
Markoidze said that Menyaev, a Russian citizen who had lived in Georgia since 2022, was last active on Telegram on August 3. His body was discovered on August 15 after neighbors alerted the police to a strong odor coming from his apartment, according to media reports.
According to the lawyer, Menyaev lived alone and had no known illnesses or other problems that, in the family’s view, would explain his death.
An initial examination found no apparent signs of violence on the body, Markoidze said. He noted, however, that the final forensic findings are still pending.
Markoidze cited an expert as saying that there were no traces of violence on the body, but the lawyer noted the body was examined about 12 days after Menyaev’s presumed death, making it impossible to identify smaller injuries.
The family has reportedly requested to be recognized as an injured party, which would allow them to access the case materials, and has called for the case to be reclassified.
Separately, the victim’s brother also told TV Pirveli about his suspicions that Menyaev may have been killed. Per the translation provided by the channel, the brother said the apartment was found in disarray, and that evidence at the scene appeared inconsistent with the initial suggestion of suicide, raising suspicions that another person may have been present.

Ex-PM Garibashvili Charged With Bribe-Taking After Claims of Blackmail
Former Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, currently serving a five-year prison sentence after pleading guilty in a money laundering case, has been charged with taking a bribe, shortly after claiming that he was subjected to pressure and blackmail to take the blame in a forthcoming corruption case.
The Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia announced on August 24 that Garibashvili had been charged with accepting a particularly large bribe as a public official and by a group of persons acting on a prior agreement. The scheme allegedly resulted in total losses of up to GEL 7 million (USD 2.7 million) to public funds, with the ex-PM facing 11 to 15 years in prison if convicted.
The charges stem from a Defense Ministry procurement case that has already led to several arrests and convictions, including of ex-Defense Minister Juansher Burchuladze, over an alleged scheme that involved purchasing medical inventory at an artificially inflated price to secure cash payment from the company involved. According to prosecutors, the charges are based on testimonies from Burchuladze and his brother-in-law, Vasil Mkheidze.
According to prosecutors, Garibashvili also participated in the deal and secured a bribe of GEL 750,000 (about USD 290,000).
Alleged Procurement Scheme
The prosecutors say that in 2022, when Garibashvili was Prime Minister and Burchuladze was Defense Minister, Mkheidze reached an agreement with a business acquaintance to tailor the tender for medical equipment and inventory to ensure the his company’s victory, asking in return for 10% of the total contract value to be paid to him in cash.
To provide additional guarantees to the businessman involved, Burchuladze allegedly agreed the deal with Garibashvili, with Garibashvili allegedly requesting his share of the “material benefit.”
According to the prosecutors, the alleged deal was followed by a procurement process in which Burchuladze’s associates created an uncompetitive environment, artificially inflating the value of the goods and services to be procured under classified contracts. As a result, the Ministry purchased medical equipment and other inventory with a real value of GEL 11,499,705 for GEL 18,484,960, the agency said.
As part of the deal, the businessman involved handed GEL 1.9 million — approximately 10% of the total contract value — to Mkheidze in several installments, the Prosecutor’s Office said. Mkheidze allegedly retained GEL 400,000 and handed the remaining GEL 1.5 million to Burchuladze, who, in turn, handed half of that amount — GEL 750,000 — to Garibashvili as a bribe.
“As a result of the aforementioned actions, the state suffered substantial property damage amounting to GEL 6,985,255, and the public interest was seriously violated,” the Prosecutor’s Office said.
Garibashvili’s Blackmail Allegations
The new charges follow fresh allegations by Garibashvili himself that he was subjected to blackmail and pressure to take the blame in a forthcoming corruption case, allegedly as a means of keeping him out of politics for good. Garibashvili is currently serving a five-year sentence after pleading guilty in a serious money laundering case. His defense has argued that admitting to receiving illicit income does not amount to confessing to corruption.

items.body_text:
Harvard Georgian Studies Program Closes After Tbilisi Does Not Extend Funding
The program on Georgian Studies at Harvard University in the U.S., launched in 2022 within the Davis Center for Russian and Eurasian Studies with the backing of the Georgian government, has closed after the Georgian Education Ministry refused to extend funding.
The Ministry cited the university’s failure to submit an “agreed program” about the project’s future as the reason for the refusal to approve the extension. Natia Chankvetadze, the program’s latest head, however, says no feedback was received from the ministry on the extension proposal, and suggested the absence of “political will” may be the true reason.
The program, with a mission to become a “leading hub” for Georgian studies outside Georgia, was first inaugurated by then-Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili in September 2021, and launched in 2022, covering teaching, research, and exchanges focused on Georgian language, history, politics, and culture, among others.
It was initially headed by Professor Stephen Jones, a longtime scholar of Georgian history and politics, before Dr. Natia Chankvetadze, a peacebuilding scholar and practitioner, assumed leadership in late August 2024.
Reports about the program’s closure emerged on August 21, with observers – including former program fellow Beka Kobakhidze – alleging that the decision stemmed from Tbilisi’s dissatisfaction with the political stances of Harvard academics, including its initial head, Stephen Jones.
Ministry Cites Absence of ‘Agreed’ Program
Commenting on initial reports about the project’s closure, the Georgian Education Ministry said on August 22 that the funding extension could not be granted because Harvard had failed to submit an “agreed program” for the project’s future.
The ministry said it “asked Harvard to provide a report on the work completed and a concrete vision for the program’s further development,” but “the program’s further extention could not be agreed because, for the launch of the new phase, no agreed program has been submitted to the ministry which would define specific activities, a budget, an implementation timeline, and measurable outcomes.”
According to the ministry, the decision not to extend the project was based “on the efficient and accountable management of state resources and the existence of the programmatic and financial framework required to launch a new phase.” It “does not mean a refusal of academic cooperation with Harvard.”
The Ministry argued that it had expressed readiness for continued cooperation as part of the program and had allocated funding, while extending funding several times, including till March 31, 2025, “to allow the program to complete remaining activities and present the relevant reports.” It also pointed to the readiness to carry out joint activities “consistent with the goals and purpose set out in the contract” after the program’s closure, noting that Harvard can still direct the funds for the program objectives “based on the submission of financial reports and documents.”
The ministry “remains ready to consider future cooperation with Harvard on the basis of clearly defined objectives, an agreed budget, an implementation timeline, and measurable outcomes,” the statement said.
Program Head Points to Lack of ‘Political Will’, No Feedback From Ministry
Speaking to Civil.ge, Natia Chankvetadze, who headed the program until late June 2026, suggested that a lack of political will may have been the real reason behind the ministry’s decision, noting that the authorities did not provide feedback on the extension proposal submitted last year.
“I think that, simply, there is no longer a political will from the ministry to extend this program rather than the reasons the Ministry cited, because they had received both the reports and the vision for the further development,” Chankvetadze said.

items.title: Armenian army suffers fourth non-combat death in one month
items.summary: A soldier was found with fatal gunshot wounds, and a murder investigation has been launched.
items.body_text:
Two Armenian soldiers died in non-combat conditions days apart. One of the soldiers, 22-year-old Edgar Gevorgyan, was shot dead on Sunday, while another unnamed soldier died on Monday. The incidents come amidst renewed scrutiny into a spate of non-combat deaths occurring within the army.
Gevorgyan was found dead from a gunshot wound and the authorities have detained a suspect in his murder.
The authorities have yet to share any additional information about the death of the unnamed 37-year-old soldier who died on Monday.
Just a week prior, a soldier was killed, and six others were injured after a lorry hit them on the road in Armenia’s Gegharkunik province. Earlier in August, one person was arrested and is suspected to have incited a fellow soldier to commit suicide. The incident triggered major reshuffles in the army following a rise in non-combat deaths this year.
In response, Pashinyan appointed Aram Hovhannisyan as head of the Military Police and dismissed Seryozha Stepanyan from his position as head of the Department of Morale and Psychological Support in the army. He also established an interagency working group to develop systemic solutions to suicides and ‘non-statutory relations’ in the army. The working group has three months to develop and submit proposals to curb such deaths in the army.
On Monday, while introducing the new government programme to parliament, Pashinyan talked about the concerning cases of army deaths.
‘Our efforts to eliminate these problems will not stop, and we are already outlining concrete programs on how we should solve this problem, while also understanding that it is in some way connected to changes in the external environment,’ he said.
Also on Monday, Defence Minister Suren Papikyan discussed the recent deaths, stating that although statistics are not a correct way to address the army deaths, historical army statistics demonstrate that suicides and similar cases have occurred consistently over the years due to criminal activities within the army. Papikyan claimed that the Defence Ministry did not get blamed for such deaths in the past.
Papikyan said that the ministry’s continuous efforts have reduced the number of deaths to two in 2025. However, according to the Military Prosecutor’s Office, in 2025, 30 soldiers died in non-combat conditions.
The difference in numbers was explained by Defence Ministry spokesperson Aram Torosyan earlier this month. He said that statistics often show a single total number without distinguishing between deaths linked to military service and those that are not.
As reports continue streaming in about non-combat deaths in the army, civil society is urging the Defence Ministry to take responsibility for these deaths and work towards resolving the underlying issues, rather than generalising responsibility and using statistics to distinguish between service-related and unrelated deaths.

items.title: Chechen trans man found dead in Batumi, brother says he was murdered
items.summary: The death is being investigated under articles pertaining to suicide.
items.body_text:
A 21-year-old Chechen trans man was found dead in Batumi in mid-August. The Georgian authorities are investigating his death under articles pertaining to suicide, however, his brother believes he may have been ‘violently murdered’ because of his gender identity.
The young man, Dmitry Menyaev, had been living in Georgia since 2022. He was found dead in an apartment in the western Georgian city of Batumi on 15 August. It is not clear when Menyaev passed away, but reports of his death first appeared in the media on 22 August.
Menyaev was born in Moscow and had also lived in Saint Petersburg before moving to Georgia. In recent years, he lived in his brother’s apartment in Batumi.
Menyaev’s body was discovered after residents of the building called 112 because of a strong odour emanating from the apartment in a residential building on Mamia Komakhidze Street. The family received notification of Menyaev’s death from the Georgian authorities after his body was found.
Menyaev’s brother, Kuzma Yakimets, has asked that the case be reclassified, saying he believes his brother was murdered and that his death may have been connected to his gender identity.
Yakimets said he last spoke to his brother on 1 August. He initially believed that 3 August was the last time Menyaev had been seen online, but later learned that a mutual acquaintance had communicated with him on 4 August.
Yakimets told OC Media that Menyaev had not shown any signs of distress before his death.
‘There were no complaints, no difficult topics — it was simple communication without complaints, without […] any hints at problems’, Yakimets said.
Yakimets said he could not disclose details due to the ongoing investigation, but described the apartment as unusually messy.
‘A lot of things were scattered around on all sides’, he said, adding that in his view, there was evidence indicating that another person had been present in the apartment.
Yakimets said he believed the death was violent, but acknowledged that the investigation has not yet been reclassified as a murder case because authorities are waiting for the medical examiner’s conclusion on the cause of death.
‘The main thing about the circumstances is that the death was violent’, he told OC Media. ‘It was a violent death — not a natural one, not an accident, not suicide’.
The lawyer representing Menyaev’s family, Zviad Markoidze, said a superficial examination of the body had not shown signs of violence, but that the cause of death had not yet been established.
Menyaev’s body had already begun to decompose by the time it was found, which the lawyer said could make determining the cause of death more difficult. The expert’s conclusions have not yet been released.
Georgia’s Interior Ministry told OC Media that Menyaev’s death is being investigated under a criminal code clause concerning ‘incitement to suicide’. The authorities often investigate deaths with no immediate explanations as to their circumstances under that clause.
Yakimets said he had asked investigators and prosecutors to change the classification of the case, but was told that they could not draw conclusions about the cause of death before receiving the medical examiner’s report.
He said he currently considered the investigator handling the case competent, although he could not assess the investigator’s motives or disclose details of the investigation.

Menyaev was trying to work as a board game host and sometimes visited local board game clubs, Yakimets added.
‘He liked it here. He considered it his home’, Yakimets said.

items.title: Tbilisi fines company behind Rustaveli Avenue construction for not working 24/7
items.summary: The company was fined a total of four times.
items.body_text:
Tbilisi City Hall has fined the company responsible for Rustaveli Avenue’s renovation and road construction, Smart Solutions, after violating the agreement that required them to continue work on the project 24/7. The construction company was fined four times for failing to adhere to the stipulated work schedule, leading to a total of ₾5,000 ($1,900) in fines.
The road construction company was fined on 23 July, twice on 29 July, and lastly on 10 August for the fourth time. All four fines were caused by the same violation, which was failing to continue to work without breaks throughout a 24-hour period. The company was fined with 0.02% of the service value, reaching up to a total of ₾5,000 ($1,900). The company says it was experiencing unforeseen delays and has disputed the justification for the fine.
Tbilisi City Hall has signed three contracts with Smart Solutions worth ₾20 million ($8 million) yo carry out the renovation project.
Reportedly, Smart Solution owner Levan Gogsadze, who is related to Georgian Dream party MP Beka Odisharia, claimed that the 100-day deadline for the renovation will not be enough.
Opposition Lelo party member Nika Cherkezishvili said that the tender for the renovation of Rustaveli Avenue was poorly organised and that Smart Solutions won the tender without any competition.
Cherkezishvili added that millions are being spent from the budget on the project, while the closed roads are causing significant problems for locals. Cherkezishvili called the fine as a percentage of the total contract ‘hilariously low’.
While still underway, the Rustaveli renovation is widely thought to become yet another City Hall project to fail to meet the originally established deadline.
Tbilisi City Hall started the Varketili Metro station renovation in late December 2022. The initial deadline for the project was 18 months, but after failing to complete it in time, authorities added an additional 18 months.
Varketili Metro was finally renovated and opened in March 2026.
Authorities have been discussing the renovation of Rustaveli Avenue since 2023. However, in 2025, Mayor Kakha Kaladze stated that work on the thoroughfare had to be postponed because studies showed that large-scale works could cause long-term problems for Tbilisi.
Rustaveli Avenue has historically been the site of numerous mass protests and clashes between protesters and riot police.

items.title: EU prepares for AI slipping beyond human control, Finnish tech chief says
items.summary: AI models have recently escaped their testing environments, sparking concerns over risks.
items.body_text:
For the European Union, the most serious security risk posed by artificial intelligence is what might happen if humans lose control of it, said Henna Virkkunen (NCP), the EU's commissioner for tech sovereignty, speaking to Yle.
"These technologies are advancing so rapidly that safeguards are indispensable," she argued, adding that they must operate within clearly defined security constraints, with humans retaining ultimate control.
Recent incidents have underscored the point, she noted. AI models have, in some cases, escaped their testing environments and caused problems with potentially serious implications.
At the end of July, an AI agent developed by OpenAI broke out of its test environment. A week later, models from Anthropic followed suit. In early August, Meta's Muse Spark model reportedly gained access to another company's systems.
Regulating threats
The EU is trying to get ahead of the risks through regulation. Its AI Act requires providers to assess risks continuously and maintain specified safety mechanisms.
This matters, she said, in a world where hostile actors are prepared to exploit AI.
"I wouldn’t say I'm afraid of it, but of course it is a risk that has been taken into account — and must continue to be taken into account. We must ensure that AI models are safe, and that they are continuously assessed and monitored, including after they enter the market," Virkkunen said.
International cooperation, according to Virkkunen, is the most important way to guard against the risks posed by AI. She says that international players are taking the EU's regulations into account.
"In this way, Europe is also helping to set the standards for AI," she said.

items.title: Siberian wildfires worsen air quality across Finland

items.body_text:
Extensive wildfires in Siberia are worsening air quality in parts of Finland on Monday, the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI) told STT.
Winds brought fine particulate matter to Lapland over the weekend. The particles spread overnight along western Finland and into the southern parts of the country.
Air quality in many areas was rated as "fair" or "satisfactory" during the morning.
However, the FMI said the situation is expected to improve by Tuesday.
The levels of fine particulate matter currently detected in Finland are typical of those commonly seen in Central Europe, according to the FMI.
Fine particulate matter refers to particles measuring less than 2.5 micrometres in diameter. These particles can travel thousands of kilometres with air masses.
The FMI's northernmost air quality monitoring station is in Kittilä, western Lapland, where air quality was rated as satisfactory on Saturday.

For a recent article on the real-life effects of Sweden's immigration laws on families in Sweden, The Local's Mandy Pipher spoke with a Swedish-American couple who are both biological scientists and living in Uppsala.
The pair met a decade ago when Anna-Karin moved to Chicago for a postdoctoral position in immunology and flu vaccine research. Chris, also a biologist, was finishing his immunology PhD at the same university. Three years later, when Anna-Karin was moving back to Sweden for another work opportunity, the two were a committed couple, and they made plans for Chris to follow to Sweden as soon as possible.

There's been confusion about to what extent the Left Party will back a Social Democrat government after leader Nooshi Dadgostar during an interview appeared to backtrack regarding her party's ultimatum to refuse support for any government they do not actively sit in. The party later claimed the comments were a "misunderstanding".
In an interview with broadcaster TV4 less than three weeks before the September 13th election, Dadgostar was first asked whether the Left Party maintains its stance that it must be part of a government to support it, to which she replied yes.
However, when asked next under what circumstances she would be prepared to bring down Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson, Dadgostar answered: "No, well, we obviously won't do that, and I don't think there will be a snap election at all. There are no incentives for anyone, except possibly the Centre Party, to do that. We will sort this out."

Party press secretary Maria Carlsson later called the comments a "misunderstanding".
"Our position remains unchanged, meaning that we must sit in government if our votes are necessary to form it," she wrote to TV4, adding that Dadgostar meant the Left Party is prepared to "negotiate with other parties to prevent us from ending up in such a situation".
The conflict between the Left Party and the Centre Party may become one of the hardest conundrums to solve for Andersson after the election. The former insists on seats in government, whereas the latter refuses to govern together with the other. (TT/The Local)

More political parties than ever before have registered to stand in this year's elections in Sweden, with 165 parties signed up for the parliamentary election alone.
