According to the Swedish Election Authority, a total of 415 unique parties have registered, which also includes 173 for the regional council elections and 380 for the municipal council elections, which both take place on the same day as the national election for parliament.
That marks a notable increase compared to the 2022 general election, when 103 parties stood for parliament, 130 for regional councils and 328 for local municipalities.

items.title: Today in Germany: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
items.summary: Nearly one in 12 long-distance DB trains cancelled this year, Volkswagen employees slam company leadership, Germany's economy grows more than expected as government debt rises and more news on Tuesday, August 25th.
items.body_text:
Tuesday's top story: Almost one in 12 long-distance Deutsche Bahn trains cancelled in 2026
In the first half of the year, almost one in 12 long-distance trains at Deutsche Bahn (eight percent) was cancelled completely or at least on part of the route.
That's three percent more cancellations than in the same period last year and the second-highest level since 2019.
This is according to a response by the Ministry of Transport to a request from the Green party, reported by the German Press Agency (DPA).
Only in the first half of 2024 were there even more train cancellations (12 percent), which were largely due to union worker strikes.
Deutsche Bahn had previously shared that in the first six months of this year, only 58.7 percent of its long-distance trains were on time.
"Deutsche Bahn and the federal government must not stand idly by and watch the number of cancelled trains increase," said Green MP Matthias Gastel. He called for more investment in reserve trains and personnel.
Volkswagen workers slam management ahead of restructuring talks
Volkswagen employees in Germany have sharply criticised the company's leadership ahead of a series of meetings on the future of the struggling carmaker, increasing pressure on management as it pursues major cost-cutting measures.
According to an internal staff survey seen by AFP, workers ranked the board's "disastrous communication" as their biggest concern, ahead of fears over job losses and potential factory closures.
The findings come as chief executive Oliver Blume prepares to visit Volkswagen sites across Germany to discuss the company's plans with employees.
Volkswagen has already agreed around 50,000 job cuts across several brands, including Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche, but management has warned that a further 50,000 positions could be at risk.
Several German factories, including sites in Zwickau, Emden, Hanover, Osnabrück and Neckarsulm, are also under review for possible closure.
Blume recently described the challenges facing Volkswagen and the wider German automotive sector as the biggest upheaval in their history, arguing that deep reforms are needed to secure future investment in new technologies, products and production facilities.
READ ALSO: Volkswagen boss warns carmaker's situation 'more than critical'
Europe will experience more frequent weather extremes, says German researcher
According to climate researcher Stefan Rahmstorf, Europe will have to prepare for a particularly large number of extreme weather events in the future due to the strong warming of the continent.
"Where warming is particularly strong, there are also stronger extremes. Their frequency increases with warming," the scientist from the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) told the Rheinische Post.
Extremes that used to occur every 500 years could now occur about every 50 years, Rahmstorf said, adding: "We have not yet experienced the most extreme events, which are expected due to the current global warming of 1.4 degrees. Let alone for an even warmer climate, which we will have in the coming decades."
Even after this year's summer of extreme heat, drought, low water in rivers and forest fires, Rahmstorf warns, "It won't stay that way, but will continue to get worse."

German economy up slightly in spring, but state budget in the red
The German economy grew somewhat more strongly in the second quarter of this year than initially assumed.

But the German state, however, was firmly in the red.

items.title: What your choice of German supermarket says about you
items.summary: In Germany, the supermarket you frequent says a lot about you, potentially revealing hints about your daily routine, diet and how much you're willing to splurge on bread or beer, writes Paul Krantz.
items.body_text:
Like many new residents, when I first came to Germany I shopped almost exclusively at the two supermarkets that were closest to my house.
My first residence was just down the street from a Penny. In the opposite direction, and about twice as far away, was a REWE.
Naturally I shopped more often at Penny initially – it was closer – and I did appreciate how cheap everything was. I could get half-litre cans of beer for around 50 cents (including the deposit), and fill my backpack up with foods for around €15. (This was 2020. Those were the days.)
But it didn’t take too long for me to notice that certain foods just weren’t at Penny. If I wanted to take a stab at a recipe with more eclectic ingredients, I found that REWE was a better bet. REWE had about twice as much produce and it tended to look a bit more fresh in my opinion.
Eventually I discovered my local Aldi and Lidl, and then a Kaufland and a BioMarkt. At each new store, there was an exciting array of new products to be found. Even if maybe 90 percent of the experience at most of these stores was pretty much the same, they all had their interesting quirks.
Everyone who has lived in Germany for some years is bound to develop a preference. So please allow me to take a tongue-in-cheek look at what your choice of supermarket says about you.
READ ALSO: The complete German supermarket survival guide
Discounters: Aldi, Lidl, Penny and Netto etc.
First up we have the so-called discounters. These are the budget-friendly markets offering basic groceries, among other things, and are marked by easy in-around-and-out layouts.
Penny
Penny shoppers are a ‘no frills, no problem’ kind of people.
There’s nothing particularly interesting about Penny’s offering. It’s got what you came for - maybe not every single ingredient, but something that’ll work.
It’s the ideal store for those moments when you need either 12 frozen pizzas or maybe two bananas, a can of tuna, a bag of rice, and a bottle of cheap whisky.
Are the bananas a bit green? Yeah, but you like them that way.
Also it’s convenient that they have nacho cheese chips on the way. You didn’t come here for those, but you’re definitely grabbing them now.
Aldi
People who prefer Aldi are honestly a little bit concerning. There’s just so much going on in Aldi that you’ve got to be a bit of a chaos goblin to cope.
The first time I went to Aldi it was to buy a service plan for my cell phone, and I was waiting in line between a person buying bread and another buying milk and pyjamas. It’s just a bit much.
Aldi stores also tend to have huge sales racks organised in the most cryptic way imaginable. Of their sales items, some are marked down to good deals but others can be questionable.
Fun fact: There is a line, which runs between Essen and Mülheim and continues across the country, dividing Germany between the land of Aldi Nord and the land of Aldi Süd. Two brothers named Theo and Karl Albrecht took over the Albrecht Diskont (Aldi) family business, and eventually had a feud and split it up.
Lidl
A Lidl shopper is practical: thrifty but has standards, and no time to waste.
Lidl combines the cheap-and-best appeal of Penny with the non-sequitur shopping experience of Aldi. (Why is this aisle full of linens, work shoes and hot sauce?)
But if you know what to look for, you can find some high-quality goods at impossibly cheap prices – like the Lidl brand craft beers for example, or Greek yogurt.
READ ALSO: 365 German beers - What I learned from drinking a different variety each day
Lidl stores are found throughout Europe, and tend to carry the same products across locations, so it can also be the place to find foreign specialty goods like Kalamata olives or Italian Wines at discount prices.
A tale of two Nettos
The last big discounter in Germany is Netto.
That’s red-letter Netto to be clear, as opposed to Netto with the dog, which is actually a Danish retailer.
In case you hadn’t noticed, because most people don’t, there are two different markets called N

items.title: What's on in Germany: Nine unmissable events in September
items.summary: As summer gives way to autumn, Germany comes alive with world-famous festivals, major sporting events, cutting-edge art, classical music and centuries-old traditions.
items.body_text:
For many people, September in Germany means one thing: Oktoberfest. Despite its name, the world's largest folk festival takes place mostly in September, drawing millions of visitors to Munich every year.
But there's far more to Germany's autumn events calendar than beer tents and Lederhosen.
If beer isn't your thing, you could spend your month discovering emerging bands at Hamburg's Reeperbahn Festival, exploring contemporary art in Berlin, watching world-class runners race through the German capital, or sampling some of the country's finest wines in the Palatinate.
Here are nine events well worth adding to your calendar in September 2026.
September 3rd–16th: International Literature Festival Berlin
One of Europe's leading literary gatherings returns to the German capital this September, bringing together authors, poets, journalists and thinkers from around the world.
The International Literature Festival Berlin (ilb) offers readings, discussions and workshops across numerous venues in the city, with a strongly international perspective and extensive English-language programming.
It's an excellent opportunity for internationally minded Berliners and visitors to discover new voices and engage with global issues through literature.
READ ALSO: Buchpreisbindung - Why does Germany have fixed prices for books?
September 3rd–6th: Glücksgefühle Festival, Hockenheimring
If you're looking for big-name music acts and festival energy, the Glücksgefühle Festival (Happy feelings festival) promises four days of exactly that.
Held at the famous Hockenheimring race circuit in Baden-Württemberg, one of Germany's largest music festivals combines pop, hip-hop and EDM across multiple stages. Camping options make it easy to turn the event into a full weekend getaway.
With its feel-good atmosphere and broad musical programme, it's particularly well suited to younger festival-goers and groups of friends.
READ ALSO: 'Wanke nicht, mein Vaterland' - Germany's state anthems explained
September 3rd–October 3rd: Beethovenfest, Bonn
Music lovers should make a note of Beethovenfest, one of Germany's premier classical music festivals.
Held in the composer's birthplace of Bonn, the festival brings together international orchestras, chamber ensembles and acclaimed soloists for a month-long celebration of classical music.
The 2026 edition is especially significant as the historic Beethovenhalle returns as the festival's principal venue following an extensive renovation programme.
Even those new to classical music may find this a memorable introduction to one of Germany's great cultural traditions.
September 9th–13th: Berlin Art Week
For five days every September, Berlin transforms into one of Europe's most important centres for contemporary art.
Numerous museums, galleries, private collections and project spaces participate in Berlin Art Week, presenting exhibitions, performances, talks and special events across the city. Many events and gallery openings can be visited free of charge.
Whether you're a dedicated collector or simply curious about modern culture, the festival offers an ideal chance to explore Berlin's renowned creative scene.
READ ALSO: Everything that changes in Germany in September 2026
September 11th–21st: Dürkheimer Wurstmarkt, Bad Dürkheim
Despite its name, the Dürkheimer Wurstmarkt is not only about sausages. In fact, its more about wine really.
Held in the picturesque Palatinate region, the event is widely regarded as the world's largest wine festival. Visitors can sample hundreds of regional wines while enjoying fairground rides, local food and live entertainment.
The main celebrations take place across two festival weekends (September 11th–15th and September 18th–21st), with a smaller Zwischenmarkt (between markets) program continuing on September 16th and 17th.
Dating back more than 600 years, the festival attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors each year and offers travellers a more local alternative to Oktoberfest.

items.title: Indonesia's Public Works Ministry joins Jambi wildfire response

items.body_text:
Hanggodo said the ministry would support drought and wildfire mitigation throughout the potentially prolonged dry season in coordination with relevant agencies.
“The ministry is not focused solely on infrastructure development. We must ensure infrastructure supports disaster mitigation, water supplies, environmental protection and community safety,” he said.
Through the Sumatra VI Jambi River Basin Organization, the ministry joined efforts to extinguish fires in a plantation area in Pematang Gajah Village, Muaro Jambi District.
Severe dry conditions caused fires across 20 hectares of highly combustible peatland on Monday, August 24, according to the provincial wildfire command post.
Although the fires have been extinguished, crews are cooling hotspots and preventing flare-ups because the region’s peat remains highly flammable.
The river basin organization worked with the Environment Ministry’s fire brigade, regional disaster agencies, military, police and other institutions during the response.
The organization deployed two portable water tanks with a combined capacity of 2,000 liters to support firefighting operations.
The Environment Ministry provided a 4,000-liter tanker, while a local disaster agency deployed another truck carrying 5,000 liters of water.
The Public Works Ministry said the river basin organization would continue coordinating with regional governments and other agencies to strengthen suppression and cooling efforts and restore public safety.

items.title: RI's parliament targets asset forfeiture bill passage by Dec 2026
items.summary: Habiburokhman, chairman of Commission III of Indonesia’s House of Representatives, said deliberations on the ...
items.body_text:
Commission III will continue public hearings, consolidate input, meet with the government, deliberate on the bill and seek final approval at a December plenary session.
“After deducting recess periods, the parliament has only about eight effective weeks remaining to deliberate on the Asset Forfeiture Bill,” Habiburokhman said here Tuesday.
Commission III has held 35 public hearings, conducted three regional working visits and received written submissions from dozens of community groups, he said.
With the ratification deadline approaching, the public may still submit written views on the draft bill, Habiburokhman said.
He said efforts to gather public input were nearing their maximum capacity, with dozens of groups submitting their views to parliament.
Most respondents strongly support the bill’s creation while also backing careful drafting, Habiburokhman said.
“This will reduce the potential for corruption in enforcement efforts, particularly abuses of power by law enforcement officers,” he said.
Habiburokhman said the bill has taken longer than other legislation, including revisions to the Criminal Procedure Code and National Police Law, because its concept is new to Indonesia.
Law Minister Supratman Andi Agtas previously said President Prabowo Subianto had ordered the government to accelerate passage of the Asset Forfeiture Bill.
“The president’s order to the minister is clear: expedite it. But because the bill was initiated by parliament, we are waiting,” Supratman said on August 14.

items.title: Transmigration areas can power Indonesia's new economic hub: Economist
items.summary: Developing transmigration areas into new economic hubs is an effective strategy for Indonesia to capture opportunities ...
items.body_text:
He believes Indonesia occupies a favorable position due to its strategic trade location, abundant natural resources, and relatively neutral political stance.
"Indonesia's current position is highly favorable, with a relatively neutral political position, strategic trade routes, and important natural resources such as nickel, which are crucial for future industries," Bakaya said in a statement on Tuesday.
Speaking at the Transmigration Executive Dialogue (TED) in Jakarta on Monday, he said these conditions make the transformation of transmigration areas increasingly relevant amid global economic and geopolitical shifts.
He described the new approach to transmigration as the right program at the right time.
According to him, these opportunities could generate broader economic gains if investment in transmigration areas is accompanied by productive job creation, skills development, local business growth, and improved access to industries and markets.
Transmigration areas also require support from agricultural processing centers, logistics networks, modern facilities, financing access, and an innovation ecosystem to generate greater regional added value.
With a more comprehensive value chain, local communities will not only serve as raw material suppliers but also benefit from production, processing, distribution, and marketing activities, Bakaya emphasized.
Additionally, farmers and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) have the opportunity to secure technology, financing, business partners, and broader market access.
Transmigration Minister Muhammad Iftitah Sulaiman Suryanagara stated that this perspective aligns with the government's new paradigm, which prioritizes economic activity and job creation before population movement.
"The future of transmigration is not about moving people and hoping economic opportunities would follow. We must create economic opportunities, prepare decent jobs and lives, and then allow population mobility to follow voluntarily, safely, and with future certainty," he remarked.
He conveyed that transmigration areas are set to become economic ecosystems connecting communities, land, science, technology, investment, industry, and markets.
This ecosystem encompasses the entire value chain, including research, nurseries, production, processing, packaging, logistics, and marketing.
Suryanagara cited China's durian consumption, estimated at around Rp137 trillion (US$7.5 billion) annually, as an opportunity to build an industrial ecosystem for the commodity in Indonesia rather than exporting raw materials.
The new transmigration paradigm is being executed through five flagship programs: Trans Tuntas for land legal certainty, Trans Lokal for local community empowerment, Trans Patriot for strengthening human resources and technology, Trans Karya Nusantara for investment and job creation, and Trans Gotong Royong for strengthening stakeholder collaboration.
To bolster regional human resources, the Ministry of Transmigration plans to deploy 1,476 Patriot Expedition Team (TEP) participants across 246 teams to 53 transmigration areas in 2026.
The 53 locations comprise 41 national priority areas, two ministry-designated priority areas, and 10 locations in Papua.
The TEP 2026 cohort includes 39 professors, 158 doctoral degree holders, 263 master's degree graduates, and 1,016 undergraduates, tasked with following up on regional potential mapping through research, mentoring, and technology application.

items.body_text:
New UK PM Andy Burnham to make visit to Kyiv on Monday – office
LONDON — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will visit Kyiv on Monday on his first international visit since taking office last month, his office said, as Ukraine marks its 35th independence anniversary.
Burnham has vowed to give strong support to Ukraine as it battles Russia’s invasion.
The Labour Party leader’s visit comes as he announced that Britain had “agreed that defense firm MBDA can release classified information on UK components for the long-range missile, SCALP, to establish local assembly lines in Ukraine”, a statement said.
READ: UK’s Burnham to welcome Zelensky in first foreign leader visit
The missile is the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow, with both using shared French and British technology.
The UK was first to gift Ukraine long-range strike weapons for defensive purposes in 2023, according to the premier’s Downing Street office.
It said that the decision to release the classified information would “allow the French and Ukrainians to move forward with the Ukrainian assembly of the missile”.
“It also complements the major UK effort to rapidly develop low-cost advanced long-range strike weapons for Ukraine through Project Brakestop,” it added.
In Kyiv, Burnham will co-chair his first meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, which brings together countries supporting Kyiv.
The French presidency confirmed on Friday that the meeting would be held in a “hybrid” format — meaning some participants would attend in person while others joined via video conference.
READ: How new PM Andy Burnham will change UK’s international role
The office of Irish prime minister Micheal Martin indicated that he would participate remotely.
“On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes,” Burnham said in a statement.
Burnham’s visit comes weeks after Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky visited London.
During that trip, London also announced it would share with Kyiv information on a new battle-tested electronic jamming capability dubbed “Stone Cloak”.
When attached to drones, the tablet-sized, military-grade jammers can hinder Russian air defence systems from tracking and targeting such weapons in-flight, Downing Street said.
Britain has been one of Ukraine’s strongest backers since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, committing around 25 billion pounds ($34 billion) in support, including 16 billion pounds in military aid. /dl

items.body_text:
Red, yellow alerts raised over Visayas grid on Aug. 24
MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — Another round of red and yellow alerts was raised over the Visayas grid on Monday, August 24, as businesses opened for the day, potentially leading to rotational brownouts.
In an advisory released at 8 a.m. today, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said the grid had an available capacity of only 2,312 megawatts, while peak demand could reach 2,395 MW.
Due to the supply insufficiency, a red alert will be in effect from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., while yellow alerts will be raised from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. and 8 p.m. to 9 p.m.
READ: CERA to DOE: Fast-track new power projects in Visayas grid
NGCP said the supply shortfall may be attributed to the unavailability of the Visayas’ large coal-fired power plants TVI 1, TVI 2, and KSPC 1, as well as limited power imports from Mindanao, resulting in high demand forecasts in the area.
To date, eight power plants remain on forced outage this month. One plant has been on forced outage since July, three since June, seven since May, one since March, three since 2025, two since 2024, two since 2023, and one since 2021. Meanwhile, 13 plants are operating at derated capacities, bringing the total unavailable capacity to 896.3 megawatts (MW).
READ: DOE orders swift repairs to restabilize Visayas grid
For its part, the Department of Energy (DOE) said it was “actively coordinating with IEMOP, NGCP, ERC, generation companies, and industry stakeholders to expedite the safe restoration of affected facilities and implement all available measures to stabilize the grid and protect consumers.”
In a statement, the DOE said it continued “to closely monitor the grid and provide the public with information as the situation develops.”
A red alert status is issued when the available power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the transmission grid’s regulating requirement. A yellow alert, meanwhile, is raised when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement.

items.title: DENR seeks P29.5 billion in 2027 budget
items.summary: The DENR wants P1.6 billion for the National Greening Program (NGP), the government’s flagship reforestation project, with priority on the Sierra Madre
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) is seeking P29.5 billion in its proposed expenditure program for 2027.
The proposed allocation is marginally higher than the agency’s P28.3 billion budget in 2026.
P1.6 billion of the DENR’s proposed budget is for the National Greening Program (NGP), the government’s flagship reforestation project. In the implementation of the NGP, priority will be given to forest and landscape restoration in Sierra Madre.
P1.3 billion is for management of sites legislated as protected areas.
Manila Bay rehabilitation is allocated P1.3 billion in the proposal.
The department’s clean water program, a component of flood management, gets P336 million. This allocation includes the rehabilitation of rivers and esteros.
The hearing for DENR’s proposed budget is set on Wednesday, August 26, at 11 am. – Rappler.com

items.title: Ombudsman seeks P7.23-billion budget for 2027
items.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman initially proposes P12.63 billion, but the Department of Budget and Management cuts it by P5.57 billion
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The proposed 2027 budget for the Office of the Ombudsman is P7.23 billion, slightly higher than its P6.42-billion budget this year.
The Ombudsman initially proposed P12.63 billion, but the Department of Budget and Management cut it by P5.57 billion.
Speaking to reporters after the House budget deliberations on Tuesday, August 25, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said the office needs additional marshals and office space for its lawyers to allow them to work more effectively.
The Ombudsman Marshal is a security group, similar to the Supreme Court’s Office of the Judiciary Marshals.
The Office of the Ombudsman is also seeking P57.47 million in confidential funds.
In its National Expenditure Program, the Office of the Ombudsman has four programs with the following proposed budget:
- Anti-corruption Investigation Program: P913.23 million
- Anti-corruption Enforcement Program: P716.46 million
- Ombudsman Public Assistance Program: P266.21 million
- Corruption Prevention Program: P208.91 million
Since late 2025, the Ombudsman’s office has been leading the investigation into public officials with alleged links to multi-billion flood control corruption.
During the budget hearing, Remulla said his office is looking into Davao City as a possible “epicenter” of the flood control corruption during the previous Duterte administration.
He said huge amounts of funding for flood control projects were allegedly poured into the city, the main bailiwick of the Dutertes – political foes of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr..
Remulla, however, said the investigation has been hampered by limited access to information, as many people are reluctant to speak out. – Rappler.com

items.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
items.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate
items.body_text:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.
There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.
Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.
LATEST UPDATES
What was Mae Divinagracia holding while examining hostile witness?
Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia says she was holding a comfort cross during her examination of Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio, which she says she always brings to court, on the 18th day of Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Tuesday, August 25.
Sara Duterte knew about confidential OVP activities, says Ortonio
Rappler.com
Impeachment trial witness and Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio claims Vice President Sara Duterte was knowledgeable about her office’s confidential fund activities, during the 18th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial on Tuesday, August 25.
Ortonio: Informants bought medicine, food supplies using confi funds
Rappler.com
Impeachment trial witness and Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio says informants bought medicine and food supplies using their office’s confidential funds during the 18th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Tuesday, August 25.
The defense and prosecution for Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial go on recess during the 18th day of Duterte’s trial on Tuesday, August 25.
Ortonio: OVP under Sara Duterte requested confidential funds in 2022 because Robredo had no CF
Rappler.com
Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio says on Tuesday, August 25, that confidential funds were requested in 2022 under Vice President Sara Duterte because former Vice President Leni Robredo had no confidential funds during her term from 2016 to 2022.
OVP Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio declared as hostile witness
Rappler.com
The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday, August 25, declares Office of the Vice President (OVP) Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio as a hostile witness, allowing the prosecution to ask him leading questions.
Ortonio is the second witness to be declared hostile in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, following ex-OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta.

items.title: Leptospirosis cases jump by 845 in 2 weeks
items.summary: Leptospirosis cases in the country climbed by 25% over the past few weeks of heavy rains.
items.body_text:
Leptospirosis cases jump by 845 in 2 weeks
MANILA, Philippines — The country recorded 845 additional cases of leptospirosis over the past two weeks following incessant rains across several areas brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon or habagat and tropical cyclones.
In its recent report released on Monday, August 24, the Department of Health (DOH) said there were 4,285 leptospirosis patients as of August 22.
This is around 25% more than the earlier record of 3,440 cases from January 4 to August 8.
According to the health department, most of the cases were recorded in the National Capital Region, Region 2 or Cagayan Valley, and Region 3 or Central Luzon.
Lepto surge
The surge in leptospirosis cases came after tropical cyclones Maymay, Neneng and Luis, as well as the enhanced habagat, swamped several low-lying areas like Metro Manila, Bulacan and Pampanga since the first week of August.
Leptospirosis is caused by Leptospira bacteria, which are contracted by humans through exposure to contaminated floodwaters and mud, or by eating and drinking contaminated food and water.
The bacteria may enter through wounds, broken skin, the mouth, nose, and eyes.
Among its symptoms are high fever and chills, severe headache, muscle aches, especially in the calves and lower back, and red eyes, which may become apparent within two days to four weeks after exposure.
Full bed capacities
This week, the National Kidney and Transplant Institute earlier limited walk-in admissions as it reached full bed capacity.
San Lazaro Hospital in Manila, meanwhile, is operating at 300% to 500% of its emergency room capacity, its medical center chief, David Suplico, told GMA News on Monday.
As of Tuesday morning, NKTI Renal Services Manager Arlene Lamban said 48 patients were currently admitted to their facilities, most of whom, or 45, were mild to severe cases currently undergoing dialysis.
Untreated leptospirosis cases may lead to organ failure and typically affect the liver and kidneys.
“Karamihan ho, itong distribution ng lepto is nandito sa Metro Manila and majority of those in Metro Manila is nasa Quezon City po,” Lamban said, referring to where most of the NKTI’s patients are from.
(Most of the leptospirosis cases are in Metro Manila, and the majority of those in Metro Manila are in Quezon City.)
Rise expected
The health department said cases are expected to rise further in the coming days given that leptospirosis has an incubation period of five to 15 days.
The agency said there are 33 DOH hospitals in Metro Manila, Regions 1, 2, and 3, and the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) that have already deactivated their fast lane or express lane for immediate response to leptospirosis.
“Tinitiyak din, sa pamamagitan ng surge capacity management, na sapat ang mga kama o bed capacity at gamot para sa mga pasyenteng kailangang i-admit,” DOH said.
(We are ensuring, through surge capacity management, that the beds and medicines for the patients who need to be admitted are enough.)
The health agency also advised the public to seek consultation within 24 to 48 hours after exposure to floods, whether symptoms appear or not.

Tacloban prosecutors charge police officer aunt of minor school shooter
Content warning: Sensitive content
MANILA, Philippines — The aunt of the minor school shooter “Nash” has been charged by Tacloban prosecutors with reckless imprudence over the use of her firearm during the June shooting incident.
In a message to reporters on Tuesday, August 25, Department of Justice Spokesperson Polo Martinez said that the Office of the City Prosecutor of Tacloban City recommended the filing of charges for reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide and physical injuries against Police Staff Sergeant Arla Ray Pacencia.
According to Martinez, the information was filed with the Family Court, Regional Trial Court of Tacloban City.
“The DOJ trusts that the criminal process will proceed in accordance with the rules on due process for all parties concerned,” Martinez said.
The complaints were filed by the parents and students of San Jose National High School following the shooting incident involving 14-year-old Nash and another 15-year-old individual last June.
The incident resulted in three students being killed and 20 individuals being injured.
Nash reportedly used Pacencia's gun in the shooting.

items.title: Australia uses international student visa revenue for university reforms, minister says amid fee hike backlash
items.summary: Australia is using fees paid by international students applying for visas to help finance reforms aimed at improving the domestic higher education system, Education Minister Jason Clare has said.
items.body_text:
Speaking at the Australian Financial Review Higher Education Summit in Sydney last week, Clare acknowledged that recent visa fee increases had been unpopular among universities, but said the revenue was helping fund measures recommended by the Australian Universities Accord, according to the transcript of his speech published by the Ministers’ Media Center.
He highlighted the government’s decision to increase the visa fee for international students, saying the change was sometimes overlooked in discussions about the decline in overseas student applications.
While acknowledging that the policy had been "not very popular," he said the higher charge had "some impact on reducing the number of applications." He also recognized that the new fee, which he described as "a lot of money," and had drawn criticism from some people.
Australia in July raised visa fees for international students, with the application fee for higher education reaching A$2,500 (US$1,723), making it the highest among the "Big Four" study destinations, including the U.S., the U.K. and Canada.
The cost was raised for both student and post-study work visas, with the increase neither announced in advance nor accompanied by a public explanation.
According to the latest update from the Department of Home Affairs, the subclass 500 student visa fee for higher education and vocational education and training (VET) has risen from $2,000 to $2,500. Students from ASEAN countries are subject to a slightly lower fee of $2,050.
The visa application fee for English-language studies (ELICOS) has increased from $2,000 to $2,050, while the Temporary Graduate Visa (subclass 485) for post-study work has surged from $4,600 to $5,750.
The cost of studying in Australia has risen steadily over the past several years. The student visa fee climbed from $710 to $1,600 in 2024, before reaching $2,000 in July 2025.
Although the government does not formally earmark visa revenue for specific programs, Clare said the fees provide an important source of funding for higher education reforms.
"How do you think we're funding the Accord? Whilst we don't strictly hypothecate the money, when you make the argument to colleagues about funding with the system, you've got to find ways to do it, and whether it's extra CSPs to meet the growing demand, or whether it's paying prac, or whether it's the billion dollars that we're putting into extra bridging courses to help young people that aren't ready to start a degree they've started, all of those things are helped by that set of investment," he said.
In simpler terms, his point is that the higher international student visa fee helps contribute to broader investment in Australia's higher education system, including expanding subsidized university places for domestic students.
He pointed to several areas that require significant investment, including expanding the number of Commonwealth Supported Places (CSPs) as demand for university education grows, providing financial support for students undertaking mandatory practical placements, and investing in additional bridging courses.
The bridging courses are intended to help young people who are not yet academically prepared to begin a university degree, giving them an alternative pathway into higher education. He argued that all of these initiatives require additional government funding, and that the increased visa fee contributes to the broader pool of resources available for such investments.
The Commonwealth Prac Payment offers A$338.60 per week to eligible students while they are undertaking a mandatory placement in a Bachelor's or Master's degree in teaching, nursing, midwifery or social work, according to the Department of Education.
Australia earned around A$583 million from application fees paid by foreign students who were awarded visas last financial year, and another A$157 million from those whose applications were rejected. Since then, the fees have risen a further 25%, according to Times Higher Educ

items.title: Thai Queen begins fighter jet training, eyes historic solo flight milestone
items.summary: Thailand's Queen Suthida has commenced training on the Gripen fighter jet in Surat Thani, embarking on a rigorous aviation program that could culminate in a historic solo flight.
items.body_text:
If she successfully completes the program and flies the aircraft unassisted, she could become the first reigning queen in the world to pilot a fighter jet, according to local reports.
The privately arranged training program began Aug. 20 and will run through Sept. 4. It strictly follows the Royal Thai Air Force's (RTAF) standard training sequence for the Swedish-made tactical aircraft.
Flight instructors and aviation specialists are supervising the 48-year-old queen throughout the program, providing guidance during each stage of the training, according to the news outlet Thaiger.
Before advancing to the Gripen, Queen Suthida trained on the L-39 advanced jet trainer at the RTAF Flying Training School in Kamphaeng Saen, Nakhon Pathom.
She has also completed multiple simulator sessions, including recent exercises at an Air Force facility in Don Mueang.
The queen has made several private visits to Wing 7, which serves as Thailand's main base for its Gripen 39 C/D fleet. During these visits, she studied the aircraft's complex systems and met with operational pilots.
In July, the RTAF celebrated the 15th anniversary of the Gripen 39 C/D fighter jets and Saab 340 airborne early-warning aircraft entering service at Wing 7.
A former flight attendant for Thai Airways, the queen has steadily built her piloting credentials over the past decade, according to Reuters.
She completed the RTAF Civilian Aviation Course in December 2010 and the Army Fixed-Wing Aviation Cadet Course in January 2011, flying the Cessna T-41 for both programs.
By December 2012, she had finished an advanced aviation course at the RTAF Flying Training School, where she operated CT-4E and PC-9 aircraft.
Her international training in Germany included earning a Private Pilot License covering the Cessna 172, Mooney M-20, and Piper PA-34 Seneca.
She later obtained a Commercial Pilot License with a Boeing 737 type rating and completed the theoretical requirements for an Airline Transport Pilot License, according to The Nation.
Queen Suthida subsequently received a full Airline Transport Pilot License from Thailand’s Civil Aviation Authority. She has already put this to use, serving as a co-pilot on royal Boeing 737-400 and Boeing 737-800 aircraft.
The current Gripen program marks a significant leap in her aviation journey, transitioning her from civilian, military, and commercial passenger planes to a high-performance, operational fighter jet.

items.title: Delivery rider rams scooter into knife attacker, gets named after video game hero
items.summary: A 20-year-old food delivery rider rammed a knife-wielding man with his electric scooter on a street in northwestern China, ending an attack that had wounded two people.
items.body_text:
Yu Rongxian was carrying two orders for the delivery platform Meituan shortly after 9 p.m. on Aug. 18 when he passed a confrontation outside the Jinniu residential compound in Chengdong District, Xining, the capital of Qinghai Province.
The Beijing News reported that a man who had been drinking was holding a knife, that two people had been slashed and that several residents were trying to talk him down while others held him off with sticks.
Yu set the meals down at the roadside, rode around behind the man and drove the scooter into him, knocking him to the ground.
Bystanders moved in and held him down until police arrived and subdued him, The Beijing News reported.
Qinghai police said on Aug. 20 that compulsory measures, which range from detention to formal arrest, had been taken against the man.
Yu had just picked up the food on Beixiao Street and was passing the compound gate near the Xinsheng Lane intersection when he saw the knife, he told Cover News.
A crowd had gathered but nobody would go near a man holding a blade, he said, and he could see the man was drunk, with his attention fixed entirely on the person in front of him.
"I was out delivering that evening and saw a man running around with a knife. I thought this was the sort of thing I should step in and stop," Yu wrote in a post on his own social media account.
"So I put the food to one side, went around behind him and knocked him over. After that I went back to delivering."
Yu, who has ridden off-road motorbikes, said he did not squeeze the throttle all the way, to keep the scooter's impact from causing excessive injury.
The scooter was the fastest and most effective option he could think of, he told Cover News, and he controlled how hard he hit.
Bystander footage of the maneuver circulated widely on Chinese social media, where viewers compared the way Yu launched the scooter to a signature move by Sun Ce, a character in Tencent's mobile game "Honor of Kings". They began calling him the game's best Sun Ce player.
Yu had played the Sun Ce character before, he said, though not often, and did not mind the nickname.
The first video Yu posted to his own account drew more than 3.4 million likes and close to 100,000 followers within 24 hours, Jimu News reported.
He said he had put it up only because he was worried about being misunderstood.
Asked by commenters whether he would have been liable had someone been badly hurt, Yu told Jimu News that stepping in is a decision made on the spot, with no time to weigh it up.
Yu, who comes from Hainan Prefecture in Qinghai, turned 21 on Aug. 20, two days after the incident.
Meituan presented him that morning with an appreciation pennant naming him a "Pioneer Rider" and CNY5,000 ($740), and the delivery station where he works held a birthday celebration, Jimu News reported.
The Xining branch of scooter maker Niu Technologies posted a video offering him a new electric scooter and a quarterly battery-swap package, which Yu confirmed to Jimu News.
"Honor of Kings" issued a nationwide appeal to find him and said it wanted to send a gift.
items.normalised_title: delivery rider rams scooter into knife attacker gets named after video game hero

items.title: Cabinet to extend social security cover to farm, street, domestic workers
items.summary: The Labour Ministry will propose an expansion of social security coverage under Section 33 to include agricultural workers, street vendors and domestic workers.
items.body_text:
The Labour Ministry will propose an expansion of social security coverage under Section 33 to include agricultural workers, street vendors and domestic workers.
Labour Minister Julapun Amornvivat said before going into Tuesday's cabinet meeting he would submitted two proposals for approval.
The first concerns Thailand’s participation in the Global Coalition for Social Justice, an initiative launched by the director-general of the International Labour Organization (ILO). More than 400 academic institutions have joined the network.
Mr Julapun said Thailand was now ready, and he would seek cabinet approval to join the coalition with the aim of reducing inequality, promoting labour rights and advancing sustainable development.
The second proposal was for a royal decree to expand Social Security Office coverage under Section 33 of the Social Security Act. The move is intended to include occupational groups currently exempt from compulsory social security protection, the Pheu Thai Party leader said.
The three groups proposed for inclusion are employees engaged in agriculture, forestry and livestock farming; workers employed by street vendors and hawkers and domestic workers, including housekeepers
Once the decree was approved by the cabinet, reviewed by the Council of State and published in the Royal Gazette there would be a transition period, understood to be 180 days based on the council's recommendation.
After that, workers in the three groups would be eligible to enter the social security system, with contributions made by employers, employees and the state to provide greater financial security, said Mr Julapun.
- Domestic violence -
The Ministry of Social Development and Human Security would propose amendments to the Protection of Victims of Domestic Violence Act to ensure the law covers all forms of abuse, said Mr Julapun, whose party oversees the ministry.
The proposed amendments would expand the definition of domestic violence from three dimensions to four - physical, psychological, sexual and economic abuse. They would also introduce measures aimed at ensuring victims receive swift protection and assistance.
Officials would be given clearer authority to provide assistance, while cooperation among government agencies would be strengthened to ensure fair and standardised enforcement.
Importantly, domestic violence cases would become non-compoundable offences, meaning that the cases could not be settled through compromise. Penalties would be set at appropriate and proportionate levels, taking into account the severity of the violence and the victims' circumstances.
Harsher penalties would apply in cases involving repeated offences or violence against children (under 18). The amendments would also establish a continuously updated database of domestic violence cases, creating a mechanism aligned with international standards and providing a clearer legal framework.
Mr Julapun said the government was giving more importance to the issue, poining out that domestic violence was common in Thai society.
The proposed legislation would help ensure that Thai families could live with greater confidence and safety, he said.

items.title: Convenience store bombed in deep South as two suspects arrested
items.summary: PATTANI — Another convenience store was bombed and set ablaze in the deep South, while two suspects were arrested after a brief gunfight in this southern border province on Monday night.
items.body_text:
PATTANI — Another convenience store was bombed and set ablaze in the deep South, while two suspects were arrested after a brief gunfight in this southern border province on Monday night.
According to the Internal Security Operations Command (Isoc), the incident occurred at a 7-Eleven store in Ban Ta Bae village, tambon La Nga, in Mayo district around 8pm.
Local police rushed to the scene and exchanged gunfire with the attackers. The store was set ablaze, and an armoured security vehicle was damaged.
After the shooting ended, police found bloodstains and spent cartridges at the scene. Security officials later arrested two suspects at a checkpoint. The men, identified only as Afdol and Aris, were taken to the 42nd Ad Hoc Paramilitary Ranger Unit in Nong Chik district for interrogation.
Convenience stores have been frequent targets in a spate of violent attacks that began in the far South on Saturday night.
Col Ekwarit Chobchupol, deputy spokesman for the Region 4 Forward Command of Isoc, said on Monday that 75 violent incidents had occurred over the weekend in Narathiwat, Pattani, Songkhla and Yala provinces.
Pol Lt Col Cherd Aksornrat, director of the secretariat of the Southern Border Provinces Administrative Centre (SBPAC), said the attacks had injured 11 people and damaged 17 buildings, 40 vehicles, 32 power poles and four cellular-phone antennas.
Security officials gather at the convenience store shortly after it was set ablaze following the attack in Mayo district, Pattani, on Monday night. (Photo: Internal Security Operations Command)
Security officials arrest two male suspects after the convenience store attack in Pattani on Monday night. (Photo: 42nd Ad Hoc Paramilitary Ranger Unit)

items.title: Hormuz crisis: 68 attacks hit commercial vessels during six-month Iran war
items.summary: LONDON, Aug 25 — The Strait of Hormuz has been the main focus of the six-month war between Iran and the US a...
items.body_text:
LONDON, Aug 25 — The Strait of Hormuz has been the main focus of the six-month war between Iran and the US and Israel, with many commercial vessels targeted in the vital conduit for oil and gas shipments.
In total, 68 incidents have been confirmed by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) in the Gulf and neighbouring bodies of water, the equivalent of one every 2.6 days.
Across all incidents, at least 20 seafarers or port workers were reported killed, 35 wounded and one missing, the UN maritime agency said.
About half of the incidents have involved tankers, 20 per cent container ships and 15 per cent bulk carriers.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) classified 47 of the incidents as attacks.
Liberia-flagged vessels have been most affected, being involved in 13 incidents, followed by 10 vessels each from Panama and the Marshall Islands.
Iran-flagged vessels were reported as being involved in four incidents.
The rate of incidents has ebbed and flowed during the various phases of the war.
From the outbreak of war at the end of February until an agreement establishing a framework for peace talks was struck in mid-June, an incident was reported on average once every 2.3 days.
Incidents during this period accounted for 16 of the deaths and 19 of the injuries, and were recorded throughout the Gulf—both east and west of Hormuz, and off the coasts of Iraq, Iran, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Oman and the United Arab Emirates.
As peace talks continued, until around July 7, that rate halved to one incident every 4.6 days, on average.
No seafarers or other workers were reported killed, missing or injured during this period.
Four of the five incidents during this period were clustered off the Omani coast around the strait’s narrowest point, along a route not authorised by Iranian authorities.
Iran, which hopes to retain control of the Hormuz after the war and charge fees for passage, had warned vessels against taking the alternative route.
Since talks collapsed, the rate has climbed almost back to pre-talks levels, with an incident recorded on average every 2.8 days.
Four seafarers or workers have been killed, 16 injured and one reported missing as a result. — AFP

items.title: Canada set to announce response to Trump tariffs as trade war with US escalates
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Aug 25 — Canada said it will announce today its response to President Donald Trump&rsq...
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Aug 25 — Canada said it will announce today its response to President Donald Trump’s new tariffs, as neighbors that used to be close allies spiral into a trade war.
In response to what it called “these challenging times,” the Canadian government said night that the ministers of finance, industry, labor and other officials would hold a press conference in Ottawa to detail Canada’s answer to the new levies.
Canada and the United States failed Friday to reach a deal to avert new 50-per cent US tariffs on select Canadian goods after weeks of talks. The duties took effect Saturday, and Ottawa laid out plans for retaliation.
Trump added today that he would double tariffs on Canadian autos starting next year to 50 per cent.
The current US tariff impacting Canadian autos stands at 25 per cent for non-US content, while imported steel to the United States generally faces a 50-per cent duty. US automakers did not immediately comment on the matter.
After rejecting what he called a “bad deal,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs effective September 8.
He said these will target US steel and dairy industries, while also covering sectors like agricultural equipment, paper and electronics.
The government statement released late yesterday said ministers will “announce new measures to protect and support Canadian workers and businesses during these challenging times.”
Carney said yesterday that the goal of trade talks with Washington “has always been to get the best deal for Canadians, never a deal at any price or on any time frame.”
“We learned that, during the negotiations, the Americans wanted to destroy our major industries—including the automotive, steel, and aluminum sectors—through unfair negotiating terms. And that is one of the main reasons why we said no.”
He stressed that building domestically and diversifying trade abroad has been “plan A from the start.”
Over the weekend Carney added that, at the 11th hour, US negotiators also sought restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries.
US negotiators made unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture” too, he said, referring to eastern Canada’s French-speaking province.
At a separate event yesterday, however, US Vice President JD Vance blamed Canada’s “unreasonable last-minute demands.”
The United States is by far Canada’s biggest trading partner, with Canadian exports to its neighbor representing 70 per cent of its overall total.
Canada is the United States’ second biggest trading partner in goods this year, behind Mexico, government data showed.
We don’t need Canada
Three in four Canadians support the Carney government’s decision to walk away from trade talks, according to polling released Sunday by the Angus Reid Institute.
However, the research group noted that two in five Canadians have some fear about their jobs.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford criticized Trump’s tariff threat on autos, saying he could “kiss my ass.”
Ford warned that an electricity surcharge was on the table. In an earlier phase of the dispute, Ontario imposed a 25-per cent surcharge on electricity exports to three US states.
Trump lashed out at Ford online, warning of “far worse” consequences.
The White House had alleged “discriminatory treatment” by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in rolling out the 50-per cent tariffs.
Trump delayed their implementation by three days last week, but both sides failed to reach an agreement after talks went down to the wire.
The latest duties hit about 5.5 per cent of Canadian goods entering the US, worth some $20 billion, impacting products like hockey sticks and cement.
Trump charged that “Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” adding “we don’t need Canada, they need us.”

items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Aug 25 — US President Donald Trump vowed today to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles beginning next year, as the historically friendly neighbors spiral into a trade war.
Trump’s threat comes after the North American allies failed Friday to reach a deal to avert new 50-per cent US tariffs on select Canadian goods. The duties took effect Saturday, and Ottawa laid out plans for retaliation.
“On January First, 2027, Tariffs on all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel, will be increased to 50 per cent,” Trump wrote today on his Truth Social platform.
The current US tariff impacting Canadian autos stands at 25 percent for non-US content, while imported steel to the United States generally faces a 50-percent duty. US automakers did not immediately comment on the matter.
After rejecting what he called a “bad deal,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs effective September 8.
These will target US steel and dairy industries, while also covering sectors like agricultural equipment, paper and electronics.
Carney said Monday that the goal of trade talks with Washington “has always been to get the best deal for Canadians, never a deal at any price or on any time frame.”
“We learned that, during the negotiations, the Americans wanted to destroy our major industries—including the automotive, steel, and aluminum sectors—through unfair negotiating terms. And that is one of the main reasons why we said no.”
He stressed that building domestically and diversifying trade abroad has been “plan A from the start.”
Over the weekend Carney added that, at the 11th hour, US negotiators also sought restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries.
US negotiators made unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture” too, he said, referring to eastern Canada’s French-speaking province.
At a separate event Monday, however, US Vice President JD Vance blamed Canada’s “unreasonable last-minute demands.”
The United States is by far Canada’s biggest trading partner, with Canadian exports to its neighbor representing 70 percent of its overall total.
Canada is the United States’ second biggest trading partner in goods this year, behind Mexico, government data showed.
We don’t need Canada
Three in four Canadians support the Carney government’s decision to walk away from trade talks, according to polling released Sunday by the Angus Reid Institute.
However, the research group noted that two in five Canadians have some fear about their jobs.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford criticized Trump’s tariff threat on autos, saying he could “kiss my ass.”
Ford warned that an electricity surcharge was on the table. In an earlier phase of the dispute, Ontario imposed a 25-percent surcharge on electricity exports to three US states.
Trump lashed out at Ford online, warning of “far worse” consequences.
The White House had alleged “discriminatory treatment” by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in rolling out the 50-per cent tariffs.
Trump delayed their implementation by three days last week, but both sides failed to reach an agreement after talks went down to the wire.
The latest duties hit about 5.5 percent of Canadian goods entering the US, worth some US$20 billion, impacting products like hockey sticks and cement.
Trump charged today that “Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” adding “we don’t need Canada, they need us.”
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told The New York Times on Saturday that the Trump administration offered to eliminate a 10-percent tariff on softwood lumber, and reduce the 25-percent autos tariff.
Washington was also ready to cut steel tariffs from 50 percent to 25 percent for most Canadian steel, said Greer.
Besides the tariffs fight, Washington and Ottawa have to agree on revisions to the US-Mexico-Canada free trade agreement (USMCA) which Trump has declined to renew in its current form.

items.title: Homes submerged, tens of thousands relocated in China's south as flooding intensifies
items.body_text:
Homes submerged, tens of thousands relocated in China's south as flooding intensifies
HONG KONG: Widespread floods triggered by heavy rain from Typhoon Narra intensified on Tuesday (Aug 25) across southern China, with homes and shops submerged and thousands of people relocated, while another storm system made its way towards Japan and Taiwan.
Authorities in Chongzuo, in China's Guangxi region, famous for its giant waterfalls and karst limestone mountains, evacuated more than 15,000 people after water levels surpassed a record high set in 2008.
Rising floodwaters have prompted China to relocate a total of 54,000 people in Guangxi, state television said.
Narra has lingered over the Beibu Gulf, also known as the Gulf of Tonkin, in the northwestern part of the South China Sea for several days, dumping heavy rain on Guangxi and the nearby provinces of Hainan and Guangdong.
Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of Vietnam and southern China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, state media said.
In Chongzuo, river water overflowed into the city, with water levels reaching the rooftops of some buildings and power lines.
A notice from Chongzuo authorities on Monday ordered all businesses and tourist operations to cease and urged evacuated residents not to return to high-risk areas.
TYPHOON SAUDEL APPROACHES JAPAN, TAIWAN
Meanwhile, medium-strength Typhoon Saudel moved towards southern Japan and northern Taiwan where it is expected to bring sporadic heavy rain, as Taiwan reported one dead and four missing from a separate weather system over its south and east.
Japan's weather agency warned of destructive gusts as Typhoon Saudel approached the southwestern islands of Okinawa prefecture, also causing extremely strong winds and high seas.
Saudel is expected to pass to the north of Taiwan and dump water on its north starting late Thursday and into Friday, though its intensity is forecast to gradually weaken and its storm-force wind radius to shrink, the island's Central Weather Administration said.
However, there is uncertainty about the timing and extent of the typhoon's rainfall impact, it added.
In southern and eastern Taiwan, the government reported one person dead and four missing from a tropical depression that brought flooding in the cities of Tainan and Kaohsiung, home to more than 4 million people.
During the three days from Sunday to Tuesday, almost a metre of rain fell in Kaohsiung, which the government said exceeded rainfall during 2009's devastating Typhoon Morakot that killed about 700 people and caused damage of up to US$3 billion.
Saudel is forecast to hit the coast in the southeastern Chinese province of Fujian from late Thursday to early Friday.

items.title: Government quality, capability set successful nations apart in a contested world: Chan Chun Sing
items.summary: Speaking at the inaugural Singapore-Vietnam Strategic Dialogue, Mr Chan said both countries feel the shifts in the rules-based international order acutely.
items.body_text:
Government quality, capability set successful nations apart in a contested world: Chan Chun Sing
Speaking at the inaugural Singapore-Vietnam Strategic Dialogue, Mr Chan said both countries feel the shifts in the rules-based international order acutely.
SINGAPORE: The quality and capability of government will increasingly distinguish successful nations from the rest amid a weakening rules-based international order and rising geopolitical competition, Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing said on Tuesday (Aug 25).
Speaking at the inaugural Singapore-Vietnam Strategic Dialogue held at Conrad Singapore Marina Bay, Mr Chan said that strong institutions help countries anticipate change and adapt when external shocks occur.
“Policy consistency, regulatory effectiveness, and the quality of the public service matter for economic competitiveness. Businesses consider these factors when deciding where to invest and where to build for the long term,” said Mr Chan, who is also Singapore’s defence minister.
“Governments also need the confidence and trust of their people. Public trust enables governments to build consensus, mobilise society, and undertake difficult reforms in which benefits may only be apparent many years later.”
Mr Chan co-chaired Tuesday’s dialogue with Permanent Member of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) Central Committee Secretariat Tran Cam Tu.
Other key figures who attended the dialogue included Vietnam's Minister of Foreign Affairs Le Hoai Trung and Singapore's Foreign Affairs Minister Vivian Balakrishnan. Singapore's Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo was also present.
At the dialogue, the foreign affairs ministers of both sides signed an agreement on a study visit programme and an executive education programme for senior CPV officials from 2027 to 2029. Both countries also issued a joint statement on the Vietnam-Singapore technology connectivity strategy.
The Singapore-Vietnam Strategic Dialogue was formed under the ambit of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between both countries, which was established last year.
“We intend for this to be a forward-looking platform where we can exchange perspectives candidly on emerging challenges, and identify areas where we can work together bilaterally and regionally,” said Mr Chan in his opening speech.
Mr Tu said in his opening remarks that the dialogue reflects the increasingly deep level of political trust and the importance of the relationship between both countries.
Speaking in Vietnamese, he added that the platform will further strengthen political trust, enhance cooperation across all fields, and help develop the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between both sides in a profound and substantive manner, becoming a model of mutually beneficial cooperation in the region.
Mr Tu also said Vietnam is interested and eager to learn from Singapore's experience in building a modern administration and effective national governance, including identifying and nurturing talent, and building a team of leadership successors with the vision and capacity to meet the country's needs in the new era.
MORE VOLATILE, CONTESTED ENVIRONMENT
In his opening speech, Mr Chan said that Singapore and Vietnam are both operating in a more complex environment today.
“For decades, Singapore and Vietnam have benefited greatly from an open and rules-based international order, deep economic integration, and a stable regional environment. These conditions provided important tailwinds for our economies to grow and for our people to prosper,” he said.
“Today, many of these conditions are weakening.”
Both counties feel the shifts acutely as small, open and trade-dependent economies, said Mr Chan.
With intensifying geopolitical competition, the boundaries between economic policy, technology policy and national security are blurring.
Supply chains and investment decisions are also being shaped by strategic and security considerations, beyond commercial ones

items.title: Prabowo orders permits to be revoked for firms linked to Indonesia forest fires
items.summary: Fires across Sumatra and Kalimantan have burned about 85,000 hectares, local media reported.
items.body_text:
Prabowo orders permits to be revoked for firms linked to Indonesia forest fires
Fires across Sumatra and Kalimantan have burned about 85,000 hectares, local media reported.
JAKARTA: Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto on Monday (Aug 24) ordered the revocation of business permits of firms suspected of ordering forest and land burning.
The order came as haze from fires in Indonesia spread to neighbouring countries including Malaysia and Singapore.
“Any corporation, whoever they are, if there is even the slightest indication they ordered the burning, we will revoke their licences,” he said while leading a coordination meeting on forest and land fire management in Riau.
“We will revoke all of the corporation’s permits. I am not playing around,” he said, as quoted by state news agency Antara.
Prabowo also called on authorities to prevent individuals from deliberately setting fires for any reason.
He added that public education should be strengthened, particularly in villages, so that communities understand that land burning is prohibited, Antara reported.
Those who need to clear land should seek government assistance instead of burning it, he said. Local governments, the Indonesian military and the National Police could help organise land clearing through farmer groups, he added.
“If they need to clear land, they should report it to the sub-district head or regent, and the government will help them,” Prabowo said.
Prabowo also visited Palembang on Monday, where he ordered authorities to act immediately when forest and land fires emerge.
“Don’t wait until it becomes a hotspot. Please go directly to those hotspots … Water sources can be drilled in those areas,” Prabowo said, as reported by Jakarta Globe.
He called for the construction of boreholes in fire-prone areas to ensure water is available for rapid firefighting and urged enforcement of the law.
The Indonesian government is also doing satellite-based hotspot monitoring, deploying helicopters for water bombing and conducting weather modification operations to encourage rainfall in fire-affected areas.
Fires across Sumatra and Kalimantan have burned about 85,000 hectares, Jakarta Globe reported on Monday.
The latest satellite data from the Environment Ministry showed South Sumatra with the highest number of hotspots nationwide, at 1,429.
This was followed by West Kalimantan with 1,226 and Central Kalimantan with 811. East Kalimantan logged 576 hotspots, ahead of Riau with 503, while West Papua and Jambi recorded 468 and 458 hotspots, respectively.
In Singapore, the National Environment Agency (NEA) warned on Monday that “occasional periods of haze” could affect the country after it detected an increase in hotspot activity over the weekend.
In Malaysia, 30 monitoring stations nationwide recorded “unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels.
Sarawak remained the epicentre of the country’s air pollution, Malay Mail reported, with the Serian district recording the highest reading nationwide of 180, approaching the “very unhealthy” threshold of 201.
Across the peninsula, half a dozen monitoring stations across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya recorded unhealthy air quality.
Shah Alam recorded the highest reading in Peninsular Malaysia and the third-highest nationwide at 162. Putrajaya recorded 156, followed by Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Kuala Selangor at 155, Banting at 152, and Petaling Jaya at 151, Malay Mail reported on Tuesday.

items.title: Tornado in southwestern France damages over 300 homes, injures dozens
items.summary: PARIS, Aug 25 - A tornado swept through the Aude region of southwestern France late on Monday, damaging more than 300 homes and injuring dozens, authorities said.
items.body_text:
Tornado in southwestern France damages over 300 homes, injures dozens
PARIS, Aug 25 - A tornado swept through the Aude region of southwestern France late on Monday, damaging more than 300 homes and injuring dozens, authorities said.
Thirty-nine people were injured, including two in critical condition in the village of Pomas, local authorities said. By Tuesday morning some 21,000 households were without power in southern France, including 1,600 in the Aude, local grid operator ENEDIS said.
"A tornado of rare intensity struck the Aude region late yesterday afternoon, severely damaging the village of Pomas," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on X.
Social media footage verified by Reuters showed the tornado swirling above the nearby village of Verzeille in Aude, late on Monday. Many of the homes caught up in its path had their windows smashed.
The tornado struck as this summer's intense heatwave gave way this week to thunderstorms in many areas of southern France. REUTERS

items.title: Hungary foreign ministry files report on $964 million pandemic-era ventilator deals
items.summary: BUDAPEST, Aug 25 - Hungary's Foreign Ministry has filed a report with prosecutors on suspected fraud and other crimes involving the 2020 purchase of ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic under the previous government, Foreign Minister Anita Orban said on Tuesday.
items.body_text:
Hungary foreign ministry files report on $964 million pandemic-era ventilator deals
BUDAPEST, Aug 25 - Hungary's Foreign Ministry has filed a report with prosecutors on suspected fraud and other crimes involving the 2020 purchase of ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic under the previous government, Foreign Minister Anita Orban said on Tuesday.
• The report on the purchase of nearly 17,000 ventilators worth a combined 300 billion forints ($963.82 million) says the ministry bought thousands of surplus ventilators that could not be used realistically at inflated prices, Orban told reporters.
• Press officials for former right-wing ruling party Fidesz did not immediately respond to emailed questions seeking comment.
• Orban says an internal audit at the ministry could recover only what she described as a partial picture of pandemic-era purchases as some files and documentation had to be recovered electronically.
• The ministry has filed a report with prosecutors based on 88 gigabytes of information, or 130,000 recovered files.
• Orban says the number of ventilators purchased by the foreign ministry far exceeded the number of doctors, intensive care nurses and hospital beds that could accommodate and operate them.
• Most ventilators purchased in 2020 still are stored in warehouses, Orban said.
• Orban said import- and tax-authority figures show that the purchased ventilators were from Hungarian vendors at prices significantly above factory prices. REUTERS

items.title: President says Syria ‘shakes off dark stain’ with removal from US terror list
items.summary: The decision on Aug 24 rescinded a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions.
items.body_text:
President says Syria ‘shakes off dark stain’ with removal from US terror list
DAMASCUS – Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa hailed early on Aug 25 the United States’ removal of his country from the state sponsors of terror list, a major sanctions relief step.
“Today, Syria shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past to embark on a path of development, reconstruction and rebuilding,” Sharaa said in a speech.
Washington’s decision on Aug 24 rescinded a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions, marking another step in warming ties between the countries following the 2024 ouster of long-time Syrian ruler Bashar al-Assad.
The Treasury Department announced corresponding sanctions relief.
Sharaa expressed his “many thanks to the President of the United States of America, Donald Trump, and to all the friendly and supportive nations that stood by us”.
The US Department of State also revoked its designation of the al-Nusra Front – latterly known as Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) – as a global terrorist organisation. Sharaa led that group, which spearheaded the blitz offensive that toppled Assad.
It was formerly the branch of Al-Qaeda in Syria before breaking ties with it in 2016.
Syria’s new authorities are trying to attract investment to support the country and rebuild its infrastructure, heavily damaged by more than a decade of civil war.
The United States had initially announced in July its intent to delist Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, a move seen as a vote of confidence in Sharaa.
The Aug 24 move gave Syria’s “a path to prosperity”, according to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The action “eliminates the final major barriers for private sector investment in Syria and promotes Syria’s economic recovery and reintegration into the global economy”, he said in a statement.
Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani described Washington’s delisting as a “historic milestone” and said it reflected “the new Syrian state’s commitment to international peace and security”.
Finance Minister Mohammed Barnieh described the move as a “success for Syrian diplomacy”, according to the official news agency SANA.
It “opens a major and long-awaited door to strengthening Syria’s integration into the global economic and financial system, attracting investment and modern technologies, and supporting development opportunities”. AFP
