items.title: Neighbor accuses Sudan of cross-border airstrikes
items.summary: Aircraft and drones from Sudan carried out strikes more than 100km inside Chad’s territory, the army said Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Neighbor accuses Sudan of cross-border airstrikes
Chad has accused parties in Sudan’s civil war of carrying out airstrikes deep inside its territory, warning that the conflict risks spilling across the border, the Chadian Armed Forces said on Saturday.
According to the statement, aircraft and drones believed to belong to the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) or forces supporting them pursued and bombed a convoy of vehicles on Thursday. The strikes began on Sudanese soil before continuing more than 100 kilometers inside Chad, reaching the Mourdi department in the eastern Ennedi-Est province.
The military said that the extent of the incursion was established following aerial and ground checks conducted on Friday. No Chadian casualties have been reported, but the army condemned what it described as a new violation of the country’s territorial integrity.
Chad warned Sudan’s warring parties against attempting to extend the conflict onto its territory, saying that its defense and security forces remain on the highest level of alert and are prepared to respond to any threat to the country’s security. There has been no response from Sudanese authorities to the Chadian military’s allegations.
Sudan plunged into a civil war three years ago after a struggle for power broke out between the SAF and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Sudan descended into chaos in April 2023 when fighting erupted between the national army (Sudanese Armed Forces, SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). This occurred after months of tension between their commanders, army generals Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo ‘Hemedti’, respectively, over a planned transition to civilian rule. What began in the capital, Khartoum, as a power struggle has devastated the country, killing tens of thousands and displacing millions.
Regional and international peace efforts, including African Union mediation and Saudi–US talks in Jeddah, have repeatedly stalled. Sudanese officials have named Colombians and Ukrainians among mercenaries backing the RSF against the army. Officials have also accused Ukraine and the United Arab Emirates of involvement and recently claimed the European Union has an “incomplete understanding of the complex situation” in the country.
Khartoum has also accused authorities in neighboring Kenya of backing the RSF and has broken ties with the East African grouping IGAD amid mistrust of regional mediation. In July, TASIS, a political coalition aligned with the paramilitary, announced the formation of a rival government months after its members signed a charter in Nairobi. It named Gen. Dagalo as chairman of a 15-member presidential council, a move rejected by the UN and AU.
The incident follows several previous cases of violence spilling across the Sudan-Chad border. In July, a drone arriving from Sudanese territory struck the eastern Chadian border town of Tine, injuring two children and damaging vehicles and shops, according to local authorities.
In March, a drone strike from Sudan killed at least 17 people in the same town, including mourners attending a funeral. President Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno condemned the attack and ordered the military to retaliate against any future strikes originating from Sudan, whether carried out by the Sudanese army or the RSF.
A month earlier, Chad shut its eastern border with Sudan after five soldiers and three civilians were killed in clashes allegedly involving the SAF and RSF. At least 12 others were wounded in the incident, which also occurred in Tine, officials said.

items.title: Two arrested over murder of boxing star
items.summary: Two men have been arrested over the murder of former world boxing champion Zolani Tete in South Africa Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Two arrested over murder of boxing star
Police in South Africa’s Eastern Cape have arrested two men in connection with the murder of former world boxing champion Zolani Tete, who was fatally shot in Mdantsane on Friday.
The two persons of interest, aged 30 and 22, were arrested in Ku Gompo on Saturday following a swift, intelligence-driven operation involving multiple law enforcement units, police said.
Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said the suspects were in custody and were being questioned in connection with Tete’s murder and the attempted murder of a 27-year-old woman who was wounded in the attack.
“Due to the sensitive nature of the ongoing investigation, the SAPS is unable to disclose further details regarding the motive or the circumstances surrounding the arrests at this time,” Gantana said. “Investigators are following up on several leads, and more arrests are imminent.”
Tete, 38, was killed outside his home in Mdantsane on Friday evening as he sat in his car waiting for the gate to open. Police said the shooting happened at about 6:30pm. Two armed men wearing balaclavas reportedly got out of another vehicle and opened fire on Tete and the woman travelling with him.
“In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard. He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene,” Gantana said.
The woman sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a nearby hospital, where she remains. On Saturday, police confirmed Tete’s identity after notifying his next of kin.
Tete was one of South Africa’s most successful boxers, winning world titles in two weight divisions. He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a world title fight.
On November 18, 2017, he stopped Siboniso Gonya in 11 seconds at the SSE Arena in Belfast. Tete won the International Boxing Federation junior bantamweight title in Kobe, Japan, in July 2014 after stopping Teiru Kinoshita. He later held the World Boxing Organisation bantamweight title from 2017 until losing it to John Riel Casimero in Birmingham in November 2019. He had 34 professional fights, winning 29, including 22 by knockout. Tete grew up in Mdantsane, started boxing at the age of 8 and was trained by former world champion Vuyani Bungu.
He had not fought since July 2022, when he tested positive for the banned steroid stanozolol following his victory over Jason Cunningham at Wembley. The result was overturned to a no contest and Tete was handed a four-year ban, which ended on July 29 this year. Tete maintained that he had never knowingly taken the substance. In an interview with boxing magazine The Ring in January, he said he planned to return to the ring this year.

items.title: Pope issues Ebola plea
items.summary: Pope Leo has called for international action against the DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak, which has killed 2,557 people Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Pope issues Ebola plea
Pope Leo has called for international action to confront the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo), where transmission remains active across six provinces and thousands of people have died.
On Sunday, the pontiff said on X that he often remembers the African state in his prayers, especially in light of the spread of the Ebola epidemic.
“I encourage on the part of the international community a response that also involves local communities in efforts of prevention, so that many human lives may be saved,” Pope Leo said.
The appeal came as the latest figures from DR Congo’s Health Ministry showed 5,375 confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths, putting the case fatality rate at 47.6%.
The outbreak has reached 56 health zones across six provinces – Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele, and Tshopo. Ituri remains the most widely affected, with cases recorded in 28 of its 36 health zones. The authorities said transmission remains active but that there has been no further geographical expansion in the latest reporting period.
The World Health Organization (WHO) has described the outbreak as the largest ever recorded in DR Congo and said it has been expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak in the country. The agency’s director-general, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has warned that the disease is spreading faster than efforts to contain it.
The WHO and the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) have also previously called for greater international support to contain the outbreak.
DR Congo declared the outbreak in May. It is the country’s 17th recorded Ebola outbreak and is caused by the Bundibugyo virus. There is currently no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment for this specific strain.
On Friday, Kinshasa received 16,520 Ervebo vaccines, with 50,120 expected by August 24. Funded by Gavi and made by MSD in Germany, the vaccine was developed and licensed against a different Ebola virus species. However, it will support the government’s response and protect people at risk, according to the country’s health minister, Roger Kamba.

items.title: Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche: Beyond sorrow
items.summary: On the sidelines of the 2026 Rimini Meeting for Friendship Among Peoples, Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche, who have come to be known as “sisters in sorrow", speak to Vatican News about the tragedy that unites them. Roseline is the sister of Fr Jacques Hamel, the French priest who was killed while celebrating Mass in a terrorist attack in 2016. Nassera is the mother of one of the two teenagers who perpetrated the attack and was subsequently shot dead by police. Read all
items.body_text:
Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche: Beyond sorrow
Below is a transcript of the interview with Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche. It has been translated from French and edited for fluency and readability.
You can watch the full interview, in French, here.
Q: Roseline, what prompted you to reach out to Nassera?
Roseline Hamel: It was a question I asked myself every day. I wondered who could possibly be suffering more than I was. It was a long journey, lasting almost a year, during which I kept asking God that question. All my conversations with Him were like a prayer, but I received no answer.
Then one morning, I turned to God and said: âMy God, tell me who could be suffering more than I am.â To me, it did not seem possible.
The following morning, I began thinking about this woman I did not know - this mother, who was a mother just like me. I reversed our roles and tried to put myself in her place. I imagined her pain, her torment and the months of struggle she had endured with her young son, who had allowed himself to be drawn down a path his mother would never have wanted for him.
I imagined the contemptuous looks she must have faced and the cloak of guilt she had to bear as a parent. That was when I realised I had found the person who might be suffering more than I was.
I said to myself: âThatâs it. I have found this path back to life, the sense of meaning I have been searching for since the funeral and since returning home.â Then I told myself: âNow, Roseline, you must do something. You must find the way to the house where this mother lives.â
Q: Nassera, what did you feel when Roseline knocked on your door for the first time?
Nassera Kermiche: It was also a long journey, because we first spoke on the telephone. At the beginning, our conversations were very brief. Then, little by little, a genuine dialogue developed between us.
One day, Roseline asked me: âIf I come to Saint-Étienne, would you be willing to meet me?â I replied: âOf course. I have been waiting for you for a long time.â
I had been hoping for that meeting for quite some time. I had already tried to meet the religious sisters who had been inside the church when the attack took place, but it had not been possible.
I was therefore very happy to be able to meet Roseline. When she arrived at my door and I opened it, I was so emotional and so happy that no words would come out of my mouth except: âForgive me, forgive me.â That was all I could say, because I needed her forgiveness.
Q: Roseline, you speak of forgiveness as a journey. Was there a particular moment when you understood or felt that forgiveness was possible?
Roseline Hamel: I had never really thought about the difficulty of forgiveness. Perhaps I had never had reason to. Forgiving is, of course, always difficult, and it depends on the magnitude of the offence.
Until then, I had faced the ordinary difficulties of life. As my daughter would say to me: âLet it go, Mum.â And I would let things go quite easily because I had other things to live for. When you are raising children, you cannot dwell indefinitely on something that has hurt or offended you.
But in the situation that brings us together today, offering forgiveness appeared, in the eyes of society, to be an immense and almost impossible undertaking. Why? Because we do not share the same religion and everything appeared destined to divide us.
That tragic day, that day of deadly violence which we both experienced, should have sown hatred towards this family. But hatred leads to revenge, violence and the destruction of our own humanity.
I do not know whether it was the sacrifice of those lives that meant we received the grace of God not to feel hatred. No member of my family felt it.
Three days before the funeral, the Archbishop of Rouen came to my sisterâs home to help us organise it. There were twelve of us in a small flat intended for four people. Before we began, he asked us a question: âDo you feel hatred?â

items.body_text:
Ukraine marks grim war anniversary
By Nathan Morley
Ukraine marks 35 years of independence on August 24, as its war with Russia enters a fourth year.
European leaders are gathering in Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital, where the so-called âCoalition of the Willingâ will meet President Volodymyr Zelensky to discuss additional support as Moscow ramps up its bombing campaign.
Meanwhile, both countries continue to trade strikes.
Ukrainian officials say five people were killed in the Kharkiv region. Russia says three teenagers died when a childrenâs centre was hit by what it called âdrone debris.â
Earlier, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham vowed to maintain pressure on Moscow during his first official visit to Ukraine, despite Russian threats.
In the Middle East, the U.S. treasury secretary warned Iran of what he called âthe single greatest financial offensive ever,â saying the U.S.âIsrael war with Iran was âentering its endgame.â
Scott Bessent said Washington would cut all economic ties with Tehran in an âeconomic DâDay,â and that any country doing business with Iran would also face isolation.
Iran dismissed the remarks and said it would halt all regional oil exports âif the war continues,â according to the Reuters news agency.

items.title: Tanzania: Religious women evangelize through Television and social media
items.summary: As technology and communication continue to evolve, the Congregation of Sisters of Our Lady of Usambara (COLU) in Tanzania is increasingly using media as a tool for evangelization. Through television and social networks, the sisters seek to share the Gospel, engage young people, and respond to questions about the Catholic faith. Read all
items.body_text:
Tanzania: Religious women evangelize through Television and social media
By Sr. Ernestina Patrick Lasway SAC and Sr. Christine Masivo CPS
Founded in 1954 by Monsignor Eugen Arthurs of the Rosminian Fathers, the COLU Sisters are a diocesan congregation rooted in evangelization and education. In 1958, Msgr. Arthurs became the first Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Tanga. The sisters were initially formed by the Missionary Sisters of the Precious Blood (CPS), and their first General Superior was Sr. Willibalda Giesbers.
The congregation began its mission in Rangwi and later moved to Korogwe, Kwamndolwa, in Tanga, while Rangwi remained the original mother house. Over time, their apostolate has focused on education at all levelsâfrom kindergarten to collegeâas well as catechesis and youth formation.
A new path for evangelization
In response to the changing times, the sisters discerned the need to reach people through modern means of communication. This led to the establishment of Usambara Mountain TV (UMTV) in July 2024 in Lushoto, in the Tanga region.
The initiative aims to offer content that supports evangelization, education, and dialogue on matters of faith. âThrough television and the internet, we are able to reach people far beyond our immediate communities,â said Sr. Paulina T. Mshana, director of UMTV. âThis strengthens our mission to share the Gospel and encourage people, especially young people, to know and love God more.â
Many young people follow UMTV through social media platforms and YouTube, where the channel offers programs focused on youth, faith, and social issues, including initiatives inspired by the spirituality of Don Bosco.
Content and outreach
UMTV broadcasts a variety of programs, including catechetical teaching, reflections on faith, and discussions on youth and society. Through these initiatives, the sisters seek to make their charism and mission more visible in a media landscape that increasingly shapes daily life.
Since its launch, the platform has reached a wide audience both locally and internationally, particularly among young people online. This growing engagement reflects a desire for content that combines education, reflection, and accessible communication.
Sr. Paulina notes that working in media allows the congregation to reach communities where they are not physically present. âI am happy to be involved in this work, even if many people still think that operating a camera is a manâs job. Sisters, too, can take on this role and communicate the Gospel to the wider community,â she said.
Collaboration and impact
The initiative has also benefited from collaboration with other members of the Church. Br. Lucas Masasi OFM Cap, one of the contributors to UMTV, highlighted the importance of the project in promoting faith-based content and supporting learning at different levels. He has followed its development from a simple YouTube channel to a more structured television platform.
Through its programming, UMTV contributes to education within local communities, offering content in areas such as culture, music, spirituality, and basic life skills, accessible even from home.
Challenges and limitations
Like many new initiatives, UMTV faces practical challenges. Limited equipment and financial resources make daily production demanding, while access to reliable internet and the cost of digital devices remain obstacles for many viewers.
Power outages also affect the regularity of broadcasts, as the lack of adequate backup systems can interrupt operations. In addition, not all members of the congregation initially recognized the importance of media for evangelization, requiring ongoing formation and awareness within the community.
Looking ahead
Despite these challenges, the sisters remain committed to using media as a space for evangelization and formation. Their goal is to reach a broader audience and to help young people engage more consciously with digital tools in their search for meaning and faith.
Inspired
